questions.subject: Torts
questions.question:
A driver was traveling along a highway during an unusually heavy rainstorm when the roadway began to flood. To protect his car from water damage, the driver pulled his car up a steep, unmarked driveway abutting the highway that led to a homeowner's residence. The driver left his car parked in the driveway and walked home, intending to return when the floodwater had subsided. Shortly after the driver started to walk home, the homeowner carefully rolled the car back down her driveway and parked it on the highway shoulder. The floodwater continued to rise and caused damage to the driver's car.
If the driver sues the homeowner to recover for damage to his car, is the driver likely to prevail?

choices.A: No, because the driver intentionally drove his car onto the homeowner's property.
choices.B: No, because the homeowner was privileged to remove the car from her property.
choices.C: Yes, because the driver was privileged to park his car on the homeowner's property.
choices.D: Yes, because the homeowner did not post any "no trespassing" signs.

questions.explanation:
Doctrine of necessity
Doctrine of necessity
Private necessityAn intrusion that is, or reasonably appears to be, necessary to protect oneself, third parties, or property
Public necessityAn intrusion that is, or reasonably appears to be, necessary to avert an imminent public disaster

A trespass is privileged when it arises out of necessity—ie, when an intrusion is, or reasonably appears to be, necessary to:

  • protect oneself, third parties, or property from serious harm (private necessity) or
  • avert an imminent public disaster (public necessity).

A landowner cannot use force to stop a trespass arising from necessity and is liable for damages caused by force used against the trespassing person or property.

Here, the driver was privileged to park his car on the homeowner's driveway because it was, or reasonably appeared to be, necessary to protect his car from the flood (private necessity). Therefore, the homeowner had no right to forcibly remove the driver's car from her driveway and onto the highway shoulder (Choice B). Since the homeowner's actions caused the car to flood, the driver will likely recover for damage to his car.

(Choice A) The driver trespassed when he intentionally drove his car onto the homeowner's property. And though a landowner can generally use reasonable force to stop a trespass (ie, defense of property), the landowner cannot do so when the trespass is privileged—as seen here. Therefore, the driver's trespass does not preclude him from recovering for the damage to his car.

(Choice D) Trespass requires intent to enter the land—not intent to enter the land without the owner's consent. Therefore, the absence of "no trespassing" signs has no bearing on the driver's intent or his privilege to seek refuge on the landowner's driveway.

📌 Educational Objective

A landowner must permit a trespass caused by necessity—an intrusion that is, or reasonably appears to be, necessary to (1) protect oneself, third parties, or property from serious harm or (2) avert an imminent public disaster—for as long as the necessity exists.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Second) of Torts § 197 (Am. Law Inst. 1965) (private necessity).
  • Restatement (Second) of Torts § 77 cmts. d–e (Am. Law Inst. 1965) (defense of property).
questions.zh-question:
一名司机在异常大的暴雨中沿高速公路行驶时，路面开始被水淹没。为保护其车辆免受水淹损害，该司机将车开上了一条与高速公路相邻、通往一户住宅的陡峭且无标记的车道。司机将车停在车道上后步行回家，并打算在洪水退去后返回。在该司机开始步行回家后不久，户主小心地将该车推下其车道，并停放在高速公路的路肩上。洪水继续上涨，对司机的车辆造成了损害。

如果司机起诉户主，要求赔偿其车辆的损失，司机是否可能胜诉？

zh-choices.A: 不会，因为司机是故意将车开到户主的地产上的。
zh-choices.B: 不会，因为户主有特权将车辆从其地产上移走。
zh-choices.C: 会，因为司机有特权将车停在户主的地产上。
zh-choices.D: 会，因为户主没有设置任何“禁止非法侵入”的标志。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Intentional Torts: Necessity

核心法律原则：紧急避险

本题考察的是侵权法中的紧急避险 (Necessity) 抗辩事由。当一个人为了防止对自己、他人或财产造成更大的损害而侵入他人土地时，该侵入行为享有“特权” (Privilege)。

📚 知识点拆解

紧急避险分为两类，本题涉及的是私下避险：

类型 定义 法律后果
公共避险
Public Necessity		 为避免公共灾难（如火灾蔓延） 完全免责（无需赔偿损失）。
私下避险
Private Necessity		 为保护个人利益（如本案中的车） 不完全特权 (Incomplete Privilege)：
1. 土地主不得驱逐。
2. 避险者需赔偿对土地造成的实际损害。

🔍 案情逻辑推演

第一步：司机的行为

司机为了保护自己的车免受洪水（自然灾害）的损害，将车开上了户主的车道。这构成了私下避险 (Private Necessity)。

👉 结论： 司机的侵入是合法的（享有特权），他不是普通的非法侵入者。

第二步：户主的反应

虽然户主通常有权将非法侵入者赶走（财产防卫 Defense of Property），但面对享有避险特权的人，这一权利被暂时中止。

👉 关键点： 只要紧急情况存在，户主就没有权利驱逐司机或移除其车辆。

第三步：责任归属

户主将车推回洪水区，导致车辆受损。由于户主无权这么做，她必须对车辆的损失负责。

❌ 为什么其他选项是错的？

选项 A (错误)： "Intentional trespass"
虽然司机是故意进入，但“紧急避险”正是针对故意侵权行为的抗辩。特权的存在使得这一故意行为不再具有可诉性（除非造成了土地损害，但本案是司机索赔）。
选项 B (错误)： "Privileged to remove"
这是最大的干扰项。通常土地主可以移除他人财物，但在对方享有“紧急避险”特权时，土地主丧失了移除权。
选项 D (错误)： "No trespassing signs"
是否设立警示牌与非法侵入（Trespass）的构成要件无关。Trespass 只需要故意进入他人土地，不需要知道那是私人领地。且这不影响避险特权的成立。
✅ 正确答案：C

会胜诉，因为司机有特权将车停在户主的地产上。

由于洪水威胁，司机享有私下避险的特权。这剥夺了户主将车移回危险地带的权利。户主强行移车的行为构成了侵权（可能是 Trespass to Chattels 或 Conversion），需赔偿损失。

💡 MBE 考试技巧：
记住口诀：
"Necessity trumps Defense of Property."
（紧急避险 压倒 财产防卫）
避险者可以留下来，但要为打破的窗户（实际损害）买单；
房主不能赶人，如果赶人导致避险者受伤，房主要赔。

reason.en: Moving the car back to the shoulder restored the flood risk the driver sought to avoid.

A.text: intentionally drove his car onto the homeowner's property

reason.zh: 忽略了基于必要性的正当侵入不妨碍获得赔偿。

B.text: privileged to remove the car from her property

reason.zh: 错误认为土地所有人可强行移走基于必要性的正当侵入者财产。

C.text: privileged to park his car on the homeowner's property

reason.zh: 指出使司机进入成为正当行为的正确原则。

D.text: did not post any "no trespassing" signs

reason.en: Trespass depends on intent to enter land, not on posted signs.
reason.zh: 侵入取决于进入土地的意图，而非是否张贴警示标志。

highlights.text: To protect his car from water damage, the driver pulled his car up a steep, unmarked driveway abutting the highway

reason.en: This sentence triggers private necessity and shows why the driver's trespass was privileged.
reason.zh: 该句触发私人必要原则，说明司机的侵入为何属于正当行为。

reason.en: The homeowner had no privilege to remove the car while the necessity continued.
reason.zh: 在必要状态存续期间，房主无权强行移走车辆。

highlights.text: floodwater continued to rise and caused damage to the driver's car

reason.en: Links the homeowner's removal to the harm supporting the driver's recovery.
reason.zh: 将房主的移车行为与司机可获赔偿的损害联系起来。

highlights.text: If the driver sues the homeowner to recover for damage to his car

reason.en: Frames whether necessity limits the landowner's defense and permits damages.
reason.zh: 界定必要性是否限制土地所有人的防卫权并允许损害赔偿。

questions.subject: Torts
questions.question:
A law student rented a furnished apartment. His landlord began to solicit his advice about her legal affairs, but he refused to provide it. The landlord then demanded that the student vacate the apartment immediately. The landlord also began engaging in a pattern of harassment, calling the student at home every evening and entering his apartment without his consent during times when he was at school. During these unauthorized visits, the landlord removed the handles from the bathroom and kitchen faucets, making the faucets unusable, but she did not touch any personal property belonging to the student. The lease has a year to run, and the student is still living in the apartment. The student has sued the landlord for trespass.
Is he likely to prevail?

choices.A: No, because he has no standing to sue for trespass.
choices.B: No, because the landlord caused no damage to his property.
choices.C: Yes, for compensatory damages only.
choices.D: Yes, for injunctive relief, compensatory damages, and punitive damages.

questions.explanation:
Explanation
Types of remedies
Nominal damagesTrivial sum of money (eg, $1) awarded to vindicate plaintiff's rights when no actual loss or damage occurs
Compensatory damagesMoney awarded to compensate plaintiff for actual loss or damage (ie, actual damages)
Punitive damagesMoney awarded to punish defendant for outrageous or evil conduct & to deter similar conduct in the future (ie, exemplary damages)
Injunctive reliefCourt order commanding or prohibiting a specified action

For trespass, the plaintiff must prove that the defendant intentionally entered land in the plaintiff's possession without the plaintiff's permission. If the plaintiff does so, he/she may receive nominal damages or compensatory damages, as well as punitive damages and/or injunctive relief.

Here, the student can establish a claim for trespass because the landlord intentionally (and repeatedly) entered the student's apartment without his consent. Therefore, the student will likely recover:

  • compensatory damages - for the removal of the faucet handles
  • punitive damages - to punish the landlord for his malicious and evil pattern of harassment
  • injunctive relief - to stop the landlord's repeated and ongoing trespasses

However, nominal damages are not recoverable because the student suffered actual loss and damage (ie, he can recover compensatory damages).

(Choice A) A plaintiff has standing to sue for trespass if he/she has a possessory interest—the right to occupy or control property—in the land that the defendant intentionally entered. Here, even though the student does not own the apartment, he has a possessory interest in it (a lease). Therefore, he has standing to sue for trespass.

(Choice B) The landlord did damage the student's leased property by removing the faucet handles, rendering them inoperable. But even if no damage had occurred, the student could still prevail because trespass does not require proof of actual loss or damage. However, the student could not recover compensatory damages.

(Choice C) The student's recovery is not limited to compensatory damages because there is evidence to support punitive damages (landlord's malicious pattern of harassment) and injunctive relief (landlord's repeated and ongoing trespasses).

📌 Educational Objective

Trespass is an intentional, unauthorized entry onto land in the plaintiff's possession (ie, land the plaintiff occupies or controls). The plaintiff can recover nominal damages (eg, $1) for a harmless trespass or compensatory damages for a harmful trespass. Punitive damages and/or injunctive relief may also be available.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Second) of Torts § 158 (Am. Law Inst. 1965) (trespass).
  • Restatement (Second) of Torts § 903 (Am. Law Inst. 1979) (compensatory damages).
  • Restatement (Second) of Torts § 907 (Am. Law Inst. 1979) (nominal damages).
  • Restatement (Second) of Torts § 908 (Am. Law Inst. 1979) (punitive damages).
  • Restatement (Second) of Torts § 945 (Am. Law Inst. 1979) (injunctive relief for recovery of land).
questions.zh-question:
一名法学院学生租了一套带家具的公寓。他的房东开始就其法律事务向他征求建议，但他拒绝提供。随后，房东要求该学生立即搬离公寓。房东还开始了一系列骚扰行为，每天晚上给该学生打电话，并在他上学期间未经其同意进入其公寓。在这些未经授权的进入中，房东拆除了浴室和厨房水龙头的把手，致使水龙头无法使用，但她没有触碰任何属于该学生的个人财物。租赁合同还有一年到期，该学生仍居住在该公寓内。该学生以非法侵入（trespass）为由起诉了房东。

他有可能胜诉吗？

zh-choices.A: 不会，因为他没有起诉非法侵入（trespass）的诉讼资格。
zh-choices.B: 不会，因为房东没有对他的财产造成损害。
zh-choices.C: 会，但仅限于补偿性损害赔偿。
zh-choices.D: 会，可获得禁令救济、补偿性损害赔偿和惩罚性损害赔偿。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

侵权法：非法侵入与救济措施

Intentional Torts: Trespass & Remedies

✅ 正确答案：D

学生很可能胜诉，并获得禁令救济 (Injunctive Relief)、补偿性损害赔偿 (Compensatory Damages) 和 惩罚性损害赔偿 (Punitive Damages)。

核心法律分析
1. 诉讼资格 (Standing)
Possessory Interest vs. Ownership

非法侵入 (Trespass to Land) 侵犯的是占有权，而非所有权。虽然学生只是租客 (Tenant)，但他拥有合法的占有权益 (Possessory Interest)。因此，他完全有资格起诉房东非法侵入。

2. 救济措施 (Remedies)
What can the plaintiff recover?

本题的考点在于区分不同类型的赔偿金适用场景。

  • ✔
    补偿性损害赔偿 (Compensatory Damages)
    适用：造成了实际损失。
    虽然房东没有损坏学生的私人物品，但拆除水龙头把手导致公寓（学生拥有租赁权的财产）贬值且无法使用。这是对学生占有利益的实际损害。
  • ✔
    惩罚性损害赔偿 (Punitive Damages)
    适用：被告行为恶意、恶劣。
    房东的行为构成骚扰 (Harassment) 和恶意逼迁，属于恶意 (Malicious) 或 肆意 (Wanton) 的行为，符合惩罚性赔偿的标准。
  • ✔
    禁令救济 (Injunctive Relief)
    适用：金钱赔偿不足以解决问题。
    房东的行为是持续性 (Continuing) 和重复的。仅靠赔偿无法阻止她未来继续闯入，因此法院会下达禁令禁止其非法进入。
为什么其他选项错误？

❌ 选项 A (无诉讼资格)： 错误。如前所述，租客拥有占有权，足以起诉 Trespass。

❌ 选项 B (无财产损害)： 错误。Trespass 是行为犯，不要求实际损害即可成立（可获象征性赔偿）。且本案中拆除把手确实造成了租赁物使用价值的损害。

❌ 选项 C (仅限补偿性赔偿)： 错误。因为房东的行为具有恶意（支持惩罚性赔偿）且具有持续性（支持禁令），仅赔偿损失是不够的。

💡 MBE 考试技巧 (Exam Tip)

在处理 Trespass 题目时，记住以下公式：

  • 意图 (Intent) = 意图进入土地（不需要意图侵权）。
  • 损害 (Damages) = 不需要实际损害即可胜诉（Nominal Damages）。
  • 如果有实际损害 ➡ Compensatory Damages。
  • 如果有恶意/恶劣情节 ➡ Punitive Damages。

reason.en: Establishes the student's possessory interest needed for a trespass claim.
reason.zh: 确立学生提起非法侵入诉讼所需的占有利益。

reason.en: Satisfies the intentional, unpermitted entry element of trespass.
reason.zh: 满足非法侵入所要求的故意且未经许可进入。

reason.en: Supports punitive damages for outrageous conduct.
reason.zh: 支持因恶劣行为判处惩罚性赔偿。

reason.en: Shows actual harm supporting compensatory damages.
reason.zh: 表明存在实际损害，支持补偿性赔偿。

reason.en: Confirms continued lawful possession while trespasses occur.
reason.zh: 确认非法侵入发生时租户仍合法占有。

reason.en: Frames the cause of action whose elements and remedies are tested.
reason.zh: 界定本题所测试的请求权构成要件与救济。

A.text: no standing to sue for trespass

reason.en: Misstates that a tenant lacks standing despite a possessory leasehold interest.
reason.zh: 错误认为租户因无所有权而无诉权。

B.text: caused no damage to his property

reason.en: Wrongly treats actual property damage as an element of trespass liability.
reason.zh: 错误将实际财产损害视为非法侵入的成立要件。

reason.en: Omits punitive damages and injunctive relief available for ongoing malicious trespass.
reason.zh: 忽略对持续恶意侵入可判给的惩罚性赔偿与禁令救济。

reason.en: Appropriate to stop the landlord's repeated unauthorized entries.
reason.zh: 用于制止房东反复未经授权进入。

reason.en: Covers harm from rendering the faucets unusable.
reason.zh: 弥补水龙头无法使用所致损害。

reason.en: Supported by the landlord's malicious harassment pattern.
reason.zh: 因房东恶意骚扰行为模式而可支持。

highlights.text: entering his apartment without his consent

reason.en: Triggers trespass liability for intentional entry without permission.
reason.zh: 触发故意未经许可进入的非法侵入责任。

highlights.text: removed the handles from the bathroom and kitchen faucets, making the faucets unusable

reason.en: Establishes compensatory damages beyond a merely nominal trespass.
reason.zh: 表明损害超出仅可判名义赔偿的范围，支持补偿性赔偿。

highlights.text: pattern of harassment

reason.en: Justifies punitive damages for outrageous trespass-related conduct.
reason.zh: 为恶劣的非法侵入相关行为提供惩罚性赔偿依据。

highlights.text: The lease has a year to run, and the student is still living in the apartment

reason.en: Shows the student has standing as a tenant in possession despite not owning the land.
reason.zh: 表明学生虽非土地所有人，但作为占有中的租户具有诉权。

questions.subject: Torts
questions.question:
A rancher and his neighbor were involved in a boundary dispute. In order to resolve their differences, each drove his truck to an open pasture area on his land where the two properties were separated by a fence. The rancher was accompanied by four friends, and the neighbor was alone. The neighbor got out of his truck and walked toward the fence. The rancher got out but simply stood by his truck. When the neighbor came over the fence, the rancher shot him, inflicting serious injury.
In a battery action brought by the neighbor against the rancher, the rancher testified that he actually thought his neighbor was armed. However, the rancher could point to nothing that would have reasonably justified this belief.
Is the neighbor likely to prevail?

choices.A: No, because the rancher suspected that the neighbor was armed.
choices.B: No, because the rancher was standing on his own property and had no obligation to retreat.
choices.C: Yes, because deadly force is never appropriate in a property dispute.
choices.D: Yes, because it was unreasonable for the rancher to consider the use of a gun necessary for self-defense.

questions.explanation:
Self-defense
Maximum force permitted
Excessive force
Reasonable force
Force used
Anticipated harm
DeadlyHarmfulOffensiveNone
NoneOffensiveHarmfulDeadly

The privilege to use force in self-defense serves as a defense to battery and other intentional torts. But a defendant can only use deadly force in self-defense when the defendant reasonably believes that:

• an individual is intentionally inflicting or about to intentionally inflict unprivileged force upon the defendant

• the defendant is put in peril of death, serious bodily harm, or rape by the use or threat of physical force and

• the defendant can safely prevent the peril only by the immediate use of deadly force.

Here, the rancher committed a battery when he shot the neighbor (deadly force). The rancher alleges that he did so in self-defense because he actually thought that the neighbor was armed. But since the rancher could point to nothing that would have reasonably justified this belief, it was unreasonable for him to consider the use of a gun necessary for self-defense. Therefore, the neighbor will likely prevail on his battery claim.

(Choice A) Since the rancher's suspicion that the neighbor was armed was not supported by any evidence (no reasonable belief), his use of deadly force was not privileged.

(Choice B) Under the castle doctrine, a defendant has no obligation to retreat if he/she is attacked in his/her dwelling—i.e., a building, structure, or vehicle in which the defendant resides. But a dwelling does not encompass open land on the defendant's property, so the rancher had no privilege to use deadly force.

(Choice C) Although deadly force cannot be used to protect property, it can be used when a property dispute escalates into a situation in which a participant is in danger of death or serious bodily injury. But since the rancher could not reasonably believe that there was such a danger here, he was not privileged to use deadly force.

📌 Educational Objective

A defendant is privileged to use deadly force in self-defense if the defendant reasonably believes that (1) a person is intentionally inflicting or about to intentionally inflict unprivileged force, (2) such force puts the defendant in peril of death, serious bodily harm, or rape, and (3) he/she can prevent the peril only by immediately using deadly force.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Third) of Torts: Intentional Torts to Persons § 23 (Am. L. Inst., Tentative Draft No. 6, 2021) (explaining when deadly force may be used in self-defense).
questions.zh-question:
一位牧场主和他的邻居卷入了一场边界纠纷。为了解决分歧，他们各自开着卡车来到自己土地上的一片开阔牧场，两块地产由一道栅栏隔开。牧场主有四位朋友陪同，而邻居独自一人。邻居下了卡车，朝栅栏走去。牧场主也下了车，但只是站在他的卡车旁。当邻居翻过栅栏时，牧场主向他开枪，造成其重伤。

在邻居对牧场主提起的伤害罪(battery)诉讼中，牧场主作证说，他当时确实认为他的邻居持有武器。

然而，牧场主无法指出任何可以合理解释这一想法的依据。

邻居是否可能胜诉？

zh-choices.A: 不会，因为牧场主怀疑邻居持有武器。
zh-choices.B: 不会，因为牧场主站在自己的土地上，没有退让的义务。
zh-choices.C: 会，因为在财产纠纷中，使用致命武力从来都是不恰当的。
zh-choices.D: 会，因为牧场主认为有必要使用枪支进行自卫是不合理的。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

侵权法 (Intentional Torts) - 自卫 (Self-Defense)
⚖️ 黑体字法 (Black Letter Law)

被告若要主张自卫 (Self-Defense) 作为对殴打 (Battery) 指控的抗辩，必须证明：

  1. 他合理地相信 (Reasonably Believed) 自己面临迫在眉睫的伤害；且
  2. 他使用的武力与威胁的程度是成比例的 (Proportionate)。

Deadly Force 只有在被告合理相信自己面临死亡或严重身体伤害 (Serious Bodily Injury) 时才能使用。

🔍 案情关键点分析

本题的核心矛盾在于“主观想法”与“客观合理性”的冲突。

  • 事实：牧场主 (Rancher) 使用了枪支（致命武力）。
  • 主观 (Subjective)：牧场主“确实认为”邻居有枪。
  • 客观 (Objective)：题目明确指出，牧场主“无法指出任何理由”来证明这一想法是合理的。

在法律上，仅有主观的恐惧是不够的，必须通过客观理性人标准 (Objective Reasonable Person Standard) 的检验。

✅ 正确答案解析
选项 D (正确)

“会胜诉，因为牧场主认为有必要使用枪支进行自卫是不合理的。”

这是本题的题眼。自卫特权 (Privilege of Self-Defense) 的核心要素是Reasonable Belief（合理确信）。

既然题目设定了牧场主的信念缺乏依据（unreasonable），那么他的自卫抗辩就自动失效。无论他内心多么恐惧，法律不保护基于无端臆测而对他人的严重伤害。

❌ 干扰项排除
选项 A

错误原因：仅有“怀疑 (Suspected)”是不够的。法律要求这种怀疑必须有客观事实支持。如果允许仅凭主观怀疑就开枪，社会秩序将无法维持。

选项 B

错误原因：这里涉及退让义务 (Duty to Retreat)。虽然现代很多司法管辖区实行“坚守阵地法 (Stand Your Ground)”，但在普通法 (Common Law) 规则下，如果在户外（非家中）面临致命冲突且能安全撤退，通常有退让义务。

更重要的是，即使没有退让义务，牧场主开枪的行为首先因为缺乏合理威胁而非法，所以“是否需要退让”不是本案胜败的关键。

选项 C

错误原因：措辞太绝对（"Never"）。虽然一般不能用致命武力保护财产，但如果财产纠纷升级，对方先使用了致命武力，此时为了保命（而非保财产），是可以使用致命武力的。

💡 MBE 提分技巧

在处理 Intentional Torts 的抗辩题时，请务必区分Subjective (主观) 和 Objective (客观) 要素。

如果题目明确告诉你被告“诚实地相信 (honestly believed)”某事，但又补充说“没有理由 (no reason)”，那么在法律上这个信念就是无效的。MBE 非常喜欢考这种“真心实意但完全不合理”的场景。

questions.subject: Torts
questions.question:
A host pointed an unloaded revolver at her guest, threatening to shoot him. The guest knew that the revolver was not loaded, and that the ammunition for the revolver was stored in a locked basement closet, two stories below where the two were then standing.
In an action brought by the guest against the host for assault, will the guest be likely to prevail?

choices.A: No, because the host did not intend to shoot her guest.
choices.B: No, because the host did not cause anticipation of imminent contact.
choices.C: Yes, because the ammunition was accessible to the host.
choices.D: Yes, because the host threatened her guest with a revolver.

questions.explanation:
Elements of civil assault
Mental state
Δ intended to cause π to anticipate imminent, & harmful or offensive, contact with T's person
↓
Causation
Δ's affirmative conduct caused π to anticipate such contact
Δ = defendant, π = plaintiff.

Assault occurs when:

  • the defendant intends to cause the plaintiff to anticipate an imminent, and harmful or offensive, contact with the plaintiff's person and
  • the defendant's affirmative conduct causes the plaintiff to anticipate such contact.

The threatened bodily harm or offensive contact must be imminent—i.e., without significant delay. Therefore, threats made by a defendant who cannot inflict imminent harm due to the physical distance between the defendant and the plaintiff are usually insufficient to support an assault claim.

Here, though the host did intend to shoot the guest, she did intend to scare the guest by threatening to shoot him (Choice A). Therefore, the host acted the requisite intent. However, the host did not cause the guest to anticipate imminent contact because the guest knew that the host's revolver was unloaded and that her ammunition was in a locked basement closet below. As a result, the guest is not likely to prevail in an action against the host for assault.

(Choice C) Assault requires anticipation of imminent contact. Imminent means without significant delay. Here, though the ammunition was accessible to the host, it could not be retrieved without significant delay because it was locked in a closet two stories below.

(Choice D) A threat alone does not constitute an assault. The threat must cause anticipation of imminent contact (not seen here).

📌 Educational Objective

Assault requires that the threatened bodily harm or offensive contact be imminent—i.e., without significant delay.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Third) of Torts: Intentional Torts to Persons § 105 (Am. L. Inst., Tentative Draft No. 1, 2015) (setting for the requirements for assault).
questions.zh-question:
一名主人用一把未上膛的左轮手枪指着她的客人，并威胁要开枪射他。客人知道这把左轮手枪没有上膛，而且手枪的弹药存放在他们所站位置下方两层一个锁着的地下室壁橱里。

在客人对主人提起的侵袭（assault）诉讼中，客人是否可能胜诉？

zh-choices.A: 不会，因为主人无意射击她的客人。
zh-choices.B: 不会，因为主人没有让她的客人产生对即刻接触的恐惧。
zh-choices.C: 会，因为主人可以拿到弹药。
zh-choices.D: 会，因为主人用左轮手枪威胁了她的客人。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Intentional Torts: Assault
正确答案：B
⚖️ 法律规则 (Rule of Law)

侵袭 (Assault) 的成立需要被告的行为导致原告对即刻 (Imminent) 的伤害性或冒犯性接触产生合理的恐惧/预期 (Reasonable Apprehension)。

🔍 深度解析

本题的核心考点在于原告的知情状态 (Knowledge) 如何影响“恐惧” (Apprehension) 的认定。

❌
没有即刻的恐惧：
虽然主人用枪指着客人，但客人明确知道枪里没有子弹。既然知道枪是空的，客人就不可能相信自己面临“即刻”的枪击风险。
❌
缺乏即刻性 (Imminence)：
虽然有弹药，但弹药在两层楼下的锁闭壁橱里。获取弹药需要时间，无法构成“即刻”的威胁。法律要求接触必须是 without significant delay（无明显延迟）。

因此，由于原告知道威胁无法立即兑现，法律上的 Apprehension 并不存在，Assault 不成立。

💡 为什么其他选项是错的？
选项 A 错误 (Intent)：
Assault 的意图可以是造成接触，也可以仅仅是造成恐惧 (Intent to frighten)。主人虽然不想开枪，但她想吓唬客人，这满足了 Assault 的意图要件。她不承担责任是因为结果未发生（客人没被吓到），而不是因为没有意图。
选项 C 错误 (Accessibility)：
仅仅“可以拿到” (Accessible) 是不够的。Assault 要求威胁是即刻的 (Imminent)。两层楼下的距离打破了即刻性。
选项 D 错误 (Threat alone)：
单纯的威胁 (Threat) 如果没有伴随造成即刻接触的能力（或表面能力），且没有导致受害者的恐惧，是不构成 Assault 的。
🎓 MBE 提分技巧：空枪原则
  • 如果原告不知道枪是空的 → 构成 Assault（因为恐惧是合理的）。
  • 如果原告知道枪是空的 → 不构成 Assault（因为不存在对即刻伤害的预期）。

做题时务必关注原告的主观认知 (Plaintiff's knowledge)。

questions.subject: Torts
questions.question:
A college student was asleep in his bed in a college dormitory when his roommate, in a drunken fury, entered their room intending to attack the student with an ice pick while he slept. The phone rang and awakened the student. The roommate retreated quickly and threw the ice pick under his own bed in the same room. The next day, the student heard from friends about the roommate's murderous plans and later found the ice pick under the roommate's bed. Even though the college expelled his roommate, the student remained extremely upset and afraid to sleep.
In a suit against the roommate for assault, will the student prevail?

choices.A: No, because the roommate did not touch the student.
choices.B: No, because the student was not awake when the roommate entered the room and was unaware until later that the roommate had intended to attack him.
choices.C: Yes, because it was reasonable for the student to feel afraid of sleeping in his room afterward.
choices.D: Yes, because the roommate intended to inflict serious harm.

questions.explanation:
Explanation
Anticipation
No anticipation ≠ Assault
Anticipation = Assault

Assault occurs when:

  • the defendant intends to cause the plaintiff to anticipate an imminent, and harmful or offensive, contact with the plaintiff's person and
  • the defendant's affirmative conduct causes the plaintiff to anticipate such contact.

Anticipation exists only when the plaintiff is aware or has knowledge of the defendant's act.

Here, the roommate intended to attack the student with an ice pick (harmful contact). However, the attempted attack did not cause the student to anticipate imminent contact because he was asleep and unaware of the attempted attack until the following day. Therefore, there was no assault.

(Choice A) Assault requires that the plaintiff be placed in anticipation of imminent contact. Actual bodily contact is not required, so the fact that the roommate never touched the student is irrelevant.

(Choice C) The student's fear of sleeping in his room would have been relevant to determining damages had the roommate committed an assault. But this is irrelevant because no assault occurred.

(Choice D) Although the roommate intended to inflict harmful contact on the student, the student was not placed in anticipation of such contact. Therefore, the roommate is not liable for assault.

📌 Educational Objective

Assault requires that the plaintiff anticipate an imminent, and harmful or offensive, contact with the plaintiff's person. Anticipation exists only when the plaintiff is aware or has knowledge of the defendant's act.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Third) of Torts: Intentional Torts to Persons § 105 cmt. c (Am. L. Inst., Tentative Draft No. 1, 2015) (discussing the anticipation requirement for assault).
questions.zh-question:
一名大学生正在大学宿舍的床上睡觉，这时他的室友在醉酒的狂怒中进入房间，意图趁该学生睡觉时用冰锥袭击他。电话铃声响起，惊醒了该学生。室友迅速退后，并将冰锥扔到同一房间内自己的床下。第二天，该学生从朋友处听闻了室友的谋杀计划，随后在室友的床下发现了冰锥。尽管大学开除了他的室友，该学生仍然极度不安，不敢入睡。

在对室友提起的 assault 诉讼中，该学生会胜诉吗？

zh-choices.A: 不会，因为室友没有触碰到该学生。
zh-choices.B: 不会，因为室友进入房间时该学生并未醒着，并且直到后来才意识到室友曾意图袭击他。
zh-choices.C: 会，因为该学生事后害怕在自己房间睡觉是合理的。
zh-choices.D: 会，因为室友意图造成严重伤害。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Intentional Torts: Assault

本题是 Assault（恐吓/企图伤害） 这一侵权行为的经典教科书案例。要正确回答此题，必须精准掌握 Assault 的核心构成要件，特别是关于“感知”的要求。

⚖️ 法律规则 (The Rule)

Assault 的成立需要被告实施了故意行为 (Intentional Act)，导致原告产生对即将来临的有害或冒犯性接触的合理感知 (Reasonable Apprehension)。

Restatement (Second) of Torts § 21

核心考点分析

本题的关键在于 Apprehension（感知/恐惧）。

在侵权法中，如果受害人没有在当时意识到威胁，Assault 就不成立。Assault 保护的是人们“免受即时暴力威胁的心理安宁”。

案情应用：

  • 被告进入房间时，原告正在睡觉 (Asleep)。
  • 被告挥舞冰锥时，原告毫无察觉 (Unaware)。
  • 原告醒来后才得知此事。

因为原告在威胁发生时处于睡眠状态，他不可能对“即将来临的接触”产生感知。事后的恐惧（fear afterwards）不构成 Assault。

✅ 正确答案解析 (选项 B)

No, because the student was not awake...

理由： 既然学生当时并未醒来，他就没有意识到（Apprehend）即将发生的攻击。没有当时的意识，就没有侵权法上的 Assault。

❌ 干扰项陷阱排除

选项 A (No touching): 错误。
这是 Battery (殴打) 的要求，不是 Assault 的要求。Assault 不需要身体接触，只需要产生接触的“威胁感”。
选项 C (Reasonable fear later): 错误。
Assault 要求的是对 Imminent (迫在眉睫) 接触的感知。事后得知真相感到害怕虽然合乎情理，但那是对“过去风险”的后怕，而非对“即时伤害”的感知。
选项 D (Intent to harm): 错误。
仅有 Intent (意图) 是不够的。侵权法要求意图加上特定的后果（此处为原告的心理感知）。虽然室友意图恶劣，但由于原告在睡觉，该意图未能完成 Assault 的构成要件。
🎓 考试技巧 (Exam Tip)

在处理 Assault 题目时，请务必检查受害人是否清醒且知情。如果受害人是从背后被袭击（且未回头看到）或在睡眠中被瞄准，通常不构成 Assault，因为缺失了 Apprehension 这一环。

questions.subject: Torts
questions.question:
A woman asked to use her friend's kitchen to cook a holiday dinner while the friend was away. The friend agreed. While cooking, the woman accidentally left a metal spoon in a bowl of food that she was heating up in the microwave. As a result, the microwave short-circuited and caught fire. When the friend returned, she had to replace the microwave. The friend then sued the woman for conversion.
Is the friend likely to recover under a theory of conversion?

choices.A: No, because the friend gave the woman permission to use the kitchen.
choices.B: No, because the woman did not intentionally deprive the friend of the microwave.
choices.C: No, because the woman did not remove the microwave from the friend's kitchen.
choices.D: Yes, because the friend had to replace the microwave.

questions.explanation:
Trespass to chattels v. Conversion
Trespass to chattels
  • Minor intentional interference with plaintiff's right to control chattel
  • Liable for actual damages—eg, cost of repairs, loss of use
Conversion
  • Substantial intentional interference with plaintiff's right to control chattel
  • Liable for fair market value of chattel at time of conversion

Conversion occurs when a defendant intentionally commits an act that either:

  • deprives the plaintiff of possession of the plaintiff's chattel (i.e., tangible personal property) or
  • interferes with the plaintiff's chattel in a manner so serious as to deprive the plaintiff of the use of the chattel.

However, if the defendant had permission to use the chattel, then accidental damage to the chattel is not conversion.

Here, the friend gave the woman permission to use the kitchen—including the microwave—while she was away. Although the woman totally destroyed and deprived the friend of the microwave, she did so unintentionally by accidentally leaving a metal spoon in a bowl of food that she was heating up. For this reason, the friend is unlikely to recover under a theory of conversion (Choices A and D).

*Although the friend is unlikely to recover under a theory of conversion, she may be able to recover damages against the woman based on a negligence theory.

(Choice C) The tort of conversion does not require the carrying away of property. To be liable for conversion, the defendant's interference with the plaintiff's chattel need only be serious enough to deprive the plaintiff of its use.

📌 Educational Objective

Conversion occurs when a defendant intentionally commits an act that deprives the plaintiff of possession of her chattel or interferes with the chattel in a manner so serious as to deprive the plaintiff of its use. Accidental damage to the chattel is not conversion if the defendant had permission to use it.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Second) of Torts § 222A (Am. Law Inst. 1965) (conversion).
  • Restatement (Second) of Torts § 227 (Am. Law Inst. 1965) (conversion by using chattel).

questions.subject: Torts
questions.question:
A man tied his dog to a bike rack in front of a store and left the dog there while he went inside to shop. The dog was usually friendly and placid. A five-year-old child started to tease the dog by pulling gently on its ears and tail. When the man emerged from the store and saw what the child was doing to the dog, he became extremely upset.
Does the man have a viable claim against the child for trespass to chattels?

choices.A: No, because the child did not injure the dog.
choices.B: No, because the child was too young to form the requisite intent.
choices.C: Yes, because the child touched the dog without the man's consent.
choices.D: Yes, because the child's acts caused the man extreme distress.

questions.explanation:
Trespass to chattels
Plaintiff has possession or immediate
right to possession of chattel
↓
Defendant intentionally interferes with
possession through either:
Dispossession
↓
Harm inferred
Use or intermeddling
↓
Causes harm
  • actual harm to chattel
  • substantial loss of use of chattel or
  • bodily harm to plaintiff

Trespass to chattels (ie, trespass de bonis asportatis) occurs when the defendant intentionally interferes with the plaintiff's possession of a chattel through dispossession, use, or intermeddling (ie, causing physical contact). Harm is inferred when the interference is through dispossession. But when the interference is through use or intermeddling, the plaintiff must prove one of three harms:

  • actual harm to the chattel (ie, impairment of its physical condition, quality, or value)
  • substantial loss of use of the chattel or
  • bodily harm to the plaintiff.

Here, the child intentionally interfered with the man's dog (chattel) by pulling on its ears and tail (intermeddling). But there is no evidence that:

  • the man's dog was injured (no actual harm)
  • the man lost substantial use of his dog or
  • the man suffered bodily harm.

Therefore, the man does not have a viable claim against the child for trespass to chattels.

(Choice B) A child of any age can commit an intentional tort like trespass to chattels as long as the child is capable of forming the requisite intent. Here, the child formed the intent to interfere with the man's possession of his dog through intermeddling when the child teased the dog by pulling at its ears and tail. But since the child's intentional act did not cause the requisite harm, the child is not liable for trespass to chattels.

(Choice C) Although the child touched the dog without the man's consent (intermeddling), the child is not liable for trespass to chattels because the child did not cause the requisite harm—actual harm to the dog, substantial loss of use of the dog, or bodily harm to the man.

(Choice D) Trespass to chattels requires proof that the defendant's use of or intermeddling with the plaintiff's chattel caused the plaintiff bodily harm—not merely emotional harm. Therefore, the man's extreme emotional distress does not support this claim.

📌 Educational Objective

Trespass to chattels by intentionally dispossessing the plaintiff of a chattel requires no proof of harm. However, intentional use of or intermeddling with the plaintiff's chattel requires proof of (1) actual harm to the chattel, (2) substantial loss of use of the chattel, or (3) bodily harm to the plaintiff.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Second) of Torts § 217 (Am. Law Inst. 1965) (trespass to chattels).
questions.zh-question:
一名男子将他的狗拴在一家商店门前的自行车架上，然后进店购物。这只狗通常很友善温顺。一名五岁的儿童开始逗弄这只狗，轻轻地拉它的耳朵和尾巴。当该男子从商店出来，看到孩子对狗的行为时，他变得非常沮丧。

该男子对该儿童的动产侵权(trespass to chattels)主张是否可以成立？

zh-choices.A: 不成立，因为该儿童没有伤害到这只狗。
zh-choices.B: 不成立，因为该儿童年龄太小，无法形成必要的主观意图。
zh-choices.C: 成立，因为该儿童未经该男子同意触摸了这只狗。
zh-choices.D: 成立，因为该儿童的行为给该男子造成了极度的精神痛苦。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Intentional Torts / Trespass to Chattels
⚖️ 核心法则：动产侵权 (Trespass to Chattels)

动产侵权是指故意干扰原告对动产的占有权。这种干扰可以通过两种方式发生：

  1. 剥夺占有 (Dispossession)： 拿走动产。此时损害被推定，无需证明实际损失。
  2. 干预/妨碍 (Intermeddling)： 仅仅是接触或使用动产，但未剥夺占有。

关键区别：如果是第2种（干预），原告必须证明实际损害 (Actual Damages)。

🔍 本案深度解析

本题考察的是对 Intermeddling (干预) 构成要件的精准掌握。

🐶
行为定性：
儿童拉扯狗的耳朵和尾巴，属于对动产的“干预”或“妨碍”，而非“剥夺占有”。
🚫
损害缺失：
对于“干预”行为，法律要求必须造成以下三种损害之一才构成侵权：
  • 动产受损（价值降低或物理损坏）
  • 原告丧失了对动产的使用权
  • 原告遭受了人身伤害 (Bodily Harm)
✅
结论：
题目明确指出狗“未受伤”，且男子仅感到“沮丧 (upset)”而非受到身体伤害。由于缺乏必要的实际损害，侵权主张不成立。

因此，正确答案是 选项 A。
⚠️ 常见 MBE 陷阱

陷阱 1：儿童的意图 (Choice B)
错误观点： 孩子太小，没有意图。
法律事实： 只要儿童能够形成进行该动作的主观意愿（volitional act），即视为有意图。5岁儿童完全可以形成拉扯狗耳朵的意图。年龄本身不是抗辩理由。

陷阱 2：精神痛苦 (Choice D)
错误观点： 精神痛苦足以构成损害。
法律事实： 在 Trespass to Chattels 中，如果涉及对人的影响，必须是人身伤害 (Bodily Harm)。单纯的情绪困扰（Emotional Distress）不足以支持此项诉因。

陷阱 3：未经同意的接触 (Choice C)
错误观点： 只要碰了就是侵权。
法律事实： 这与不动产侵权 (Trespass to Land) 不同。对于动产，轻微的、无害的接触（Technical Trespass）如果不造成实际损失，法律不予救济。

Reference: Restatement (Second) of Torts § 217, § 218

questions.subject: Torts
questions.question:
A bus passenger was seated next to a woman he did not know. The woman stood to exit the bus, leaving a package on the seat. The passenger lightly tapped the woman on the back to get her attention and to inform her that she had forgotten her package. Because the woman had recently had back surgery, the tap was painful and caused her to twist and seriously injure her back.
If the woman sues the passenger to recover for the back injury, will she likely prevail?

choices.A: No, because she is presumed to have consented to the ordinary contacts of daily life.
choices.B: No, because she was not put in apprehension by the touching.
choices.C: Yes, because she did not consent to the harmful contact.
choices.D: Yes, because the passenger's intentional touching seriously injured her.

questions.explanation:
Types of consent
(defense to intentional torts)
Actual • Plaintiff willingly—expressly or inferred from facts—submits to defendant's conduct
Apparent • Defendant reasonably believes that plaintiff actually consented to defendant's conduct, even if plaintiff did not
Presumed or implied • Under prevailing social norms, defendant is justified in engaging in conduct in absence of plaintiff's actual/apparent consent and
• defendant has no reason to believe that plaintiff would not have actually consented
Emergency doctrine • Purpose of defendant's conduct is to prevent/reduce risk to plaintiff's life or health
• Defendant reasonably believes that:
   • conduct is necessary to prevent/reduce risk that substantially outweighs plaintiff's interest in avoiding conduct and
   • immediate action is necessary to prevent/reduce that risk before obtaining actual consent
• Defendant has no reason to believe that plaintiff would not have actually consented

A defendant is liable for battery if (1) he/she intends to cause contact with the plaintiff's person, (2) the defendant's affirmative conduct causes such contact, and (3) the contact causes bodily harm or is offensive to the plaintiff. However, the defendant is not liable for battery if the plaintiff consented to such contact (see table above). Presumed (i.e., implied) consent exists when:

• under prevailing social norms, the defendant is justified in engaging in the conduct in the absence of the plaintiff's actual or apparent consent and

• the defendant has no reason to believe that the plaintiff would not have actually consented had the defendant requested the plaintiff's consent.

Here, the passenger tapped the woman on her back, causing her to seriously injure her back. But under prevailing social norms, the passenger was justified in lightly tapping the woman on her back to get her attention. And the passenger had no reason to believe that the woman would not have consented to this contact because there is no indication that he should have known that she recently had back surgery (Choice C). Therefore, the woman is presumed to have consented to this ordinary contact of daily life and likely will not prevail in her battery claim.

(Choice B) The harm required for assault is apprehension of contact, whereas battery requires actual contact. Consequently, the fact that the woman was not put in apprehension by the touching is irrelevant to her battery claim.

(Choice D) The severity of the harm caused by an intentional touching has no effect on liability for battery (e.g., pinching and punching equally support a battery claim). Therefore, the seriousness of the woman's injury does not matter.

📌 Educational Objective

Presumed consent to contact exists when (1) under prevailing social norms, the defendant is justified in engaging in the conduct in the absence of the plaintiff's actual or apparent consent and (2) the defendant has no reason to believe that the plaintiff would not have actually consented had the defendant requested the plaintiff's consent.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Third) of Torts: Intentional Torts to Persons § 16 (Am. L. Inst., Tentative Draft No. 4, 2019) (setting forth the requirements for presumed consent).
questions.zh-question:
一名巴士乘客坐在他不认识的一名女子旁边。该女子起身准备下车，将一个包裹留在了座位上。该乘客为了引起她的注意并告知她忘记了包裹，轻轻地拍了拍她的背部。由于该女子最近刚做过背部手术，这次轻拍造成了疼痛，并导致她扭伤，背部严重受伤。

如果该女子就其背部伤害起诉该乘客要求赔偿，她是否可能胜诉？

zh-choices.A: 不会，因为她被推定为已经同意了日常生活中的普通接触。
zh-choices.B: 不会，因为该触碰并未使她产生担忧。
zh-choices.C: 会，因为她没有同意该有害接触。
zh-choices.D: 会，因为乘客的故意触碰严重伤害了她。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析：侵权法

Intentional Torts: Battery & Consent

核心考点：日常接触的同意

本题考察的是非法侵犯/殴打 (Battery) 的构成要件以及同意 (Consent) 这一抗辩事由。

Battery (非法侵犯) 的定义：
被告意图造成有害或冒犯性的身体接触，且该接触实际发生。
Intent to cause harmful or offensive contact, and such contact results.

虽然本案中存在“意图”和“接触”，但关键在于该接触是否具有“冒犯性” (Offensive) 以及原告是否“同意” (Consented)。

✅ 正确答案解析 (选项 A)

为什么该女子无法胜诉？

1
表见同意 (Apparent Consent)：
法律规定，在社会交往中，人们被推定为同意那些“日常生活中不可避免的普通接触” (Ordinary contacts of daily life)。
2
拥挤的世界理论 (Crowded World Theory)：
正如著名法官 Wallace 在判例中所述：“在一个拥挤的世界里，某种程度的人身接触是不可避免的，必须被接受。”
3
本案应用：
乘客为了提醒女子遗落物品而“轻轻拍打” (lightly tapped)，这属于社会公认的合理接触。除非女子事先明确表示拒绝触碰，否则法律推定她同意这种程度的接触。因此，该行为不构成 Battery。

❌ 干扰项排除

选项 B (Assault vs. Battery)
错误。恐吓/企图伤害 (Assault) 要求原告产生“担忧” (Apprehension)，但 Battery 不需要原告事先知情或担忧（例如背后袭击）。本题讨论的是 Battery，是否担忧与此无关。

选项 C (Harmful Contact)
错误。虽然接触确实导致了伤害，但缺乏“非法性”。因为存在“默示同意”，该接触在法律上是被允许的特权行为 (Privileged)。

选项 D (Severity of Injury)
错误。这是典型的误导。如果行为本身不构成侵权（因为有同意），那么无论后果多么严重，被告都不承担责任。只有当被告的行为首先构成侵权时，才需要对所有后果负责（薄头盖骨规则）。

🎓 MBE 考试技巧：薄头盖骨规则的陷阱

看到“背部手术”和“严重受伤”，很多考生会立刻想到薄头盖骨规则 (Eggshell Skull Rule) —— 即被告要对不可预见的严重后果负责。

⚠️ 注意：该规则仅在责任 (Liability) 确立后才适用！
如果是日常合理的轻拍，被告根本没有过错/责任，因此无需赔偿，无论原告的身体状况多么脆弱。

reason.zh: 接触的性质与目的决定是否适用推定同意。

questions.subject: Torts
questions.question:
A customer pledged a stock certificate to a bank as security for a loan. Under its loan agreement with the customer, the bank was obligated to return the certificate once the loan was repaid. A year later, when the customer fully repaid the loan, the bank refused the customer's demand to return the certificate because the officer dealing with the loan had the mistaken belief that there was still a balance due. No one at the bank reviewed the records until two months later, at which time the error was discovered. The bank then offered to return the certificate, but the customer refused to accept it. At the time the customer pledged the certificate, the shares were worth $10,000; at the time the customer repaid the loan, the shares were worth $20,000; and at the time the bank offered to return the certificate, the shares were worth $5,000.
If the customer brings an action against the bank based on conversion, how much, if anything, should the customer recover?

choices.A: Nothing, because the bank lawfully came into possession of the certificate.
choices.B: $5,000, because that was the value of the shares when the customer refused to accept the certificate back.
choices.C: $10,000, because that was the value of the shares when the bank came into possession of the certificate.
choices.D: $20,000, because that was the value of the shares when the customer was entitled to the return of the certificate.

questions.explanation:
Damages = fair market value at time of conversion
Customer gives
certificate to bank
$10,000
Conversion
Customer requests return of certificate and bank refuses
$20,000
Bank offers
to return
certificate
$5,000

Conversion (an intentional and substantial interference with another's right to control a chattel) occurs when a defendant refuses to return a chattel upon demand to a plaintiff who is entitled to its immediate possession. In the event of a conversion, the plaintiff can recover the fair market value of the chattel at the time of the conversion.

Here, conversion occurred when the bank refused to return the customer's stock certificate even though the customer had fully repaid the loan and was entitled to immediate possession of the certificate pursuant to the loan agreement. Accordingly, the customer should recover the fair market value of the shares when the bank refused to return the certificate in response to the customer's rightful demand (the time of conversion)—$20,000.

(Choice A) A defendant who refuses to return the plaintiff's chattel may be liable for conversion even if the defendant initially acquired the chattel lawfully. Therefore, though the bank lawfully obtained the stock certificate as security for the customer's loan, it committed conversion by refusing to return the certificate when the customer was entitled to immediate possession.

(Choices B & C) The customer should recover the fair market value of the certificate at the time of the conversion—not when the bank first came into possession of the certificate or when the customer refused to accept it back two months later.

📌 Educational Objective

Conversion occurs when a defendant refuses to return a chattel upon demand to a plaintiff entitled to its immediate possession, after which the plaintiff can recover the fair market value of the chattel at the time of the conversion.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Second) of Torts § 222A (Am. Law Inst. 1965) (definition of conversion).
  • Restatement (Second) of Torts § 237 (Am. Law Inst. 1965) (conversion by demand and refusal).
questions.zh-question:
一位客户向银行质押了一份股权凭证作为贷款担保。根据其与客户的贷款协议，一旦贷款偿还完毕，银行有义务返还该凭证。一年后，当客户全额偿还贷款时，银行拒绝了客户返还凭证的要求，因为处理该贷款的职员误以为仍有未付余额。直到两个月后，银行才有人审查记录，并发现了这个错误。银行随后提出返还该凭证，但客户拒绝接受。客户质押凭证时，该股票价值10,000美元；客户偿还贷款时，股票价值20,000美元；银行提出返还凭证时，股票价值5,000美元。

如果客户以conversion（动产侵占）为由对银行提起诉讼，客户应获得多少赔偿（如果有的话）？

zh-choices.A: 无，因为银行是合法占有该凭证的。
zh-choices.B: 5,000美元，因为这是客户拒绝收回凭证时股票的价值。
zh-choices.C: 10,000美元，因为这是银行占有该凭证时股票的价值。
zh-choices.D: 20,000美元，因为这是客户有权要求返还凭证时股票的价值。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Intentional Torts: Conversion
核心考点：动产侵占 (Conversion)
Conversion 是指被告有意地行使对他人动产 (Chattel) 的支配或控制，且这种干涉严重到了剥夺原告权利的程度，以至于法律强制被告按该动产的全额价值进行赔偿。这通常被称为“强制出售” (Forced Sale)。
本案法律逻辑推演
1
侵权行为的发生时刻
当客户还清贷款并要求返还凭证，而银行拒绝 (Refusal) 时，Conversion 就发生了。尽管银行最初是合法占有 (Lawful Possession)，但一旦拒绝归还权利人，合法占有即转变为侵权。
2
意图 (Intent) 与错误 (Mistake)
Conversion 是故意侵权 (Intentional Tort)，但这里的“故意”仅指故意实施了扣留行为。银行职员“误以为”还有余额 (Mistake of Fact) 并不是有效的抗辩理由。只要银行有意拒绝归还，就满足了 Intent 的要求。
3
赔偿金计算 (Measure of Damages)
Conversion 的标准赔偿是动产在侵占发生时 (Time of Conversion) 的公平市价 (Fair Market Value)。
4
结论
侵占发生时（即银行拒绝返还时），股票价值为 $20,000。因此，这就是客户应得的赔偿额。
易错点辨析
  • 选项 A (无责任): 错误。虽然最初占有合法，但拒绝返还即构成 Conversion。
  • 选项 B ($5,000): 错误。这是银行提出归还时的价值。在 Conversion 中，原告有权选择“强制被告买下”该物品，因此无需接受迟来的归还，尤其是在物品贬值后。
  • 选项 C ($10,000): 错误。这是质押时的价值，与侵权发生时的损失无关。
💡 考试技巧 (Exam Tip)
在处理 Conversion 题目时，记住口诀：
"You break it (or keep it), you bought it."
赔偿额永远锁定在侵权行为发生的那一刻的市场价值。

questions.subject: Torts
questions.question:
A disgruntled former employee of a corporation posted false job listings online for his former position. The false job listings directed applicants to email multiple documents, including a resume, to the employee's former manager. The employee intended to generate enough email responses to impede performance of the corporation's computer system.
However, the employee accidentally posted an email address belonging to a small business owner. As a result, the owner received hundreds of emails from job applicants. This made it hard for the owner to find emails relevant to her business but caused no functional disruption to her computer system. Upon discovering that the employee had posted the false job listings, the owner filed suit against the employee for trespass to chattels.
Should the owner prevail in her lawsuit?

choices.A: No, because the employee intended to interfere only with the corporation's computer system.
choices.B: No, because the owner cannot show that the employee's interference caused her actual damages.
choices.C: Yes, because the emails constituted an intentional invasion of another's property without permission or legal privilege.
choices.D: Yes, because the employee intentionally used or intermeddled with the owner's computer system.

questions.explanation:
Trespass to chattels
Plaintiff has possession or immediate right to possession of chattel
Defendant intentionally interferes with possession through either:
Dispossession
Harm inferred
Use or intermeddling
Causes harm
  • actual harm to chattel
  • substantial loss of use of chattel or
  • bodily harm to plaintiff

Trespass to chattels (ie, tangible personal property) occurs when an actor intentionally interferes with another's right of possession by either:

• dispossessing the other person of the chattel or

• using or intermeddling with the other person's chattel.

And under the doctrine of transferred intent, an actor's intent to commit trespass to chattels against one person will transfer to the actor's commission of the tort against a different person.* However, in the absence of actual damages (eg, actual harm to chattels), an action for trespass to chattels based on use or intermeddling will fail.

Here, the employee intended to intermeddle with the corporation's computer system by having email responses to the false job listings sent to the employee's former manager. This intent to commit a trespass to chattels then transferred to the owner when the employee accidentally directed the emails to the owner instead (Choice A). But since the emails caused no functional disruption to the owner's computer system, the owner cannot show that the employee's interference caused her actual damages. Therefore, the owner should not prevail (Choice B).

*Transferred intent applies if an actor intends to commit an intentional tort against one person but commits a different intentional tort against the same person, the same intentional tort against a different person, or a different intentional tort against a different person.

(Choice C) A trespass to land (ie, real property) is defined as an intentional invasion of another's property without permission or legal privilege. But here, the owner is suing for trespass to chattels (ie, tangible personal property).

Educational objective:

Trespass to chattels is an intentional interference with another's tangible personal property through dispossession, use, or intermeddling. The intent to commit this tort against one person will transfer to the commission of the tort against another person.

References
  • Restatement (Second) of Torts § 217 (Am. Law Inst. 1965) (ways of committing trespass to chattels).
  • Restatement (Third) of Torts: Liab. for Physical & Emotional Harm § 110 (Am. Law Inst. 2015) (transferred intent).
questions.zh-question:
一名心怀不满的公司前雇员在网上发布了关于其先前职位的虚假招聘信息。该虚假招聘信息指示申请人将包括简历在内的多份文件通过电子邮件发送给该雇员的前任经理。该雇员意图产生足够多的电子邮件回复，以阻碍公司计算机系统的性能。

然而，该雇员意外地发布了一个属于小企业主的电子邮件地址。结果，该企业主收到了数百封来自求职者的电子邮件。这使得企业主难以找到与她业务相关的电子邮件，但并未对她的计算机系统造成功能性中断。在发现该雇员发布了虚假招聘信息后，企业主以侵害动产（trespass to chattels）为由对该雇员提起诉讼。

该企业主能否在诉讼中获胜？

zh-choices.A: 否，因为该雇员的意图只是干扰公司的计算机系统。
zh-choices.B: 否，因为该企业主无法证明雇员的干扰行为对她造成了实际损害。
zh-choices.C: 是，因为这些电子邮件构成了未经许可或法律特权对他人财产的故意侵犯。
zh-choices.D: 是，因为该雇员故意使用或干涉了企业主的计算机系统。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Intentional Torts: Trespass to Chattels

正确答案：B 企业主不能胜诉，因为她无法证明该干扰行为造成了实际损害 (Actual Damages)。
核心法律规则解析

侵害动产 (Trespass to Chattels) 是指故意干涉他人对动产的占有权。这种干涉分为两种形式，其对“损害”的要求截然不同：

1. 剥夺占有 (Dispossession)
行为人拿走了动产。此时，损害是推定的，原告不需要证明实际损失即可起诉。
2. 使用或干涉 (Intermeddling)
行为人没有拿走动产，只是触碰、使用或干扰它（如本题中的发送垃圾邮件）。此时，原告必须证明有实际损害 (Actual Damages)。
本案逻辑推演
  • 行为定性：雇员发送垃圾邮件的行为属于“干涉” (Intermeddling)，而非“剥夺占有”。
  • 损害要件：题目明确指出，虽然很难找到邮件，但“未对计算机系统造成功能性中断” (caused no functional disruption)。
  • 结论：在电子侵权（如垃圾邮件）的判例中（例如著名的 Intel Corp. v. Hamidi），如果仅仅是占用了服务器空间或造成了不便，而没有导致系统物理损坏或功能受损，通常不构成 Trespass to Chattels 的实际损害。
为什么其他选项错误？
  • 选项 A (Transferred Intent)：虽然雇员想干扰的是公司，但根据意图转移 (Transferred Intent) 原则，意图会转移到实际受害者（企业主）身上。所以意图不是抗辩理由，A 错误。
  • 选项 C (Invasion of Property)：这是混淆了侵害不动产 (Trespass to Land)。侵害不动产不需要证明实际损害，但本案涉及的是计算机系统（动产）。
  • 选项 D (Intentional Use)：虽然雇员确实故意使用了系统，但如前所述，对于“使用/干涉”类型的侵害动产，仅有故意是不够的，必须伴随实际损害。
💡 MBE 考试技巧 遇到涉及计算机、服务器或电子数据的 Trespass to Chattels 题目时，务必寻找“物理损坏”或“功能性瘫痪”。

如果题目说“仅仅是烦人”、“降低了工作效率”但系统本身完好无损，通常答案都是No，理由是缺乏 Actual Damages。

questions.topic: Defenses to claims for physical harms
questions.question:
While in line for the restroom at a football game, the defendant overheard two fans arguing at the front of the line. The defendant could not see their faces, but he could see that one fan was six feet tall with black hair and a red jersey and the other was wearing a blue jersey. The defendant then saw the fan in red hit the other fan in the face with the butt of a handgun, and the fan in blue ran away with a bloody nose. The fan in red ran into the bathroom. The defendant immediately ran into the restroom and grabbed a six-foot-tall man with black hair and a red jersey, telling him he was under arrest for battery. The defendant then locked the man in a bathroom stall. When a security guard arrived, the defendant let the man out of the stall. It then became clear that the defendant had apprehended the wrong person and that the fan who had committed the battery had already been apprehended and arrested for felony aggravated battery.
Assume that the majority rules for intentional torts and their defenses apply.
If the man sues the defendant for false imprisonment, is he likely to succeed?

choices.A: No, because a battery occurred in the defendant's presence.
choices.B: No, because the defendant made a reasonable mistake as to the man's identity.
choices.C: Yes, because the defendant arrested the man by using unreasonable force.
choices.D: Yes, because the man did not commit a battery.

• defendant reasonably believes that law enforcement will likely be unable to apprehend plaintiff unless defendant immediately confines plaintiff
Misdemeanor Majority
• Misdemeanor is being committed or reasonably appears about to be committed in presence of defendant and
• misdemeanor is breach of peace
Third
Restatement
• Misdemeanor creates substantial risk of bodily harm and
• defendant reasonably believes that law enforcement will likely be unable to prevent or terminate crime unless defendant immediately uses force

In most jurisdictions, false imprisonment occurs when a defendant intentionally confines the plaintiff within a limited area and the plaintiff is conscious of the confinement. However, in most jurisdictions, a defendant who is a private citizen (i.e., not a law-enforcement officer) is privileged to confine or arrest a plaintiff when:

• a felony has been committed and
• the defendant reasonably suspects that the plaintiff committed the felony.

And under this approach, this privilege applies even if the private actor makes a reasonable mistake as to the felon's identity.

Here, the defendant intentionally confined the man to the bathroom stall, placing him under arrest. The defendant mistakenly believed that the man had hit another fan in the face with the butt of a handgun (i.e., a felony). But this mistake was reasonable because the man and the perpetrator shared similar physical attributes (six feet tall, black hair, and red jersey). Because the defendant made a reasonable mistake as to the man's identity, this conduct is privileged. Therefore, the man is unlikely to succeed if he sues the defendant for false imprisonment.

*However, the privilege will not apply when the mistake is as to whether a felony occurred.

(Choice A) The fact that the battery occurred in the defendant's presence is insufficient to support his arrest of the man. The defendant also need to have reasonable grounds to believe that the man was the one who committed the felony.

(Choice C) Locking the man in a bathroom stall until a security guard arrived was reasonable force under the circumstances.

(Choice D) Although the man did not actually commit the battery, the defendant is not liable because he made a reasonable mistake as to the felon's identity.

📌 Educational Objective

In most jurisdictions, a defendant who is a private citizen is privileged to confine or arrest a plaintiff when (1) a felony has been committed and (2) the defendant reasonably suspects that the plaintiff committed it. This privilege applies even if the private actor makes a reasonable mistake as to the felon's identity.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Third) of Torts § 7: Intentional Torts to Persons (Am. L. Inst., Tentative Draft No. 3, 2018) (providing the definition for false imprisonment).
  • Restatement (Third) of Torts: Intentional Torts to Persons § 35 (Am. L. Inst., Tentative Draft No. 6, 2021) (explaining the privilege of arrest).

questions.subject: Torts
questions.question:
An elderly woman had no living relatives or close friends. A much younger man who lived nearby befriended the woman in an effort to convince her to devise her house and other property to him in a will. Shortly thereafter, a new family moved next door to the woman. The woman developed a close friendship with the family. When the woman later refused to execute a will in the man's favor, he blamed the family. The man decided to cause the woman severe emotional distress by kidnapping the family and holding them hostage in the woman's home while she was away. The man did so and told the woman about it. The woman suffered severe emotional distress that caused her to suffer a heart attack.
The woman sued the man for intentional infliction of emotional distress.
Will the woman be likely to prevail in that action?

choices.A: No, because the woman was not present when the man kidnapped the family and held them hostage.
choices.B: No, because the woman was not related to the family.
choices.C: Yes, because the man acted with the purpose of causing the woman severe emotional distress.
choices.D: Yes, because the woman suffered bodily injury.

questions.explanation:
Explanation
IIED liability for emotional distress
caused by harm to third party
Δ's extreme & outrageous conduct
physically or emotionally harmed third party
Δ was at least reckless as to risk of causing IIED severe emotional distress because:
• TT contemporaneously perceived conduct
• TT was close relative of injured person
TT suffered severe emotional distress as a result
Liable for IIED
(fast track)
Δ's purpose was to
cause TT severe
emotional distress

Intentional infliction of emotional distress (IIED) requires proof that the defendant was at least reckless as to the risk that his/her extreme and outrageous conduct would cause the plaintiff severe emotional distress. To establish this element in cases where the plaintiff's distress stems from conduct that physically or emotionally harmed a third party, the plaintiff must generally prove the following facts:

• The plaintiff contemporaneously perceived it (i.e., saw or overheard) the defendant's conduct.
• The plaintiff was a close relative (i.e., immediate family member) of the harmed third party.

However, the plaintiff need not prove the above facts if the defendant's design or purpose was to cause severe emotional distress to the plaintiff.

Here, the man kidnapped and held the family (a third party) hostage in the woman's home, which caused her to suffer severe emotional distress. The woman was neither present when the man kidnapped and held the family hostage (no contemporaneous perception) nor related to the family, which ordinarily would defeat her claim for IIED. But since the man acted with the purpose of causing the woman severe emotional distress, she will likely prevail (Choices A & B).

(Choice D) Severe emotional distress is often accompanied by bodily injury (e.g., heart attack). Although this helps prove that the emotional distress is genuine, recovery for IIED is not limited to cases in which bodily injury occurs.

📌 Educational Objective

A defendant whose extreme and outrageous conduct harmed a third party may be liable for intentional infliction of emotional distress on the plaintiff—regardless of whether the plaintiff witnessed the conduct or was closely related to the third party.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Third) of Torts: Liability for Physical & Emotional Harm § 46 cmt. m (Am. L. Inst. 2012)

questions.subject: Torts
questions.question:
The warden of a state prison prohibits the photographing of the face of any prisoner without the prisoner's consent. A news photographer wanted to photograph a notorious mobster incarcerated at the prison. To circumvent the warden's prohibition, the photographer flew over the prison exercise yard and photographed the mobster. A prisoner, who was imprisoned for a technical violation of a regulatory statute, happened to be standing next to the mobster when the photograph was taken.
When the picture appeared in the press, the prisoner suffered severe emotional distress because he believed that his business associates and friends would think he was consorting with gangsters. The prisoner suffered no physical harm as the result of his emotional distress. The prisoner brought an action against the photographer for intentional or reckless infliction of emotional distress.
What is the best argument that the photographer can make in support of a motion for summary judgment?

choices.A: As a news photographer, he was privileged to take photographs that others could not.
choices.B: No reasonable person could conclude that the photographer intended to photograph the prisoner.
choices.C: No reasonable person could conclude that the photographer's conduct was extreme and outrageous as to the prisoner.
choices.D: The prisoner did not suffer any physical injury arising from the emotional distress.

questions.explanation:
Defendant's motion for summary judgment
For intentional infliction of emotional distress,
a reasonable jury could find:
↓
A intended to cause π severe emotional distress
(or was reckless as to the risk)
No
Grant motion
↓
A's conduct was extreme and outrageous
No
Grant motion
↓
A caused π severe emotional distress
No
Grant motion
↓
Deny motion

A defendant's motion for summary judgment will be granted when there is no genuine issue of material fact (ie, no reasonable jury could find in the plaintiff's favor) and the defendant is entitled to judgment as a matter of law (eg, at least one element of the plaintiff's claim lacks legally sufficient evidence). For intentional or reckless infliction of emotional distress (IIED), the defendant's motion should be granted if it disproves one or more of the following elements:

  • The defendant intended to cause the plaintiff severe emotional distress (or acted recklessly as to the risk of causing such distress).
  • The defendant's conduct was extreme and outrageous.
  • The defendant caused the plaintiff severe emotional distress.

Accordingly, the photographer's best argument is that no reasonable person could find that his conduct was extreme and outrageous.

(Choice A) News photographers are not immune from liability for IIED, so the photographer could be liable like any other person—if all the elements of this claim are met.

(Choice B) IIED requires the specific intent to cause severe emotional distress—not intent to do the act that caused the distress. Therefore, even if no reasonable person could find that the photographer intended to photograph the prisoner, the photographer's summary judgment motion would fail if a reasonable person could still find that he intended to cause the prisoner severe emotional distress (or recklessly caused that distress).

(Choice C) Although most tort claims require proof of bodily harm before plaintiffs can recover for emotional harm, IIED claims allow plaintiffs to recover for stand-alone emotional harm (eg, emotional harm that does not result from bodily harm). Therefore, the prisoner's lack of physical injury does not support the photographer's motion for summary judgment.

(Choice D) Although most tort claims require proof of bodily harm before plaintiffs can recover for emotional harm, IIED claims allow plaintiffs to recover for stand-alone emotional harm (eg, emotional harm that does not result from bodily harm). Therefore, the prisoner's lack of physical injury does not support the photographer's motion for summary judgment.

📌 Educational Objective

For intentional infliction of emotional distress, the plaintiff must prove that the defendant intentionally or recklessly caused the plaintiff severe emotional distress by acting in an extreme and outrageous manner.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Third) of Torts: Liab. for Physical & Emotional Harm § 46 (Am. Law Inst. 2012) (intentional or reckless infliction of emotional distress).
  • Fed. R. Civ. P. 56(a) (summary judgment).
questions.zh-question:
州立监狱的典狱长禁止在未经囚犯同意的情况下拍摄其面部。一名新闻摄影师想拍摄一名被关押在该监狱的臭名昭著的黑帮分子。为了规避典狱长的禁令，该摄影师飞越监狱的操场，并拍摄了那名黑帮分子。一名因技术性违反监管法规而入狱的囚犯，在照片拍摄时恰好站在那名黑帮分子旁边。

当照片在媒体上刊登后，该囚犯遭受了严重的情感困扰，因为他认为他的商业伙伴和朋友会认为他在与黑帮为伍。该囚犯并未因其情感困扰而遭受任何身体伤害。该囚犯对摄影师提起了诉讼，诉由为故意或鲁莽造成情感困扰。

摄影师为支持其即决判决动议，可以提出的最佳论点是什么？

zh-choices.A: 作为一名新闻摄影师，他享有拍摄他人所不能拍摄的照片的特权。
zh-choices.B: 没有一个理性人会认为摄影师有意图拍摄该囚犯。
zh-choices.C: 没有一个理性人会认为摄影师对该囚犯的行为是极端和过分的。
zh-choices.D: 该囚犯没有因情感困扰而遭受任何身体伤害。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Intentional Torts: IIED

故意造成情感困扰

⚖️ 核心法律规则

要确立 IIED (Intentional Infliction of Emotional Distress) 侵权责任，原告必须证明以下四个要素：

1. 行为 (Act) 被告的行为必须是极端和过分的 (Extreme and Outrageous)。
2. 意图 (Intent) 被告故意造成严重情感困扰，或对此表现出鲁莽 (Recklessness)。
3. 因果关系 (Causation) 被告的行为导致了原告的困扰。
4. 损害 (Damages) 原告遭受了严重的情感困扰 (Severe Emotional Distress)。

✅ 正确答案解析：选项 C

最佳论点 "没有一个理性人会认为摄影师的行为是极端和过分的。"

为什么这是最佳论点？

在即决判决 (Summary Judgment) 阶段，法官需要判断是否存在事实争议。对于 IIED 来说，"极端和过分" (Extreme and Outrageous) 是一个非常高的门槛。

  • 法律标准： 行为必须"超越了文明社会中所有可能的体面界限" (beyond all possible bounds of decency)，被视为"极其残暴且完全无法容忍" (atrocious and utterly intolerable)。
  • 本案分析： 摄影师虽然违反了监狱规定（规章违规），甚至可能构成对监狱领空的侵入，但单纯的拍照行为（即使是偷拍）通常不被视为法律意义上的"极端和过分"。
  • 结论： 如果行为本身达不到这个高门槛，原告的案件在法律上就无法成立 (fail as a matter of law)。这是被告最强有力的防御。

❌ 常见陷阱与错误选项

陷阱 D "没有遭受身体伤害"

这是 MBE 考试中关于 IIED 最经典的干扰项。

  • 考点： 大多数侵权行为（如过失致人情感困扰 NIED）通常要求有身体伤害或身体症状。但 IIED 是个例外。
  • 规则： IIED 允许对独立的情感伤害 (Stand-alone emotional harm) 进行索赔，不需要证明身体受损。

陷阱 B "无意图拍摄该囚犯"

这个选项很有迷惑性，但不够强。

  • 理由： IIED 的意图要素包括鲁莽 (Recklessness)。即使摄影师不想拍那个囚犯，如果他为了拍黑帮分子而鲁莽地无视了可能给旁人造成的严重困扰，他仍可能承担责任。
  • 对比： 相比之下，攻击行为本身的性质（选项C）是更基础的法律门槛。

错误 A "新闻特权"

新闻媒体没有实施侵权行为（如非法侵入或 IIED）的特权。此论点在法律上站不住脚。

🎓 MBE 实战技巧

遇到 IIED 题目时，请按以下步骤思考：

  1. 检查行为性质： 行为是否真的"令人发指"？（简单的侮辱、烦扰或轻微威胁通常不够）。这是最常见的考点。
  2. 检查伤害类型： 是否有"严重"的情感困扰？（不需要身体伤害，但困扰必须严重）。
  3. 区分 IIED 与 NIED：
    • IIED (故意)： 不需要身体伤害。
    • NIED (过失)： 通常需要身体伤害或处于危险区域 (Zone of Danger)。
Based on NCBE MBE Standards • Q83023

questions.subject: Torts
questions.question:
As an encyclopedia salesman approached the grounds on which a woman's house was situated, the salesman saw a sign that said, "No salesmen. Trespassers will be prosecuted. Proceed at your own risk." Although the salesman had not been invited to enter, he ignored the sign and drove up the driveway toward the house. As he rounded a curve, a powerful explosive charge buried in the driveway detonated, and the salesman was injured.
Is the salesman likely to recover damages from the woman for his injuries?

choices.A: No, because the salesman ignored the sign, which warned him against proceeding further.
choices.B: No, if the woman reasonably feared that intruders would come and harm her or her family.
choices.C: Yes, because the woman's sign made trespassers anticipate imminent harmful contact.
choices.D: Yes, if the woman was responsible for the explosive charge under the driveway.

questions.explanation:
Explanation

Two types of intent

Two types of intent

A defendant is liable for battery if the defendant intends to cause contact with the plaintiff's person and the defendant's affirmative conduct causes contact that is harmful or offensive to the plaintiff. Intent for battery exists when the defendant acts with either:

  • purpose – the desire to cause contact with the plaintiff's person or
  • knowledge - the substantial certainty that such contact will result.

Here, the salesman was injured by an explosive charge that detonated in the woman's driveway (harmful contact). And the woman would have been substantially certain that the charge would contact a person driving over it had she planted it under the driveway (intent). If she did so, then the salesman is likely to recover damages for battery and also defendense.

(Choice A) Assumption of the risk--i.e., the plaintiff's voluntary acceptance of a known risk of harm—is an affirmative defense to negligence or strict liability, but not to intentional torts like battery (as seen here). Even if this defense did apply, the salesman did not knowingly or voluntarily accept the risk of harm because the woman's sign only warned of prosecution—not explosion.

(Choice B) A person is privileged to use reasonable force to defend his/her property against trespassers. However, deadly force (e.g., the explosive charge) is reasonable only if the defendant reasonably believes the trespasser is about to inflict death or serious bodily harm (not seen here). Therefore, the woman was not privileged to use deadly force.

(Choice C) Liability for assault arises when (1) the defendant intends to cause the plaintiff to anticipate an imminent, harmful or offensive, contact with the plaintiff's person and (2) the defendant's affirmative conduct causes such anticipation. But here, the woman's sign did not cause that anticipation because it warned of prosecution—not harmful or offensive contact.

📌 Educational Objective

Battery liability arises when the defendant intended (i.e., purposefully or knowingly) to cause contact with the plaintiff's person and the defendant's affirmative conduct caused contact that was harmful or offensive to the plaintiff.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Third) of Torts: Intentional Torts to Persons § 102 (Am. L. Inst., Tentative Draft No. 1, 2015) (defining the requisite intent for battery).
questions.zh-question:
一名百科全书推销员在接近一名女子房屋所在的场地时，看到了一个牌子，上面写着：“推销员不得入内。非法侵入者将被起诉。进入后果自负。”尽管推销员未被邀请进入，他无视了该牌子，并开车沿着车道向房屋驶去。当他拐过一个弯时，埋在车道里的一个强力爆炸装置爆炸了，导致推销员受伤。

该推销员是否有可能因其所受伤害向该女子要求损害赔偿？

zh-choices.A: 不会，因为推销员无视了警告他不要继续前进的牌子。
zh-choices.B: 不会，如果该女子有合理理由担心入侵者会前来伤害她或她的家人。
zh-choices.C: 会，如果该女子对车道下的爆炸装置负有责任。
zh-choices.D: 会，除非该女子在埋设爆炸装置时，其意图仅为威慑而非伤害可能的入侵者。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Intentional Torts & Defenses
核心法则：财产防卫 (Defense of Property)

业主可以使用合理武力 (Reasonable Force) 来保护财产，但绝不能仅为了保护财产而使用致命武力 (Deadly Force) 或造成严重身体伤害的武力。

🚫 禁止使用机械陷阱： 法律禁止使用弹簧枪 (Spring guns) 或陷阱来伤害入侵者，除非该入侵者对业主构成了死亡或严重伤害的威胁。

案情逻辑推演

本题考察的是故意侵权行为中的非法侵犯/殴打 (Battery) 及其抗辩理由。

  1. 原告身份： 推销员无视警告牌进入，属于非法侵入者 (Trespasser)。
  2. 被告行为： 埋设强力爆炸装置 (Powerful explosive charge)。这属于致命武力。
  3. 法律后果： 尽管原告是非法侵入者，但被告无权使用致命武力来保卫空无一人的财产（车道）。
  4. 意图 (Intent)： 埋设地雷/陷阱意味着被告对有人触发并受伤具有“实质确定性 (Substantial Certainty)”，因此构成 Battery 的意图。
📚 经典判例联想：Katko v. Briney (1971)
这是美国法学院著名的“弹簧枪案”。房主在无人居住的农舍安装了猎枪陷阱，打伤了小偷。法院判决房主败诉，因为“法律对人类生命和肢体安全的重视高于对财产权益的保护”。
选项深度解析
正确 C 会，如果该女子对车道下的爆炸装置负有责任。
这是唯一正确的结论。只要证明是该女子埋设了炸弹（即证明了 Causation 和 Intent），她就必须为 Battery 负责。因为使用致命武力保护财产不是有效的抗辩理由 (Privilege)。
错误 A 不会，因为推销员无视了警告...
虽然推销员是 Trespasser，但这并不赋予房主将其“炸飞”的权利。非法侵入不是遭受致命武力的正当理由。此外，警告牌只说了“会被起诉 (Prosecuted)”，并没有警告“会被炸死”。
错误 B 不会，如果该女子有合理理由担心...
这是一个干扰项。自卫 (Self-Defense) 需要面对迫在眉睫 (Imminent) 的威胁。预先埋设的炸弹是无差别的，它无法判断当下的入侵者是否真的构成威胁。除非炸弹爆炸时，该女子正面临生命危险，否则此抗辩不成立。
错误 D 会，除非...意图仅为威慑...
法律上的意图 (Intent) 不等于动机 (Motive)。即使动机是“威慑”，但埋设炸弹的行为本身就包含了对“有人会受伤”的实质确定性 (Substantial Certainty)。因此，仅有威慑的动机不能免除 Battery 的责任。
MBE 考试技巧：
看到“保护财产” + “致命陷阱/恶犬/枪支”
👉 几乎总是判定房主有罪/赔偿。
生命权 (Life/Limb) > 财产权 (Property)。

questions.subject: Torts
questions.question:
A bank employee took substantial kickbacks to approve certain loans that later proved worthless. Upon learning of the kickbacks, the bank president fired the employee, telling him, "If you are not out of this bank in 10 minutes, I will have the guards throw you out bodily." The employee left at once.
If the employee asserts an assault claim against the bank president, will the employee prevail?

choices.A: No, because the bank president gave the employee 10 minutes to leave.
choices.B: No, because the guards never touched the employee.
choices.C: Yes, because the bank president threatened the employee with harmful or offensive bodily contact.
choices.D: Yes, if the bank president intended to cause the employee severe emotional distress.

questions.explanation:
Explanation

Elements of civil assault

Mental state
Δ intended to cause π to anticipate imminent, & harmful or offensive contact with π's person
↓
Causation
Δ's affirmative conduct caused π to anticipate such contact

Δ = defendant, π = plaintiff.

Assault requires that a defendant cause the plaintiff to anticipate imminent harmful or offensive contact. Imminent means without significant delay. Therefore, a defendant is not liable for assault if the defendant causes anticipation of future contact.

Here, the employee was not placed in anticipation of imminent contact because the bank president threatened future harm—i.e., that he would have the guards throw the employee out bodily if he did not leave in 10 minutes. Because the threat of future harm does not satisfy the imminent-contact requirement, the bank president is not liable for assault.

(Choice B) Assault only requires anticipation of imminent contact, so the employee need not prove that the guards actually touched him. In contrast, battery—i.e., an intentional act that causes harmful or offensive contact with another—requires proof of actual contact.

(Choice C) Although the bank president threatened the employee with bodily contact, assault requires anticipation of imminent contact. Since the bank president threatened future contact (after 10 minutes), he is not liable for assault.

(Choice D) Severe emotional distress is not an element of assault. Rather, it is an element of intentional infliction of emotional distress—i.e., extreme or outrageous conduct that intentionally or recklessly causes a plaintiff severe emotional distress.

📌 Educational Objective

Assault requires anticipation of imminent contact. Therefore, a threat of future contact does not support an assault claim.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Third) of Torts: Intentional Torts to Persons § 105 cmt. e (Am. L. Inst., Tentative Draft No. 1, 2015) (explaining the imminence requirement for assault).
questions.zh-question:
一名银行雇员收受巨额回扣，批准了一些后来被证明毫无价值的贷款。银行行长得知回扣事件后，解雇了该雇员，并告诉他：“如果你十分钟内不离开这家银行，我将让警卫把你扔出去。”该雇员立即离开了。

如果该雇员对银行行长提起胁迫攻击(assault)的诉讼，他会胜诉吗？

zh-choices.A: 不会，因为银行行长给了该雇员十分钟的离开时间。
zh-choices.B: 不会，因为警卫从未触碰过该雇员。

zh-choices.D: 会，如果银行行长意图对该雇员造成严重的情感困扰。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点精讲

Intentional Torts: Assault
⚖️ 核心法律规则

Assault (恐吓/胁迫) 的成立必须满足以下要素：

  1. 被告实施了故意行为 (Intentional act)；
  2. 导致原告产生了合理的恐惧/预期 (Reasonable Apprehension)；
  3. 恐惧的内容是即刻发生的 (Imminent) 有害或冒犯性接触。

🔍 为什么选 A？

本题的关键在于 Imminence (即刻性)。

Assault 要求受害人感到的威胁是迫在眉睫的，意味着“没有明显的延迟”(without significant delay)。

在本案中，银行行长说：

"If you are not out... in ten minutes..."
（如果你十分钟内不离开……）

这构成了 对未来伤害的威胁 (Threat of future harm)。

虽然十分钟很短，但在法律上，只要给了受害人逃避或采取其他行动的时间窗口，就不满足“即刻发生”的要求。因此，Assault 不成立。

🚫 为什么其他选项是错的？

❌ 选项 B (No touch):
这是混淆了 Assault 和 Battery。Assault 是“心理上的恐惧”，不需要实际的身体接触。只要有即刻接触的恐惧即可。
❌ 选项 C (Threat of contact):
虽然确实有威胁，但忽略了“即刻性”要素。仅仅威胁身体接触是不够的，必须是马上就要发生的接触。
❌ 选项 D (Emotional Distress):
这是 IIED (Intentional Infliction of Emotional Distress) 的标准，而不是 Assault。Assault 保护的是“免受即刻身体接触恐惧”的利益，而不是免受情绪困扰。
🎓 MBE 实战技巧

在处理 Assault 题目时，警惕以下两种情况，它们通常不构成 Assault：

  • 附条件的威胁 (Conditional Threats): "If you weren't an old man, I would hit you." (如果你不是老人，我就打你了 —— 意味着现在不会打)。
  • 未来的威胁 (Future Threats): "I will beat you up tomorrow / in 10 minutes." (缺乏即刻性)。
