questions.subject: Torts
questions.question:
A young man was walking peacefully along a public street when he encountered a woman he had never seen before. Without provocation or warning, the woman picked up a rock and struck the young man with it. It was later established that the woman was mentally ill and suffered recurrent visual hallucinations.
In an action by the young man against the woman for battery, which of the following, if supported by evidence, will be the woman's best defense?

choices.A: The woman did not desire to cause harm to the young man.
choices.B: The woman did not know that she was striking a person.
choices.C: The woman did not understand that her act was wrongful.
choices.D: The woman thought the young man was about to attack her.

questions.explanation:
Effect of mental deficiency on intent

Deficient mental capacity is not a defense to liability for intentional torts. Instead, mental capacity is considered when determining whether the defendant acted with the requisite intent. For battery, the defendant must act with the intent—i.e., the purpose or knowledge—to cause contact with the plaintiff's person.

Here, although the woman struck the young man with a rock, she is liable for battery only if she did so with the intent to strike him. Therefore, the woman's best defense is that she did not know she was striking a person—e.g., her recurrent visual hallucinations caused her to perceive the young man as a tree or wild dog.

(Choice A) A majority of jurisdictions apply the single-intent rule for battery, under which a defendant must intend to cause a contact but need not intend for that contact to be harmful or offensive. Therefore, even if the woman did not desire to harm the young man, she would be liable for battery if she intended to make contact with him.

(Choice B) To meet the intent requirement for battery, the woman had to understand that she was striking the young man with a rock—not that her act was wrongful.

(Choice C) Self-defense is only available as a defense if the defendant reasonably believed that force was necessary. Here, the woman could not have reasonably believed that the young man was about to attack her because he was walking peacefully. Therefore, this defense is not available.

📌 Educational Objective

Deficient mental capacity is not a defense to liability for intentional torts, but it is considered in determining whether the defendant acted with the requisite intent. Battery requires the intent to cause contact with the plaintiff's person.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Third) of Torts: Intentional Torts to Persons § 102 cmt. a (Am. L. Inst., Tentative Draft No. 1, 2015) (discussing a mentally impaired individual's ability to form the requisite intent for battery).
questions.zh-question:
一名年轻男子在公共街道上平静地行走时，遇到了一位他从未见过的女子。在没有任何挑衅或警告的情况下，该女子捡起一块石头砸向该年轻男子。后来证实，该女子患有精神疾病，并有复发性幻视。

在该年轻男子以伤害罪（battery）起诉该女子的诉讼中，如果以下哪一项得到证据支持，将是该女子最好的抗辩理由？

zh-choices.A: 该女子无意对该年轻男子造成伤害。
zh-choices.B: 该女子不知道她正在攻击的是一个人。
zh-choices.C: 该女子不明白她的行为是错误的。
zh-choices.D: 该女子认为该年轻男子即将攻击她。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Intentional Torts & Mental Capacity
⚖️ 核心原则 (General Rule) 在侵权法中，精神疾病 (Insanity) 本身并不是故意侵权行为的抗辩理由。只要被告具有实施侵权行为所需的“意图 (Intent)”，无论其动机是否源于妄想，都需承担责任。
✅ 为什么选 B 是最好的抗辩？

本题考察的是 Battery（非法侵犯/殴打）构成要件中的 Intent（意图）。

Battery 的意图要求被告意图引起有害或冒犯性的身体接触 (Intent to cause harmful or offensive contact)。

虽然精神错乱通常不能免责，但如果精神错乱导致被告无法形成必要的意图，则不构成侵权。

  • 如果选项 B 成立（她不知道她在打一个人），说明她的幻觉极其严重（例如她以为她在敲打一块木头或驱赶空气）。
  • 在这种情况下，她缺乏与“人”进行接触的意图。没有意图，Battery 的构成要件就不满足。

这是否定原告立案依据 (Prima Facie Case) 的抗辩，因此是“最好”的。

❌ 为什么其他选项无效？
选项 A (无意造成伤害):
Battery 不需要意图造成“伤害 (Harm)”，只需要意图造成“接触 (Contact)”。只要接触本身是有害或冒犯性的即可。这是 Intent to Contact vs Intent to Harm 的区别。
选项 C (不明白行为是错误的):
这是刑法中 M'Naghten Rule 的标准，不适用于侵权法。在侵权法中，被告是否具有道德上的罪责感 (Moral Culpability) 是无关紧要的。
选项 D (误以为自卫):
自卫 (Self-Defense) 要求被告的信念必须是客观合理的 (Reasonably Believed)。基于精神妄想的“自卫”是不合理的，因此不能作为有效的肯定性抗辩 (Affirmative Defense)。
💡 MBE 避坑指南

切勿混淆刑法与侵权法！

在刑法 (Criminal Law) 中，精神错乱 (Insanity) 是一个完整的抗辩理由。但在侵权法 (Torts) 中，精神病患者通常要对故意侵权负责（如 McGuire v. Almy 案）。

解题关键： 只有当精神状态导致被告甚至不知道自己做了动作或不知道接触对象是人时，才能因“缺乏意图”而免责。

questions.subject: Torts
questions.question:
In an action for battery, the evidence established the following: The plaintiff was bad-tempered and, as the defendant knew, carried a gun and used it often; the plaintiff struck the defendant first; during the altercation, the plaintiff repeatedly tried to get to his gun; the defendant picked up a metal pipe and hit the plaintiff multiple times; and the blows inflicted upon the plaintiff by the defendant resulted in the plaintiff being hospitalized.
Which finding of fact would be most likely to result in a verdict for the defendant?

choices.A: The defendant actually believed that hitting the plaintiff with the metal pipe was the only way to protect himself against death or serious bodily harm.
choices.B: The defendant actually feared death or serious bodily harm.
choices.C: The defendant reasonably believed that hitting the plaintiff with the metal pipe was the only way to protect himself against death or serious bodily harm.
choices.D: The defendant was justified in retaliating against the plaintiff because the plaintiff struck the first blow.

questions.explanation:
Explanation
Deadly force in self-defense
Defendant reasonably believes:
  • individual is intentionally inflicting or about to intentionally inflict unprivileged force upon defendant
  • defendant is put in peril of death, serious bodily harm, or rape by use or threat of physical force and
  • defendant can safely prevent peril only by immediate use of deadly force

A defendant is not liable for an intentional tort (e.g., battery) committed while acting in self-defense—i.e., the privilege to use force to protect oneself against another's use of unprivileged force. However, a defendant can only use deadly force in self-defense when the defendant reasonably believes that:

  • an individual is intentionally inflicting or about to intentionally inflict unprivileged force upon the defendant
  • the defendant is put in peril of death, serious bodily harm, or rape by the use or threat of physical force and
  • the defendant can safely prevent the peril only by the immediate use of deadly force

Here, the defendant hit the plaintiff with a metal pipe multiple times. But the plaintiff struck the defendant first and repeatedly tried to grab his gun that he had often used. This would lead the defendant to reasonably believe that (1) the plaintiff was about to intentionally inflict unprivileged force upon the defendant, (2) such force put the defendant in peril of death or serious bodily harm, and (3) such peril could be prevented only by hitting the plaintiff with the metal pipe (deadly force). Therefore, such a finding would most likely result in a verdict for the defendant.

(Choices A & B) The use of deadly force in self-defense requires that the defendant reasonably fear death, serious bodily harm, or rape and reasonably believe that deadly force is required. The defendant's actual fear or belief is not enough to establish this privilege.

(Choice D) The self-defense privilege never permits retaliation and terminates once there is no further threat of harm—e.g., the defendant would not be privileged to use force in self-defense if the plaintiff walked away after striking the first blow.

📌 Educational Objective

A defendant is privileged to use deadly force in self-defense if the defendant reasonably believes that (1) a person is intentionally inflicting or about to intentionally inflict unprivileged force, (2) such force puts the defendant in peril of death, serious bodily harm, or rape, and (3) he/she can prevent the peril only by immediately using deadly force.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Third) of Torts: Intentional Torts to Persons § 23 (Am. L. Inst., Tentative Draft No. 6, 2021) (explaining when deadly force may be used in self-defense).

questions.subject: Torts
questions.question:
A company owned and operated a private golf course. One of the fairways on the course ran parallel to a navigable body of water that is rarely used by boats. The company was aware that golfers frequently but unintentionally hit golf balls into the water when playing that hole because there were no barriers to prevent the balls from going into the water. The golf balls resulted in pollution of the water in violation of a local ordinance that prohibits the pollution of bodies of water in the jurisdiction.
A 12-year-old child was sailing on the water with his family when he was struck by a golf ball that a golfer unintentionally hit from the golf course toward the water. The child suffered a serious physical injury.
The injured child's parents have filed a public nuisance action against the company, on behalf of their child, to recover for his injuries.
Are the parents precluded from recovery?

choices.A: No, because of the attractive nuisance doctrine.
choices.B: No, because the child suffered harm that was different from that suffered by the public at large.
choices.C: Yes, because the child did not have an ownership interest in land.
choices.D: Yes, because the golfer's action was unintentional.

questions.explanation:
Public nuisance by private plaintiff
(special damage requirement)

Same harm ≠ special damage      Different harm = special damage

Public nuisance is an unreasonable interference with a right common to the general public, which requires proof that:

  • the defendant interfered with a public right—eg, affecting the public by polluting bodies of water—
  • and that interference was unreasonable—ie, it (1) significantly affected public health, safety, peace, or property rights or (2) violated an ordinance, statute, or administrative regulation.

Generally, only a public entity (ie, a state) can sue for public nuisance. However, a private individual can bring an action for public nuisance if that individual suffered special damage—ie, harm different from (not merely greater in extent or degree than) the harm sustained by the public at large.

Here, the company interfered with a public right by polluting the navigable body of water with golf balls from its course. This interference was unreasonable because it violated a local ordinance. But since the child is a private individual, his parents will prevail on a public nuisance claim on his behalf only if they can prove that his harm was different from the harm (pollution) sustained by the public. The parents can likely do so because the child was struck by a golf ball while sailing (a rare use of the water). Therefore, they are not precluded from recovery.

(Choice A) The attractive nuisance doctrine applies when a child trespasses on the defendant's property and is injured by an artificial condition on that property (not seen here).

(Choice C) Private nuisance requires proof that the defendant interfered with the plaintiff's use and enjoyment of property in which the plaintiff has an ownership interest. However, public nuisance (the claim asserted here) does not require that the plaintiff have an ownership interest.

(Choice D) The fact that the golfer unintentionally hit the golf ball toward the water is irrelevant to determining whether the parents may recover for public nuisance.

📌 Educational Objective

A private individual can prevail in an action for public nuisance—ie, an unreasonable interference with a public right—if that individual can show harm different from that suffered by the public at large (ie, special damage).

📚 References
  • Restatement (Second) of Torts § 821B (Am. Law Inst. 1977) (defining public nuisance).
  • Restatement (Second) of Torts § 821C (Am. Law Inst. 1977) (explaining that a private plaintiff must prove special damage).

questions.question:
During a deer-hunting season open to rifle hunters, a hunter saw a deer in the forest. He shot his rifle at the deer, hoping to hit and kill it. Instead, he hit and injured a hiker. The hunter had not realized that the hiker was there.
Does the injured hiker have an actionable battery claim against the hunter?

choices.A: No, because the hunter did not intend to shoot the hiker.
choices.B: No, because the hunter did not make direct physical contact with the hiker.
choices.C: Yes, because the bullet from the hunter's rifle made direct physical contact with the hiker.
choices.D: Yes, because the hunter intentionally shot the rifle.

在一个对步枪猎人开放的猎鹿季节，一名猎人在森林里看到了一只鹿。他向鹿开枪，希望能击中并杀死它。然而，他却击中并伤害了一名徒步者。猎人并未意识到徒步者在那里。

受伤的徒步者是否可以对猎人提起可诉的殴击之诉（actionable battery claim）？

zh-choices.A: 不可以，因为猎人无意射击徒步者。
zh-choices.B: 不可以，因为猎人没有与徒步者发生直接的身体接触。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析：殴击与意图

本题考察的是侵权法（Torts）中殴击（Battery）的核心构成要件，特别是对意图（Intent）的界定。

法律规则 (Rule of Law):
殴击的成立必须具备以下要素：
  1. 被告实施了故意行为 (Intentional Act)；
  2. 该行为导致了对原告的伤害性或冒犯性接触 (Harmful or Offensive Contact)；
  3. 被告具备特定的意图 (Intent)。

为什么选 A？逻辑推演

正确答案是 A。核心在于猎人缺乏构成殴击所需的法律意图。

1. 意图的双重标准

在侵权法中，意图 (Intent) 不仅仅是“想要做某动作”（如扣动扳机），而是指：

  • 目的 (Purpose): 被告渴望造成接触；或者
  • 认知 (Knowledge): 被告明知 (Substantially Certain) 接触将会发生。

2. 案件事实应用

1
目的测试：猎人的目的是击中鹿，而不是徒步者。
2
认知测试：题目明确指出猎人“并未意识到徒步者在那里”。因此，他不可能“明知”开枪会击中人。

3. 结论

虽然发生了伤害性接触（子弹击中人），但由于缺乏针对人的意图，殴击不成立。这可能构成过失 (Negligence)，但不是故意侵权。

陷阱选项分析

选项 B：间接接触 (Indirect Contact)

错误原因： 法律并不要求“皮肤对皮肤”的直接接触。通过物体（如子弹、陷阱、投毒）造成的间接接触同样可以构成殴击。选项 B 的法律陈述本身是错误的。

选项 C：结果责任 (Strict Liability?)

错误原因： 仅有接触是不够的。殴击是故意侵权 (Intentional Tort)，不是严格责任。必须证明被告有意造成这种接触。

选项 D：动作意图 vs. 结果意图

错误原因：这是最大的陷阱。 猎人确实是“故意”扣动扳机的（Volitional Act）。但是，殴击要求的意图是针对后果的意图（即意图造成接触），而不仅仅是针对动作本身的意图。

reason.en: Shows the hunter acted deliberately, but not necessarily toward the hiker.
reason.zh: 表明猎人系故意行为，但未必针对徒步者。

reason.en: The hunter's purpose was to strike the deer, not the hiker.
reason.zh: 猎人目的是击中鹿，而非徒步者。

reason.en: Contact and injury occurred, but intent toward this person still must be shown.
reason.zh: 已发生接触与伤害，但仍须证明针对该人的意图。

keywords.text: had not realized that the hiker was there

reason.en: Negates intent to shoot or harm this specific person.
reason.zh: 否定针对该特定人士开枪或伤害的意图。

reason.en: Frames whether all battery elements, especially intent, are satisfied.
reason.zh: 界定是否满足殴打各项要件，尤其是意图。

A.text: did not intend to shoot the hiker

reason.en: States the correct missing element: no intent toward the injured person.
reason.zh: 指出正确缺失要件：无意针对受伤者。

B.text: did not make direct physical contact

reason.en: Misstates battery law by requiring direct bodily contact by the defendant.
reason.zh: 误认殴打须被告本人直接身体接触。

C.text: bullet from the hunter's rifle made direct physical contact

reason.en: Contact alone is insufficient without intent to harm this plaintiff.
reason.zh: 仅有接触不足，尚须伤害该原告的意图。

reason.en: Swaps intent to fire at a deer with intent required for battery against the hiker.
reason.zh: 将对鹿开枪的故意混同为针对徒步者的殴打故意。

highlights.text: He shot his rifle at the deer, hoping to hit and kill it.

reason.en: Shows deliberate action aimed at the deer, not the injured hiker.
reason.zh: 表明故意行为针对鹿，而非受伤徒步者。

highlights.text: Instead, he hit and injured a hiker.

reason.en: Establishes contact and injury but does not alone prove battery intent.
reason.zh: 证明有接触与伤害，但本身不足以证明殴打意图。

highlights.text: The hunter had not realized that the hiker was there.

reason.en: This fact defeats intent to cause harmful contact with the hiker.
reason.zh: 该事实否定对徒步者造成有害接触的意图。

highlights.text: Does the injured hiker have an actionable battery claim against the hunter?

reason.en: The question turns on whether battery's intent element is met.
reason.zh: 问题核心在于是否满足殴打的意图要件。

questions.subject: Torts
questions.question:
A mother and her six-year-old child were on a walk when the mother stopped to talk with an elderly neighbor. Because the child resented having his mother's attention diverted by the neighbor, the child angrily threw himself against the neighbor and knocked her to the ground. The neighbor suffered a broken wrist as a result of the fall.
In an action for battery by the neighbor against the child, what is the strongest argument for liability?

choices.A: The child intended to throw himself against the neighbor.
choices.B: The child was not justified in his anger.
choices.C: The child was old enough to appreciate that causing a fall could inflict serious injury.
choices.D: The child was old enough to appreciate the riskiness of his conduct.

questions.explanation:
Tort liability of minor children
Intentional tort Liable if child was capable of forming requisite intent
Negligence Liable if child failed to act as reasonable child of similar age, intelligence, & experience would have acted under similar circumstances

Battery requires that:

  • the defendant intended to cause contact with the plaintiff's person
  • the defendant's affirmative conduct caused such contact and
  • that contact caused bodily harm or was offensive to the plaintiff.

Age is not a defense to intentional tort liability. Instead, a child's level of maturity is considered when determining whether the child is capable of forming the requisite intent. So though a child's ability to appreciate the riskiness or consequences of his/her conduct is important to this inquiry, the ultimate question is whether the child acted with the requisite intent (Choices C & D). Therefore, the strongest argument for liability is that the child intended to throw himself against the neighbor.

(Choice B) Although justification (e.g., consent, self-defense) is a defense to battery, anger is never a valid justification.

📌 Educational Objective

Battery requires the intent to cause contact with the plaintiff's person. If a child is capable of forming that intent, then the child may be held liable for battery.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Third) of Torts: Intentional Torts to Persons § 102 cmt. a (Am. L. Inst., Tentative Draft No. 1, 2015) (discussing a child's ability to form the requisite intent for battery).
questions.zh-question:
一位母亲和她六岁的孩子正在散步，母亲停下来与一位年长的邻居交谈。由于孩子不满母亲的注意力被邻居分散，他愤怒地撞向邻居，将她撞倒在地。邻居因此次摔倒而手腕骨折。

在邻居对该儿童提起的伤害罪（battery）诉讼中，支持其承担责任的最有力论据是什么？

zh-choices.A: 该儿童意图撞向邻居。
zh-choices.B: 该儿童的愤怒没有正当理由。
zh-choices.C: 该儿童的年龄足以认识到导致他人摔倒可能会造成严重伤害。
zh-choices.D: 该儿童的年龄足以认识到其行为的风险性。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Intentional Torts (Battery)

核心法律规则

Battery (非法侵犯/殴打) 的构成要件：

  • 被告实施了意图造成有害或冒犯性接触的行为 (Intent to cause harmful or offensive contact)；
  • 该行为确实导致了此类接触。

关键点：对于故意侵权行为，年龄不是抗辩理由。只要儿童具备形成特定意图 (Specific Intent) 的能力，即应对其行为负责。

✅ 正确答案：A (该儿童意图撞向邻居)

法律推理：

这是本题最强的论据，因为它直接确立了 Battery 的核心要素——意图 (Intent)。

在侵权法中，要构成 Battery，原告只需证明被告意图进行接触 (Contact)，而不需要证明被告意图造成具体的伤害 (Injury)（如骨折）。

只要这个6岁的孩子在主观上想要“撞向”邻居（即意图产生身体接触），并且这种接触在法律上被视为有害或冒犯性的，他就构成了 Battery。至于他是否预见到邻居会摔倒骨折，并不影响 Battery 的成立。

⚖️ 经典判例关联

Garratt v. Dailey (1955)

这是美国法学院侵权法课必学的经典案例。案中一名5岁儿童抽走了阿姨身后的椅子，导致阿姨摔伤。法院裁定，只要该儿童知道其行为（抽椅子）会导致阿姨摔倒（即产生接触），即便他没有恶意伤害阿姨的动机，也构成 Battery。

为什么其他选项是错误的？

❌ 选项 C 和 D (关于认识到伤害或风险)
这两个选项描述的是过失 (Negligence) 的标准，即“预见性” (Foreseeability)。
在故意侵权 (Intentional Torts) 中，我们不关心被告是否“欣赏”风险或后果的严重性。我们只关心他是否故意实施了那个导致接触的行为。混淆“故意”与“过失”是 MBE 常见的陷阱。

❌ 选项 B (愤怒没有正当理由)
这是关于动机 (Motive) 的描述。恶意的动机有助于证明意图，但不是必要条件；同样，缺乏正当理由并不能直接确立侵权责任的构成要件。

🎓 MBE 考试技巧

当题目涉及儿童 (Minors) 和故意侵权 (Intentional Torts) 时：

  1. 不要因为年龄小就认为无责任。
  2. 寻找描述“意图进行接触”的选项。
  3. 警惕那些谈论“理解后果”、“预见风险”或“像合理儿童那样行事”的选项——这些通常是过失 (Negligence) 的考点，而非 Battery。

reason.en: The claim requires proving intent to cause harmful or offensive contact.
reason.zh: 该诉因须证明行为人意图造成有害或冒犯性接触。

reason.en: Age affects whether the child could form requisite intent, not negligence alone.
reason.zh: 年龄影响未成年人能否形成所需故意，而非仅适用过失标准。

reason.en: Shows affirmative conduct directed at causing contact with the plaintiff.
reason.zh: 表明积极行为旨在与原告发生接触。

reason.en: Confirms the contact caused bodily impact from the defendant's act.
reason.zh: 确认接触由被告行为造成身体撞击。

reason.en: Satisfies the bodily harm element of battery.
reason.zh: 满足殴打侵权的身体伤害要件。

reason.en: Directs selection of the strongest legal basis, not merely any plausible theory.
reason.zh: 要求选择最强法律依据，而非任一可能理由。

A.text: intended to throw himself against the neighbor

reason.en: States the core intentional tort element supporting battery liability.
reason.zh: 陈述支持殴打责任的核心故意要件。

reason.en: Anger is not a defense; this misframes the inquiry as justification.
reason.zh: 愤怒不能作为抗辩；此选项误将争点引向正当化。

C.text: old enough to appreciate that causing a fall could inflict serious injury

reason.en: Focuses on appreciating consequences, which is a negligence inquiry, not battery intent.
reason.zh: 关注后果认知，属于过失判断而非殴打故意。

D.text: old enough to appreciate the riskiness of his conduct

reason.en: Risk appreciation alone does not establish intent to cause contact.
reason.zh: 仅认知风险不足以证明意图造成接触。

highlights.text: In an action for battery by the neighbor against the child

reason.en: Frames the dispute as intentional tort battery, not negligence.
reason.zh: 将争点框定为故意侵权中的殴打，而非过失。

highlights.text: six-year-old child

reason.en: Triggers analysis of whether the child could form requisite intent.
reason.zh: 引发未成年人能否形成所需故意的分析。

highlights.text: the child angrily threw himself against the neighbor and knocked her to the ground

reason.en: The deliberate act of throwing himself establishes contact directed at the neighbor.
reason.zh: 故意扑向邻居的行为表明针对原告的接触。

highlights.text: what is the strongest argument for liability?

reason.en: Requires choosing intent over weaker or inapplicable theories.
reason.zh: 要求选择故意理论，而非较弱或不适用理由。

highlights.text: The neighbor suffered a broken wrist as a result of the fall.

reason.en: Confirms battery caused actionable bodily harm.
reason.zh: 确认殴打造成可诉的身体伤害。

questions.subject: Torts
questions.question:
A restaurant building was expanded into a vacant lot north of its original location. The contractor who was working on the restaurant expansion found that the north wall of the enlarged structure needed extensive support, so anchor rods and concrete were added. The supporting anchor rods and concrete extended into a neighboring property farther to the north at a point 20 feet below the surface.
Although the anchor rods and concrete did not impact the surface of his land or its existing uses, the owner of the neighboring property has sued the restaurant owner for trespass.
Which party is likely to prevail?

choices.A: The neighboring property owner, because he should have been given notice of the intrusion before it occurred.
choices.B: The neighboring property owner, because the restaurant intruded upon his property without his permission.
choices.C: The restaurant owner, because the decision to provide the additional support was reasonable.
choices.D: The restaurant owner, because the anchor rods and concrete did not disturb the neighboring property owner's peaceful enjoyment of his land.

questions.explanation:
Ways of committing trespass

Trespass is the intentional entry onto another's property without permission. The entry can occur on, beneath, or above the property.

Here, the restaurant installed supporting anchor rods and concrete that entered the neighboring property 20 feet below the surface. Since the neighboring property owner did not consent to the sub-surface entry, he will likely prevail on his trespass claim.

(Choice A) Even if the neighboring property owner had been given prior notice, he would prevail on his trespass claim if he did not consent to the intrusion.

(Choice C) The reasonableness of the decision to provide additional support may show that the restaurant owner was not negligent—eg, he used reasonable care to prevent injury to the adjacent landowner. But reasonableness is irrelevant to trespass, which requires intentional conduct.

(Choice D) Disturbance of peaceful enjoyment of the neighboring property is relevant to an action for private nuisance (a substantial and unreasonable interference with another's use or enjoyment of land)—not trespass.

📌 Educational Objective

Trespass (an intentional entry onto another's property without permission) can occur on, beneath, or above the surface.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Second) of Torts § 158 (Am. Law Inst.1965) (intentional trespass).
  • Restatement (Second) of Torts § 159 (Am. Law Inst. 1965) (trespass on, beneath, and above the surface).
questions.zh-question:
一家餐厅扩建至其原址北侧的一块空地。负责餐厅扩建的承包商发现，扩建后结构的北墙需要大量支撑，因此增加了锚杆和混凝土。这些支撑用的锚杆和混凝土延伸至更北边的邻近地块，在地表下20英尺深处。

尽管这些锚杆和混凝土并未影响其土地表面或现有用途，但该邻近地块的业主已就非法侵入（trespass）起诉餐厅业主。

哪一方可能会胜诉？

zh-choices.A: 邻近地块的业主，因为在入侵发生前，他本应收到通知。
zh-choices.B: 邻近地块的业主，因为餐厅未经其许可侵入了他的地产。
zh-choices.C: 餐厅业主，因为提供额外支撑的决定是合理的。
zh-choices.D: 餐厅业主，因为锚杆和混凝土并未干扰邻近地块业主对其土地的安宁享用。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Torts: Trespass to Land (Subsurface)
地表 (Surface)
餐厅
Restaurant
邻居
Neighbor
核心法律规则 (The Rule)

土地非法侵入 (Trespass to Land) 的定义是：

被告未经许可，故意 (Intentionally) 进入或导致物体进入他人的土地。

这种“进入”不仅限于地表，还包括：

  • 地表之上 (Above the surface)
  • 地表之下 (Beneath the surface)
本题解析 (Analysis)

本题的正确答案是 B。

1. 物理侵入 (Physical Invasion)：
餐厅的锚杆和混凝土延伸到了邻居地界内地下20英尺处。根据普通法原则，土地所有权延伸至地下（ad inferos）。虽然现代法律对高空飞行有豁免，但对于地下结构（如地基、管道、锚杆），只要在土地所有者可以利用的深度内，均视为该土地的一部分。

2. 故意性 (Intent)：
Trespass 是一种故意侵权 (Intentional Tort)。这里的“故意”指的是被告有意实施了“放置锚杆”这一行为，并不要求被告知道这是违法的或知道越界了。只要物体进入了邻居的土地，且没有得到许可，就构成了 Trespass。

3. 损害非必要 (No Harm Required)：
这是本题最大的陷阱。Trespass 是 actionable per se（本身即构成诉因），原告不需要证明实际损害。即使锚杆没有破坏地表，也没有影响邻居目前的土地使用，邻居依然可以胜诉。

为什么其他选项是错的？

❌ 选项 C (Reasonableness/Negligence)：
“合理性”是过失侵权 (Negligence) 的抗辩理由。但在 Trespass 中，无论被告多么小心、多么合理，只要未经许可越界，就是侵权。Strict liability applies to the boundary.

❌ 选项 D (Peaceful Enjoyment/Nuisance)：
“干扰安宁享用”是私人妨害 (Private Nuisance) 的要素。Nuisance 处理的是非物理性的干扰（如噪音、气味）。本题中有具体的物体（锚杆）进入，属于物理侵入，适用 Trespass，不看是否干扰了享用。

💡 MBE 考试技巧

在处理 Trespass to Land 的题目时，切记：
1. 不要寻找损害 (Damages)：只要脚踩过界或物体越界，哪怕只是一寸，哪怕没有造成任何经济损失，原告也能赢。
2. 区分 Nuisance 和 Trespass：
• 有实体物体进入 = Trespass
• 无形干扰 (光、声、味) = Nuisance

reason.zh: 证明故意在邻地地下实施物理侵入。

reason.en: Frames the dispute as intentional trespass, not nuisance or negligence.

questions.subject: Torts
questions.question:
A homeowner's next-door neighbor went into the homeowner's garage without permission and borrowed the homeowner's chain saw. The neighbor used the saw to clear broken branches from the trees on his property. After he had finished, the neighbor noticed several broken branches on the homeowner's trees that were in danger of falling on the homeowner's roof. While the neighbor was cutting the homeowner's branches, the saw broke.
In a suit for conversion by the homeowner against the neighbor, will the homeowner recover?

choices.A: No, because the neighbor did not intend to keep the saw.
choices.B: No, because the neighbor was using the saw to benefit the homeowner when it broke.
choices.C: Yes, for the actual damage to the saw.
choices.D: Yes, for the value of the saw when the neighbor borrowed it.

questions.explanation:
Explanation

Trespass to chattels
  • Minor intentional interference with plaintiff's right to control chattel
  • Liable for actual damages—eg, cost of repairs, loss of use
Conversion
  • Substantial intentional interference with plaintiff's right to control chattel
  • Liable for fair market value of chattel at time of conversion

For conversion, the plaintiff must prove that:

  • the defendant intentionally exerted dominion or control over the plaintiff's chattel and
  • the interference was so severe that the plaintiff should recover the fair market value of the chattel at the time of the conversion.

Here, the neighbor converted the homeowner's saw when he borrowed it without permission and used it to clear broken tree branches on his property. Since the neighbor then broke the saw, the homeowner should recover the fair market value of the saw at the time the neighbor borrowed it—the time of conversion.

(Choice A) Even though the neighbor did not intend to keep the saw, he is liable for conversion because he borrowed the saw without the homeowner's permission and broke it.

(Choice B) A defendant who uses the plaintiff's chattel without permission may be liable for conversion even if he/she acts with the intent to benefit the plaintiff (here, cutting the homeowner's tree branches).

(Choice C) Since the remedy for conversion is the fair market value of the chattel, the homeowner can recover the entire value of the saw—not just the actual damage to the saw (eg, repair costs). In contrast, the remedy for trespass to chattels is limited to actual damage.

📌 Educational Objective

Conversion is an intentional exertion of dominion or control over chattel that so seriously interferes with the owner's right of control that the owner should recover the fair market value of the chattel at the time of the conversion.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Second) of Torts § 222A (Am. Law Inst. 1965) (conversion).
  • Restatement (Second) of Torts § 227 (Am. Law Inst. 1965) (conversion by using chattel).
questions.zh-question:
一名房主的隔壁邻居未经许可进入房主的车库，并借用了房主的链锯。该邻居使用链锯清理了自己地产上树木的断枝。完成后，邻居注意到房主的树上有几根断枝，有掉落到房主屋顶的危险。当邻居正在砍伐房主的树枝时，链锯坏了。

在房主对邻居提起的侵占动产之诉中，房主能否胜诉？

zh-choices.A: 不会，因为邻居无意永久占有该链锯。
zh-choices.B: 不会，因为当链锯损坏时，邻居正在使用它为房主谋利。
zh-choices.C: 会，就链锯的实际损害获得赔偿。
zh-choices.D: 会，就邻居借用链锯时的价值获得赔偿。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Intentional Torts: Conversion

核心考点：侵占动产 vs. 侵犯动产

本题考察的是对动产干扰程度的区分。在普通法中，根据干扰的严重程度，分为两种侵权行为：

比较维度 侵犯动产
(Trespass to Chattels)		 侵占动产
(Conversion)
干扰程度 轻微干扰 (Minor interference) 严重干扰，行使支配权 (Substantial dominion & control)
法律后果 赔偿实际损失 强制出售 (Forced Sale)
赔偿金额 维修费或价值减损额 (Actual damages) 侵占时的公平市价 (FMV at time of conversion)
案情法律分析

本案中，邻居未经许可拿走链锯（Intentional interference），并且在使用过程中导致链锯损坏 (Saw broke)。

根据 Restatement (Second) of Torts § 222A，当动产被完全损坏或严重损毁时，这种干扰极其严重，足以构成侵占动产 (Conversion)。

法律逻辑是：既然你像主人一样行使权利并把它弄坏了，法律就强制你把它“买下来”。

选项深度解析
正确 D 会，就邻居借用链锯时的价值获得赔偿。

这是 Conversion 的标准赔偿原则。一旦构成侵占，被告必须支付该物品在侵占发生时（即邻居拿走链锯时）的公平市价 (Fair Market Value)。这相当于被告强行买下了这个链锯。
错误 A 关于意图 (Intent)。
Conversion 是故意侵权，但这里的“故意”仅指故意实施了干扰行为（拿走锯子），并不要求被告有“偷窃”或“永久占有”的恶意。邻居故意拿走了锯子，这就满足了 Intent 的要件。
错误 B 关于动机 (Motive)。
虽然邻居后来是为了帮房主修剪树枝（Good motive），但这不能免除 Conversion 的责任。未经许可的严重干扰（导致损坏）本身就是侵权，动机良好不是抗辩理由。
错误 C 关于赔偿范围。
这是最具迷惑性的选项。如果只是轻微刮擦，适用 Trespass to Chattels，赔偿实际修理费（选项C）。但本题中链锯坏了 (Broke)，属于严重干扰，适用 Conversion。Conversion 的赔偿是全额价值，而非仅仅是修理费。
🎓 MBE 提分技巧：
在动产侵权题中，看到物品"丢失" (Lost)、"被毁" (Destroyed) 或 "长时间未归还" (Long duration)，通常指向 Conversion，对应的赔偿永远是 Full Value (FMV)。

如果只是"划伤" (Scratched) 或 "短时间借用" (Brief use) 且归还了，通常是 Trespass to Chattels，赔偿是 Cost of Repair。

questions.subject: Torts
questions.question:
An avid baseball fan purchased a ticket to an afternoon game at great expense. The fan hoped to not only see his favorite team's powerhouse player break the all-time single-season home run record, but also catch the record-breaking baseball. The fan brought his baseball glove and positioned himself in a section of the ballpark where the greatest number of the player's home runs had landed.
In the ninth inning, with the bases loaded and a full count, the player swung, and the baseball sailed over the right-field fence and descended toward the large crowd gathered in the fan's section. The fan shouted, "It's mine!" just as the baseball made contact with tip of his glove, but a burly man reached for the ball at that same instant. In so doing, he propelled the baseball back onto the field, where it was retrieved by the opposing team's outfielder. The fan was unable to recover the baseball.
The fan has sued the man for trespass to chattels.
Is the fan likely to prevail?

choices.A: No, because the man did not dispossess the fan of the baseball.
choices.B: No, because the man did not intend to propel the baseball back onto the field.
choices.C: Yes, because the man deprived the fan of his immediate right to possession of the baseball.
choices.D: Yes, because the man intentionally intermeddled with the fan's personal property.

questions.explanation:
Trespass to chattels

Plaintiff has possession or immediate right to possession of chattel
Defendant intentionally interferes with possession through either:
Dispossession
Harm inferred
Use or intermeddling
Causes harm
  • actual harm to chattel
  • substantial loss of use of chattel or
  • bodily harm to plaintiff

OLWorld

Trespass to chattels is an intentional interference with another's right of possession in tangible personal property (i.e., chattel) through dispossession, use, or intermeddling. As a result, an action for trespass to chattels may be brought by anyone who had possession or the right to immediate possession of the chattel in question at the time of the interference.

Here, the fan sued the man for trespass to chattels after the man reached for the baseball and propelled it back onto the field. But the fan had not yet caught the baseball (no possession) and had no more right to possess it than any other person in the crowd ((Choice C)). Therefore, the man could not dispossess the fan of the baseball, and the fan is unlikely to prevail.

(Choice B) The intent required for trespass to chattels is the intent to do the interfering act - e.g., to reach out for the baseball. The defendant need not have intended to interfere with another's possession of tangible property - e.g., to propel the baseball back onto the field.

(Choice D) The man intermeddled (i.e., caused physical contact) with the baseball and deprived the fan of possessing and using it by propelling it back onto the field. But since the baseball was not the fan's personal property, his trespass-to-chattels claim will fail.

📌 Educational Objective

Anyone who had possession or the right to immediate possession of a chattel (i.e., tangible personal property) at the time of the interference may bring an action for trespass to chattels.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Second) of Torts §§ 216–17 (Am. Law Inst. 1981) (discussing possession of and trespass to chattel).

questions.zh-question:
一位狂热的棒球迷花大价钱购买了一张下午比赛的门票。这位球迷不仅希望看到他最喜欢的球队的强力击球手打破单赛季本垒打的历史记录，还希望能接住那颗破纪录的棒球。球迷带上了他的棒球手套，并占据了球场中该球员击出本垒打落点最多的一个区域。

在第九局，满垒满球数的情况下，该球员挥棒击球，棒球飞越右外野的围栏，朝着聚集在该球迷所在区域的大批观众飞去。就在棒球接触到他手套掌心的那一刻，球迷大喊：“这是我的！”，但一个魁梧的男子也在同一瞬间伸手去抢球。在此过程中，他将棒球推回了场内，并被对方球队的外野手捡到。该球迷未能拿回棒球。

该球迷以非法侵占动产 (trespass to chattels) 为由起诉了该男子。

该球迷有可能胜诉吗？

zh-choices.A: 不会，因为该男子并未剥夺球迷对棒球的占有。
zh-choices.B: 不会，因为该男子并非有意将棒球推回场内。
zh-choices.C: 会，因为该男子剥夺了球迷对棒球的即时占有权。
zh-choices.D: 会，因为该男子故意干涉了球迷的个人财产。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Intentional Torts: Trespass to Chattels

⚖️ 核心法律规则

要赢得非法侵占动产 (Trespass to Chattels) 的诉讼，原告必须证明以下几点：

  1. Intent (意图)：被告有意实施了干涉行为。
  2. Interference (干涉)：被告干涉了原告对动产的占有权（通过剥夺占有、使用或造成损害）。
  3. Plaintiff's Possession (原告的占有)：在干涉发生时，原告必须拥有该动产的占有权 (Possession) 或 即时占有权 (Right to Immediate Possession)。

💡 关键点：如果原告从未真正“拥有”该物品，那么被告的行为就不构成对原告财产的侵权。

🔍 案情深度解析

本题的核心在于“谁拥有那个棒球？”

1
棒球的性质：
飞入看台的棒球被视为无主物（类似于野生动物，ferae naturae），直到有人对其建立完全的控制 (Complete Control)。
2
球迷的状态：
球迷虽然手套碰到了球，并大喊“是我的”，但他并未完成抓取动作，也没有确立对球的排他性控制。
3
结论：
因为球迷从未获得对棒球的占有 (Possession)，这颗球在法律上还不是他的“动产” (Chattel)。既然球不是他的，被告（那个魁梧男子）就没有侵犯球迷的财产权利。

✅ 为什么选 A？

选项 A 正确。

"No, because the man did not dispossess the fan of the baseball."

这里的逻辑是：你不能失去你从未拥有的东西。

非法侵占动产中的“剥夺占有” (Dispossession) 前提是原告已经占有了该物。由于球迷在法律上从未完成对棒球的占有，被告的行为虽然导致球飞回场内，但并未构成对球迷动产的“剥夺”。

❌ 为什么其他选项是错的？

  • 选项 B (Intent): 错误。侵权法中的意图是指“有意做那个动作” (intent to do the act)，即伸手去抢球。被告不需要有意图去“造成损害”或“把球推回场内”。只要他有意伸手，意图要件就满足了。
  • 选项 C (Right to Possession): 错误。球迷买票进场并不赋予他拥有飞入该区域棒球的“权利”。在接住球之前，他和在场的任何人权利平等。
  • 选项 D (Intermeddling): 错误。虽然被告确实“干涉” (Intermeddled) 了棒球的运动轨迹，但这个侵权行为必须是针对原告的个人财产。既然球不是原告的，这个主张就不成立。

🎓 MBE 考试技巧

在处理财产侵权 (Property Torts) 题目时（如 Trespass to Chattels, Conversion, Trespass to Land），请遵循以下步骤：

  1. 第一步：确认原告的权利。 原告是否真的拥有该财产，或者拥有合法的占有权？如果原告没有权利，侵权诉讼直接失败（如本题）。
  2. 第二步：分析意图。 被告是否有意实施了该物理行为？（不需要恶意）。
  3. 第三步：分析损害。 动产侵权通常需要证明实际损害（Actual Damages）或剥夺占有。

⚠️ 陷阱提示： 不要被题目中描述的“失望”、“大喊”或“几乎得到”等情绪化细节干扰。法律看重的是实际控制 (Actual Control)。

questions.subject: Torts
questions.question:
A man built a garage in his backyard that encroached two feet across the property line onto property owned by his neighbor. Thereafter, the man sold his property to a buyer. Prior to the man's sale to the buyer, the man and the neighbor were unaware that the garage encroached onto the neighbor's property.
The neighbor later learned of the encroachment and she sued the man for damages for trespass.
In this action, will the neighbor prevail?

choices.A: No, because the man no longer owns or possesses the garage.
choices.B: No, because the man was unaware of the encroachment when the garage was built.
choices.C: Yes, because the man knew where the garage was located, whether or not he knew where the property line was.
choices.D: Yes, unless the buyer was aware of the encroachment when he purchased the property.

questions.explanation:
Explanation
Trespass to land

Requires proof that:

  • defendant intentionally entered land in question and
  • plaintiff did not consent to entry

For trespass to land (ie, trespass quare clausum fregit), a defendant must intentionally enter or cause something to enter the land in question. If the plaintiff did not consent to the defendant's intentional entry, then the defendant is liable for trespass. It does not matter whether the defendant knew that the property belonged to the plaintiff or believed that the entry was permissible.

Here, the man built a garage that encroached across the neighbor's property line. Although the man did not know that the garage was on his neighbor's property, he still intended for it to be on the land in question. And since the neighbor did not consent to that entry, the man is liable for trespass.

(Choice A) If the defendant intentionally causes an object to enter and remain on the plaintiff's property, the defendant is liable for its continued trespass even after the defendant transfers his/her legal interest in the object to another. Since the man intentionally built his garage on the land in question, he is liable for its continued trespass even though he no longer owns it.

(Choice B) Trespass requires that the defendant intend to be (or cause something to be) on the property in question, but the defendant need not know that the property belongs to the plaintiff. Therefore, it does not matter whether the man knew that the garage encroached onto the neighbor's property when it was built.

(Choice D) A person who purchases property that encroaches onto the land of another is liable for trespass if he/she knows about the trespass and fails to remedy it. However, the sale does not absolve the seller of liability for trespass. Therefore, the man is liable for trespass even if the buyer was aware of the garage's encroachment.

📌 Educational Objective

Trespass to land requires the intent to enter the land in question, but does not also require that the defendant know that the property belongs to the plaintiff.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Second) of Torts § 158 (Am. Law Inst. 1965) (definition of trespass to land).
  • Restatement (Second) of Torts § 164 (Am. Law Inst. 1965) (trespass to land by mistake).
questions.zh-question:
一名男子在其后院建造了一个车库，该车库侵占了邻居的地产，越过地界线两英尺。

此后，该男子将其地产出售给了一位买家。在该男子将地产出售给买家之前，他与邻居都不知道车库侵占了邻居的地产。

邻居后来得知了侵占事实，并以侵犯地产（trespass）为由起诉该男子，要求损害赔偿。

在此诉讼中，邻居会胜诉吗？

zh-choices.A: 不会，因为该男子已不再拥有或占有该车库。
zh-choices.B: 不会，因为该男子在建造车库时并不知道存在侵占行为。
zh-choices.C: 会，因为该男子知道车库的位置，无论他是否知道地界线的位置。
zh-choices.D: 会，除非买家在购买该地产时已经意识到侵占的存在。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Intentional Torts: Trespass to Land
核心法则：意图 (Intent) 的界定

在侵犯地产（Trespass to Land）中，被告必须具有进入该特定土地的意图。

关键点：被告不需要知道这块地属于别人。即使被告真诚地误以为这块地是自己的（Mistake），只要他是有意识地踏上或在上面建造物体，就构成了侵权。

本案逻辑推演

本题考察的是对“意图”这一要素的精确理解。

✔ 为什么选 C (Correct Answer)

事实：男子建造车库时，是有意识地将砖块、木材放置在那个具体的物理位置上。

法律分析：这种“放置”的行为是故意的（Volitional act）。虽然他不知道那是邻居的地（Mistake of fact），但这不影响侵权责任的成立。法律保护土地所有者的排他性占有权。

引用：Restatement (Second) of Torts § 164 明确指出，进入他人土地的错误（Mistake）不能作为抗辩理由。

为什么其他选项是错的？

✘ 选项 A：男子已卖掉房产

解析：这是关于“持续性侵权”（Continuing Trespass）的考点。虽然男子不再拥有车库，但他最初的建造行为导致了侵权状态的产生。只要该物体还在邻居地上，作为始作俑者，他仍需对最初的侵入及造成的损害负责。

✘ 选项 B：男子不知道越界

解析：这是MBE最常见的陷阱。如前所述，善意（Good faith）不是抗辩理由。只要他意图进入那个空间，就是 Trespass。

✘ 选项 D：除非买家知情

解析：买家是否知情可能会影响买家自己的责任（如果买家知情而不移除，买家也构成侵权），但这并不能免除卖方（建造者）对自己原始侵权行为的责任。

在处理 Intentional Torts 题目时，区分以下两种意图：

  1. Intent to act: 意图做这个动作（如：走路、挥手、盖房）。
  2. Intent to harm: 意图造成伤害或侵犯权利。

对于 Trespass to Land，只需要第 1 种意图（Intent to be on the land）。不要被“他以为那是他自己的地”这种借口迷惑。

MBE 法律知识点解析 | Torts

questions.subject: Torts
questions.question:
A car driven by the defendant entered land owned by and in the possession of the plaintiff, without her permission.
Which of the following allegations, without additional facts, would provide a sufficient basis for a trespass claim by the plaintiff against the defendant?

choices.A: The defendant knew that the land was the plaintiff's private property.
choices.B: The defendant negligently drove his car onto the plaintiff's land.
choices.C: The defendant purposely drove his car onto the plaintiff's land.
choices.D: The defendant's car damaged the plaintiff's land.

questions.explanation:
Types of trespass to land
Conduct Consent Harm
Intentional Intentional entry onto plaintiff's land Without plaintiff's consent (No harm required)
Reckless Reckless entry onto plaintiff's land Without plaintiff's consent Causing harm to land or plaintiff
Negligent Negligent entry onto plaintiff's land Without plaintiff's consent Causing harm to land or plaintiff

For an intentional trespass, a defendant must act with the intent to enter the plaintiff's land, which is either (1) the purpose to enter the plaintiff's land or (2) the knowledge that the entry is substantially certain to occur. If the plaintiff does not consent to the defendant's intentional entry, then the defendant is liable for intentional trespass.

Here, the plaintiff did not give the defendant permission to enter her land. Therefore, the plaintiff can prevail on an intentional trespass claim if she can show that the defendant drove his car with the purpose to enter the plaintiff's land (or knowledge that the entry was substantially certain to occur).

(Choice A) The fact that the defendant knew that the land was the plaintiff's private property has no bearing on the defendant's tortious conduct—the intentional, reckless, or negligent entry onto the plaintiff's land—and is therefore irrelevant to a trespass claim.

(Choices B & D) A defendant is liable for negligent or reckless trespass when the plaintiff does not consent to the defendant's negligent or reckless entry AND the entry causes actual harm to the land or the plaintiff. Here, the defendant entered the plaintiff's land without permission. However, neither (1) the fact that the defendant drove negligently (or recklessly) nor (2) the fact that the defendant's car damaged the plaintiff's land can—on its own—support a claim for trespass. Both allegations are required.

📌 Educational Objective

A defendant who intentionally enters the plaintiff's land without permission is liable for intentional trespass, even if the entry does not harm the land or the plaintiff. In contrast, a defendant whose entry results from negligent or reckless conduct is only liable for trespass if he/she causes actual damages.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Second) of Torts § 158 (Am. Law Inst. 1965) (intentional trespass).
  • Restatement (Second) of Torts § 165 (Am. Law Inst. 1965) (reckless or negligent trespass).
questions.zh-question:
一辆由被告驾驶的汽车，在未经原告许可的情况下，进入了原告拥有并占有的土地。

在没有其他事实的情况下，下列哪项指控为原告向被告提起的非法侵入之诉提供了充分的依据？

zh-choices.A: 被告知晓该土地是原告的私人财产。
zh-choices.B: 被告因过失将其汽车驶入原告的土地。
zh-choices.C: 被告故意将其汽车驶入原告的土地。
zh-choices.D: 被告的汽车损坏了原告的土地。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

非法侵入土地 (Trespass to Land)
⚖️ 核心法律规则 (The Rule)

故意非法侵入 (Intentional Trespass) 的构成要件不需要证明实际损害 (Actual Damages)。只要被告故意进入了原告的土地，无论是否造成破坏，原告均可起诉。

相反，如果是过失 (Negligence) 或鲁莽 (Recklessness) 导致的侵入，原告必须证明存在实际损害才能胜诉。

为何选项 C 是正确答案？
选项 C 被告故意将其汽车驶入原告的土地。

法律依据： 在普通法下，非法侵入土地 (Trespass to Land) 是一种故意侵权 (Intentional Tort)。其核心要素是：
  1. 意图 (Intent)： 被告有进入该特定土地的目的 (Purpose)，或者明知进入是基本确定的 (Substantially Certain)。
  2. 物理侵入 (Physical Invasion)： 实际进入了土地。

推理逻辑： 题目问的是哪项指控能“单独”提供充分依据。选项 C 指出被告是“故意” (Purposely) 驶入的。

一旦确立了“故意侵入”，法律就假定存在损害（即所谓的 Actionable per se，无需证明实际损害）。即使车轮没有压坏一根草，原告也有权获得名义损害赔偿 (Nominal Damages) 以维护其财产权。因此，仅凭“故意进入”这一事实，就足以构成诉因。
为何其他选项不足以构成诉因？
选项 B & D 过失 (Negligence) 与 损害 (Damages) 的分离

分析： 这两个选项展示了 MBE 常见的陷阱——将构成要件拆分。
  • 选项 B (过失)： 仅有过失行为是不够的。对于过失侵入 (Negligent Trespass)，法律要求必须造成实际损害 (Actual Harm) 才能索赔。选项 B 没提损害，所以不充分。
  • 选项 D (损害)： 仅有损害也是不够的。侵权法通常不实行严格责任 (Strict Liability)。如果被告既没有故意，也没有过失（例如因不可抗力被风刮进去），即使造成了损害，通常也不承担非法侵入责任。
结论： B 和 D 必须结合在一起（过失 + 损害）才能构成有效的索赔依据，单独任何一个都不行。
选项 A 知晓土地所有权 (Knowledge of Title)

分析： 非法侵入的“意图”是指进入该物理空间的意图，而不是“侵犯他人权利”的意图。

即使被告诚实地误以为那是公共土地或自己的土地（Mistake of Fact），只要他是有意走到那块地上的，他就构成了非法侵入。因此，被告是否“知晓”这是原告的私产，对于是否构成侵权是无关紧要的。
侵入类型 (Type) 意图要求 (Intent) 损害要求 (Damages)
故意侵入
(Intentional)		 有目的进入 或 明知会进入 不需要 (No Harm Required)
过失/鲁莽侵入
(Negligent/Reckless)		 未尽注意义务 必须证明实际损害 (Actual Harm Required)
🎓 MBE 考试技巧 (Exam Tip)

在处理 Intentional Torts（如 Battery, Assault, Trespass）的题目时，请记住：
"The intent is to do the act, not to cause the harm."
（意图是指实施该行为的意图，而非造成伤害的意图。）

看到 "Trespass to Land" 时，立即检查：
1. 是故意进入吗？如果是 ➡️ 不需要损害。
2. 是意外/过失进入吗？如果是 ➡️ 必须找损害。

reason.en: Entry onto the plaintiff's land is the core act for any trespass theory.
reason.zh: 进入原告土地是任何非法侵入主张的核心行为。

reason.en: Nonconsensual entry is required for trespass liability.
reason.zh: 未经同意的进入是非法侵入责任的要件。

reason.en: Identifies the tort and its distinct element requirements.
reason.zh: 界定所测侵权类型及其不同构成要件。

reason.en: Each choice must alone establish liability without added facts.
reason.zh: 各选项须在无额外事实下单独成立责任。

reason.en: Tests whether one allegation completes the claim.
reason.zh: 检验单一指控能否单独完成诉因。

keywords.text: owned by and in the possession of the plaintiff

reason.en: Confirms the plaintiff has the property interest invaded.
reason.zh: 确认原告拥有被侵入的财产利益。

A.text: knew that the land was the plaintiff's private property

reason.en: Knowing ownership does not establish intent to enter.
reason.zh: 知悉权属并不构成进入意图。

reason.en: Negligent trespass also requires proof of actual harm.
reason.zh: 过失非法侵入还须证明实际损害。

reason.en: Purpose to enter satisfies the intent element for intentional trespass.
reason.zh: 故意进入满足故意非法侵入的意图要件。

reason.en: Damage alone cannot support trespass without a negligent or reckless entry allegation.
reason.zh: 仅有损害而无过失或轻率进入指控不足以成立非法侵入。

highlights.text: without her permission

reason.en: Lack of permission is a universal element for trespass liability.
reason.zh: 未经许可是非法侵入责任的共通要件。

highlights.text: without additional facts, would provide a sufficient basis

reason.en: Forces evaluation of whether each choice alone states every required element.
reason.zh: 要求判断各选项是否单独具备全部要件。

highlights.text: sufficient basis for a trespass claim

reason.en: Frames whether the pleaded conduct completes any trespass theory.
reason.zh: 界定所指控行为能否完成任一非法侵入理论。

highlights.text: entered land owned by and in the possession of the plaintiff

reason.en: Establishes the defendant's unauthorized physical invasion of protected land.
reason.zh: 确立被告未经授权物理侵入受保护土地的事实。

questions.subject: Torts
questions.question:
The plaintiff, a successful high-school student with a promising future and a well-paying tutoring job, joined a cult that requires its members to solicit new recruits and turn over 25% of their earnings. After the plaintiff's grades, demeanor, and overall appearance began to suffer, her parents brought her to a cult deprogrammer. After her stay at the deprogrammer's home, the plaintiff returned home a happier, healthier person and was able to raise her grades and resume her tutoring job.
Despite this progress, the plaintiff brought suit against the deprogrammer for false imprisonment. At trial, the deprogrammer acknowledged that the plaintiff went to the deprogrammer's home against her will but established that she had ample opportunity to leave or contact the police, which the plaintiff knew upon arrival.
Will the plaintiff likely succeed in an action for false imprisonment against the deprogrammer?

choices.A: No, because the plaintiff was not actually confined in the deprogrammer's home.
choices.B: No, because the plaintiff was not harmed by the confinement in the deprogrammer's home.
choices.C: Yes, because the deprogrammer intended to confine the plaintiff within the deprogrammer's home.
choices.D: Yes, because the deprogrammer unlawfully confined the plaintiff against her will.

questions.explanation:
Methods of confinement for false imprisonment
  • Physical barrier
  • Physical force or restraint (or threat thereof)
  • Duress
  • Assertion of legal authority
  • Refusal to release plaintiff

To succeed in an action for false imprisonment, the plaintiff must prove that:

  • the defendant intended to confine or restrain the plaintiff within a limited area
  • the defendant's conduct caused the plaintiff's confinement or the defendant failed to release the plaintiff from a confinement despite owing a duty to do so
  • the plaintiff was conscious of the confinement at the time it occurred and
  • the plaintiff did not consent to the confinement.

Confinement can occur through various methods (see table above), including the use of physical barriers that preclude the plaintiff from exiting a limited area. However, a plaintiff is not confined by physical barriers if the plaintiff knows of a readily available, feasible, and safe way to exit the confined area.

Here, the plaintiffs parents brought her to the home of a deprogrammer, who presumably intended to confine the plaintiff against her will in the deprogrammer's home. Although the deprogrammer's home was a physical barrier, the plaintiff had ample opportunity to leave the home or contact the police. And since the plaintiff knew of this readily available, feasible, and safe way to exit, she was not actually confined in the home (Choices C & D). Therefore, it is unlikely that the plaintiff will succeed in an action for false imprisonment against the deprogrammer.

(Choice B) In most jurisdictions, a plaintiff need not prove actual harm to succeed in a false imprisonment action. Instead, the plaintiff must show actual confinement (not seen here).

📌 Educational Objective

For false imprisonment, confinement can occur when a defendant uses physical barriers that preclude a plaintiff from exiting a limited area. However, a plaintiff is not confined by physical barriers if the plaintiff knows of a readily available, feasible, and safe way to exit a confined area.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Third) of Torts: Intentional Torts to Persons § 8 cmt. e (Am. L. Inst., Tentative Draft No. 3, 2018) (discussing that confinement by physical barriers does not result in liability if the plaintiff knows of a readily available, feasible, and safe way to exit a confined area).
questions.zh-question:
侵权法（Torts）— 故意侵权（Intentional Torts）

原告是一名成绩优异、前途光明且有一份收入可观的家教工作的高中生，后来加入了一个邪教组织。该组织要求成员招募新成员，并将其收入的 25% 上交。在原告的成绩、举止和整体外貌开始恶化后，她的父母把她送到一名邪教“去洗脑”人员（cult deprogrammer）那里。原告在该去洗脑人员家中待过一段时间后，回到家时变成了一个更快乐、更健康的人，并且能够提高成绩并恢复家教工作。

尽管如此，原告仍以 false imprisonment（非法监禁）为由起诉该去洗脑人员。审判中，该去洗脑人员承认原告是违背其意愿来到其家中的，但证明原告在到达时就知道自己有充分机会离开或联系警方。

原告在针对该去洗脑人员提起的 false imprisonment 诉讼中，最可能胜诉吗？

zh-choices.A: 否，因为原告并未被实际限制在该去洗脑人员的家中。
zh-choices.B: 否，因为原告并未因被限制在该去洗脑人员家中而受到损害。
zh-choices.C: 是，因为该去洗脑人员意图将原告限制在其家中。
zh-choices.D: 是，因为该去洗脑人员违背原告意愿非法限制了原告。

reason.en: The claim requires proof of unlawful confinement within a limited area.
reason.zh: 该诉因要求证明在有限区域内存在非法拘禁。

reason.en: Shows the plaintiff did not consent, but consent alone does not establish confinement.
reason.zh: 表明原告未同意，但仅此不足以构成拘禁。

reason.en: If the plaintiff knew of a feasible exit, physical barriers do not constitute confinement.
reason.zh: 若原告知晓可行出路，物理障碍不构成拘禁。

reason.en: Supports that a safe, practical way to end the confinement was available.
reason.zh: 说明存在安全、可行的方式结束所谓拘禁。

keywords.text: which the plaintiff knew upon arrival

label.zh: 到达时即知的离开途径

reason.en: Plaintiff's knowledge of the exit defeats the confinement element.
reason.zh: 原告知晓离开途径即否定拘禁要件。

reason.en: Identifies the limited area where alleged confinement occurred.
reason.zh: 界定所谓拘禁发生的有限区域。

reason.en: Correctly focuses on the missing element of actual confinement.
reason.zh: 正确聚焦于缺少实际拘禁这一要件。

reason.en: Distracts by implying harm is an element of false imprisonment.
reason.zh: 误导考生以为损害是非法拘禁的构成要件。

reason.en: Intent to confine does not satisfy the actual confinement requirement.
reason.zh: 拘禁意图本身不能满足实际拘禁要件。

reason.en: Assumes unlawful confinement without addressing the readily available exit exception.
reason.zh: 在未考虑可随时离开例外的情况下假定存在非法拘禁。

reason.en: Being present against one's will does not alone prove confinement by physical barrier.
reason.zh: 非自愿在场本身不足以证明因物理障碍而被拘禁。

highlights.text: false imprisonment

reason.en: Frames the tort and its confinement elements as the central issue.
reason.zh: 界定侵权类型及其拘禁要件为核心争点。

highlights.text: went to the deprogrammer's home against her will

reason.en: Establishes lack of consent but does not by itself prove confinement.
reason.zh: 表明缺乏同意，但本身不足以证明拘禁。

highlights.text: ample opportunity to leave or contact the police, which the plaintiff knew upon arrival

label.en: readily available exit known to plaintiff
label.zh: 原告知晓的可行离开途径

reason.en: This fact defeats confinement by physical barrier and controls the answer.
reason.zh: 该事实否定因物理障碍构成的拘禁，决定正确答案。

highlights.text: acknowledged that the plaintiff went to the deprogrammer's home against her will

reason.en: Tempts selection of intent-based answers while actual confinement is still missing.
reason.zh: 易诱选基于意图的选项，但实际拘禁要件仍不满足。

questions.subject: Torts
questions.question:
A woman was crossing the street at a crosswalk. A man on the nearby sidewalk thought he saw a speeding automobile headed in the woman's direction even though the car was clearly about to turn onto a different street before it would reach her. As a result, the man ran into the street and pushed the woman out of the path of the car. The woman fell to the ground and broke her leg.
In an action for battery brought by the woman against the man, will the woman likely prevail?

choices.A: No, because the man believed that the woman was actually in danger.
choices.B: No, because the man's intent was to save the woman.
choices.C: Yes, because the man failed to use reasonable care.
choices.D: Yes, because the man should have realized that the woman was not actually in danger.

questions.explanation:
Consent to contact
Actual
Apparent
Presumed
Emergency doctrine

If a defendant intends to cause contact with a plaintiff's person, the defendant's affirmative conduct causes contact, and such contact is harmful or offensive to the plaintiff, then the defendant is liable for battery absent a defense. Consent (actual, apparent, presumed, or emergency) is a defense to battery in certain situations. Under the emergency doctrine, a plaintiff's consent is presumed when:

  • the purpose of the conduct is to prevent or reduce a risk to the life or health of the plaintiff
  • the defendant reasonably believes that his/her conduct is necessary to prevent or reduce a risk to the plaintiff's life or health that substantially outweighs the plaintiff's interest in avoiding the conduct
  • the defendant reasonably believes that immediate action is necessary to prevent or reduce the risk before it is practicable for the defendant to obtain actual consent from the plaintiff and
  • the defendant has reason to believe that the plaintiff would have actually consented to the conduct if given the opportunity to do so.

Here, the man intentionally pushed the woman, causing her to fall and break her leg, because he believed that he needed to push the woman to prevent her from being hit by the car. Although he intended to save the woman, he should have realized that there was no need to protect her because the car was clearly about to turn onto a different street before it would reach her (Choices A & B). Since there was no emergency, consent cannot be presumed and the woman will likely prevail in her battery action. (Choice C) Whether the man failed to use reasonable care would be relevant in a negligence action—not the woman's battery action.

Educational objective:
Under the emergency doctrine, a plaintiff's consent is presumed when (1) the purpose is to prevent or reduce a risk, (2) the defendant reasonably believes that his/her conduct is necessary to prevent or reduce a risk that substantially outweighs the plaintiff's interest in avoiding the conduct, (3) the defendant reasonably believes that immediate action is needed, and (4) he/she has reason to believe that the plaintiff would have actually consented.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Third) of Torts: Intentional Torts to Persons § 17 (Am. L. Inst., Tentative Draft No. 6, 2021) (explaining when consent is presumed under the emergency doctrine).
questions.zh-question:
一名女子正在人行横道上过马路。附近人行道上的一名男子认为他看到一辆超速行驶的汽车正朝该女子的方向驶来，尽管那辆车在到达她之前显然要转弯到另一条街上。因此，该男子冲到街上，将女子推离了汽车的路径。女子摔倒在地，摔断了腿。

在该女子对该男子提起的伤害罪（battery）诉讼中，该女子是否可能胜诉？

zh-choices.A: 不会，因为该男子相信该女子确实处于危险之中。
zh-choices.B: 不会，因为该男子的意图是救助该女子，而不是伤害她。
zh-choices.C: 会，因为该男子本可以大声警告，而不是将女子推开。
zh-choices.D: 会，因为该男子本应意识到该女子并未实际处于危险之中。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Intentional Torts: Battery & Defenses
📚 核心考点：非法侵犯 (Battery) 与 意图 (Intent)

在侵权法中，构成 Battery 的意图并不要求被告想要“伤害”原告。

  • 规则：只要被告意图造成身体接触 (Intent to contact)，且该接触在法律上被认定为有害或冒犯性的 (Harmful or offensive)，即构成 Battery。
  • 误区：“好心办坏事”通常不能作为直接否认 Battery 的理由。
🛡️ 抗辩事由：法律默示同意 (Consent Implied by Law)

在紧急情况下，法律会假定原告同意被告的救助行为，但这必须满足严格条件：

  1. 原告处于紧急情况 (Emergency situation)；
  2. 被告的行为是保护原告所必需的；
  3. 关键点：被告的信念必须是合理的 (Reasonable)。
🔍 案情关键点分析

本题的决胜点在于题目中的一个形容词：

"...the car was clearly (显然) about to turn..."

MBE 题目中的形容词通常是解题线索。既然汽车“显然”要转弯，意味着一个理性人 (Reasonable Person) 能够看出该女子并未处于危险之中。

💡 为什么选 D？
✅ 选项 D (Correct):
"Yes, because the man should have realized that the woman was not actually in danger."

虽然男子主观上认为有危险，但客观上（Clearly）并没有危险。因为他的判断不符合“理性人标准”，所以他不能主张“紧急避险”或“默示同意”作为抗辩。既然抗辩不成立，他故意的推搡行为导致了伤害，必须承担 Battery 的责任。

❌ 为什么其他选项错误？
选项 A (Wrong):
仅有主观信念 (Subjective belief) 是不够的。法律要求这种信念必须是客观合理的 (Objectively reasonable)。既然危险显然不存在，他的信念就是不合理的。
选项 B (Wrong):
这是最常见的干扰项。Good Motive (良好动机) $\neq$ No Intent (无意图)。 男子意图推搡女子，这满足了 Battery 的意图要件。动机好坏只影响赔偿金额，不影响责任成立与否。
🎓 MBE 实战技巧

注意题目中的事实限定词。如果题目说 "The man reasonably believed..."，那么答案就会完全相反（他将不承担责任）。但本题用了 "clearly... turn"，这就是在以此否定被告行为的合理性。

questions.subject: Torts
questions.question:
A businessman operates a collection agency. He was trying to collect a $400 bill for medical services rendered to a young woman by a doctor.
The businessman went to the young woman's house. When the young woman's mother answered the door, the businessman told her that he was there to collect a bill owed by the young woman. The mother told the businessman that because of the young woman's illness, she had been unemployed for six months, that she was still ill and unable to work, and that she would pay the bill as soon as she could.
The businessman, in a loud voice, demanded to see the young woman and said that if he did not receive payment immediately, he would file a criminal complaint charging her with fraud. The young woman, who was severely distressed after hearing the conversation, came to the door. The businessman, in a loud voice, repeated his demand for immediate payment and his threat to use criminal process.
If the young woman asserts a claim against the businessman based on infliction of emotional distress, is she likely to prevail?

choices.A: No, because the businessman's conduct created no risk of physical harm to the young woman.
choices.B: No, unless she suffered physical harm as a result of the businessman's conduct.
choices.C: Yes, if she suffered severe emotional distress as a result of the businessman's conduct.
choices.D: Yes, unless the bill for medical services was valid and past due.

questions.explanation:
For intentional infliction of emotional distress (IIED), the plaintiff must prove that the defendant:

  • by engaging in extreme and outrageous manner
  • intended to cause the plaintiff severe emotional distress OR recklessly disregarded the risk of causing such distress and
  • caused the plaintiff severe emotional distress.

Abusing a position of authority (e.g., creditor-debtor, medical professional-patient, employer-employee) amounts to extreme and outrageous conduct when the conduct goes far beyond what is necessary to exercise that authority. For example, a creditor abuses a position of authority by threatening a debtor with unjustified criminal prosecution or by contacting the debtor's employer or neighbors.

Here, the businessman (creditor) abused his position of authority when he unjustifiably threatened to file a criminal fraud complaint against the young woman for merely failing to pay a bill (extreme and outrageous conduct). In doing so, he was indifferent to the obvious risk that the threat would cause her severe emotional distress (recklessness). And since the young woman suffered such distress after hearing the businessman's threat, she will likely prevail on an IIED claim.

(Choice A) Risk of physical harm is an element of the zone-of-danger theory for negligent infliction of emotional distress—not IIED. Therefore, the young woman can prove IIED even if the businessman's conduct created no risk of physical harm.

(Choice B) IIED compensates persons who suffered severe emotional distress even when there is no proof of physical harm. As a result, the young woman's lack of physical harm will not affect the viability of her IIED claim.

(Choice D) Even if the bill was valid and past due, the businessman could only use reasonable means to collect that debt. But since the businessman engaged in extreme and outrageous conduct that recklessly caused the young woman severe emotional distress, he is liable for IIED.

📌 Educational Objective

Intentional infliction of emotional distress (IIED) requires proof that the defendant engaged in extreme and outrageous conduct (e.g., abusing a position of authority by going far beyond what is necessary to exercise that authority).

📚 References
  • Restatement (Third) of Torts: Liab. for Physical & Emotional Harm § 46 cmts. d–e (2012) (intentional or reckless infliction of emotional distress).

一名商人经营着一家讨债公司。他试图向一名年轻女子收取一笔由医生提供的价值400美元的医疗服务账单。

该商人前往该年轻女子的住所。当年轻女子的母亲开门时，该商人告诉她，他是来收取该年轻女子所欠的账单的。母亲告诉该商人，由于女儿生病，她已经失业六个月，目前仍然生病无法工作，但她会尽快支付账单。

该商人高声要求见该年轻女子，并声称如果他没有立即收到付款，他将提起刑事诉讼，指控她欺诈。年轻女子在听到对话后感到极度痛苦，于是走到了门口。该商人高声重复了他要求立即付款的请求以及他要动用刑事程序的威胁。

如果该年轻女子以造成精神痛苦为由对该商人提出索赔，她是否可能胜诉？

zh-choices.A: 不会，因为该商人的行为并未对该年轻女子造成身体伤害的风险。
zh-choices.B: 不会，除非她因该商人的行为而遭受了身体伤害。
zh-choices.C: 会，因为她因该商人的行为而遭受了严重的精神痛苦。
zh-choices.D: 会，除非该医疗服务账单是有效且已逾期的。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

故意造成精神痛苦 (IIED)

核心法律规则

Intentional Infliction of Emotional Distress (IIED)

  • 行为：必须是极端且令人发指的 (Extreme and outrageous conduct)。
  • 主观状态：故意 (Intentional) 或鲁莽 (Reckless)。
  • 结果：实际造成了严重的精神痛苦 (Severe emotional distress)。
  • 注意：IIED 不需要证明身体伤害 (Physical harm)。

案情分析与正确逻辑

本题考察的是在债务催收 (Debt Collection) 场景下，行为何时会跨越边界成为“极端且令人发指”。

普通的催债行为，即使态度粗鲁、让人尴尬或产生压力，通常也不构成 IIED。债权人有权通过合理方式要求还款。但是，当催收行为伴随加重因素 (Aggravating factors) 时，就可能构成侵权。

在本案中，商人具备了以下致命的加重因素：

  1. 滥用法律程序威胁：单纯拖欠民事医疗费并不构成犯罪。商人用刑事欺诈指控 (Criminal fraud complaint) 来威胁逼迫还款，属于严重的滥用权利。
  2. 利用已知脆弱性：母亲已经明确告知商人，年轻女子生病且失业。在明知对方处于特殊脆弱状态下，商人依然施加极端压力。
  3. 重复骚扰：当极度痛苦的女子来到门口时，商人当面再次高声重复了刑事威胁。

这三者的结合（无根据的刑事威胁 + 已知脆弱性 + 重复高声威胁）使得该行为超出了合理催收的范围，可以被认定为 Extreme and outrageous conduct。

两个容易踩的坑

不要把 IIED 和 NIED 混在一起：直接的 IIED 不要求原告证明身体伤害，也不要求先有身体伤害风险。那些要求通常来自过失造成精神痛苦 (NIED) 的特定理论，例如 zone of danger。

不要把真实债务当成万能抗辩：债务真实、逾期，只能说明债权人可以合理催收；它不能授权债权人用无根据的刑事指控威胁来逼迫付款。

考场备考策略

在 MBE 考试中，IIED 是一个“高门槛”侵权。如果题干只是普通的侮辱、吵架或正常的催债，通常不选 IIED。但如果题干中出现了权力不对等（如雇主对雇员、债权人对债务人），并且伴随非法威胁（特别是刑事起诉威胁）、针对孕妇/病人/老人的骚扰、或极端的种族/性别侮辱，请果断考虑 IIED。牢记：IIED 只看精神痛苦，不看身体伤害！

questions.subject: Torts
questions.question:
A college student who was being initiated into a fraternity was playing a game in which all of the initiates had to drink one beer every 10 minutes. Whoever drank the most would be the winner and guarantee his admission to the fraternity. After drinking a few beers, the student was the first initiate to give up. One of the fraternity brothers told the student he could sleep off the beer in one of the bedrooms upstairs. The student was barely able to stand, so he agreed, and the fraternity brother said he would help the student to the bedroom. The fraternity brother guided the student by the arm to keep him from falling. Because the student was highly intoxicated, he did not notice that the fraternity brother was actually taking him to a mattress on the exposed roof of the fraternity house. The fraternity brother helped the student to the mattress on the roof, and the student immediately fell asleep. The next morning, the student woke up with frostbite in his fingertips due to exposure to the cold.
If the student sues the fraternity brother for battery, is he likely to succeed?

choices.A: No, because the student consented to playing the drinking game.
choices.B: No, because the student consented to sleeping on the mattress on the roof.
choices.C: Yes, because consent to an egregious intentional tort is never valid.
choices.D: Yes, because the fraternity brother took advantage of the student's mistaken consent.

questions.explanation:
Negation of actual consent
Lack of capacity
  • Plaintiff's lack of capacity due to youth, intoxication, or intellectual incompetence may negate validity of consent
  • Plaintiff who appreciates nature, extent & potential consequences of defendant's conduct has capacity to consent it
  • Adult generally is rebuttably presumed to have capacity to consent
Duress
  • Actual consent given under duress (e.g., physical force, threats) is not valid
  • Threat must be of present action, not future action
  • Threats of economic duress & moral pressure generally do not render plaintiff's consent invalid
Substantial mistake
  • Actual consent due to substantial mistake regarding nature or invasion of plaintiff's interests, extent of expected harm, or defendant's purpose in engaging in conduct is valid unless defendant:
  • caused mistake by affirmative misrepresentation or fraud or
  • knew of mistake

A defendant is liable for battery if the defendant intends to cause contact with a plaintiff's person, the defendant's affirmative conduct causes such contact, and it is harmful or offensive to the plaintiff. However, a defendant may be absolved of liability based on a defense such as actual consent. A defendant may assert actual consent as a defense to an intentional tort if the plaintiff willingly submitted to contact and the conduct was within the scope of consent(Choice C).

The plaintiff's actual consent is valid even if it was given because of a substantial mistake as to the nature or the invasion of the plaintiff's interests, the extent of the anticipated harm, or the defendant's purpose in engaging in the conduct. This is true unless the defendant:

  • caused the mistake by affirmative misrepresentation or fraud or
  • knew about the mistake.

Here, the fraternity brother intentionally guided the student to the mattress on the roof, exposing the student to the elements and causing his frostbite (battery). Although the student consented to letting the fraternity brother help him, the student mistakenly believed that he was being guided to the bedroom because the fraternity brother said so. Because the fraternity brother caused and knowingly took advantage of the student's mistake, the student's consent was ineffective. Therefore, if the student sues the fraternity brother for battery, he is likely to succeed.

*A plaintiff's lack of capacity due to intoxication may negate the validity of consent. But an individual who appreciates the nature, extent, and potential consequences of conduct has the capacity to consent. Here, the student, who was aware of his limited mobility due to intoxication, appreciated the nature, extent, and potential consequences of allowing the fraternity brother to assist him.

(Choices A and B) The student consented to participating in the drinking game and to being helped to the bedroom upstairs, but he did not consent to being taken to a mattress on the roof. Instead, he was mistaken about where he was being led, and this mistake was caused by the fraternity brother's affirmative misrepresentation.

📌 Educational Objective

Actual consent to an intentional tort given because of a substantial mistake may still be valid unless the defendant (1) caused the mistake by affirmative misrepresentation or fraud or (2) knew about the mistake.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Third) of Torts: Intentional Torts to Persons § 13 (Am. L. Inst., Tentative Draft No. 4, 2019) (defining actual consent).
  • Restatement (Third) of Torts: Intentional Torts to Persons § 15 (Am. L. Inst., Tentative Draft No. 4, 2019) (setting forth how actual consent can be negated by substantial mistake).

如果学生就 battery 起诉该兄弟会成员，他是否可能胜诉？

questions.subject: Torts
questions.question:
In a tavern, an intoxicated woman threatened to slash a man with a broken beer bottle she was holding. Another customer, who had not been threatened by the woman, forcefully grabbed the woman and locked her in the tavern's storeroom until the police could arrive. In the process, although the customer used reasonable force, the customer badly sprained the woman's wrist.
Is the woman likely to recover in an action against the customer?

choices.A: No, because the customer's conduct was privileged as a defense of others.
choices.B: Yes, based on battery only.
choices.C: Yes, based on false imprisonment only.
choices.D: Yes, based on both battery and false imprisonment.

questions.explanation:
Defense of others (i.e., third parties)

Defendant reasonably believes:

  • circumstances are such that third party has privilege of self-defense and
  • defendant's action is immediately necessary to protect third party

The privilege to use reasonable force in the defense of others (i.e., third parties) exists when the defendant reasonably believes that:

  • the circumstances are such that the third party has a privilege of self-defense and
  • the defendant's action is immediately necessary to protect the third party.

Here, the customer was privileged to grab the woman and lock her in the tavern's storeroom (reasonable force) to defend the man. That is because the customer could have reasonably believed that (1) the man had the privilege to defend himself from the woman's threat to slash him with the broken beer bottle in her hand and (2) the customer's actions were immediately necessary to protect the man from the woman. Therefore, the woman likely will not recover in an action against the customer.

(Choices B & D) Battery occurs when a defendant intends to create contact with the plaintiff's person and causes harmful or offensive contact with the plaintiff. Although the customer committed battery when he intentionally grabbed the woman and sprained her wrist, the customer is not liable because he was privileged to use reasonable force to defend the man.

(Choices C & D) False imprisonment occurs when the defendant intentionally confines the plaintiff within a limited area and the plaintiff is conscious of the confinement. Here, the customer falsely imprisoned the woman when he intentionally locked her in the storeroom, but the customer is not liable because his conduct was privileged.

📌 Educational Objective

A defendant is privileged to use reasonable force in the defense of others when the defendant reasonably believes that (1) the circumstances are such that the third party has the privilege of self-defense and (2) the defendant's action is immediately necessary to protect the third party.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Third) of Torts: Intentional Torts to Persons § 24 (Am. L. Inst., Tentative Draft No. 6, 2021) (explaining when a defendant has the privilege to use force to defend a third party).
questions.zh-question:
在一家酒馆里，一名醉酒女子威胁要用她手中持有的碎啤酒瓶划伤一名男子。另一名未受该女子威胁的顾客用力抓住该女子，并将她锁在酒馆的储藏室里，直到警察到来。在此过程中，尽管该顾客使用了合理的武力，但还是严重扭伤了该女子的手腕。

该女子在对该顾客提起的诉讼中是否可能获得赔偿？

zh-choices.A: 不会，因为该顾客的行为因“他人防卫”而享有特免权。
zh-choices.B: 会，仅基于殴击。
zh-choices.C: 会，仅基于非法监禁。
zh-choices.D: 会，基于殴击和非法监禁。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考题解析

Torts: Defense of Others
正确答案：A

结论：该女子无法获得赔偿，因为顾客的行为享有“他人防卫”的特免权。

核心考点：他人防卫 (Defense of Others)

在侵权法中，如果被告满足以下条件，则有权使用合理武力保护第三方：

  • 合理确信 (Reasonable Belief)：被告合理地相信第三方正面临即将发生的非法身体伤害。
  • 必要性 (Necessity)：被告的行为对于保护该第三方是必要的。
  • 合理武力 (Reasonable Force)：使用的武力程度与威胁的程度相当。

📝 案情逻辑推演

1. 威胁识别 (Threat) 醉酒女子手持碎啤酒瓶威胁要划伤男子。这构成了即将发生的严重身体伤害 (Imminent Bodily Harm)。
2. 介入行为 (Intervention) 顾客抓住女子并将其锁入储藏室。
注意：表面上这构成了殴击 (Battery) 和非法监禁 (False Imprisonment)。
3. 特免权抗辩 (Privilege Defense) 顾客是为了保护受威胁的男子。题目明确指出顾客使用了“合理的武力” (Reasonable Force)。
4. 法律后果 (Legal Outcome) 由于存在有效的抗辩事由（他人防卫），被告的行为享有特免权 (Privileged)。因此，被告不承担侵权责任。

🚫 为什么其他选项错误？

选项 B、C、D 错误的原因：
这些选项虽然正确识别了顾客行为在形式上构成了“殴击”或“非法监禁”的要素（故意接触、故意限制自由），但它们忽略了肯定性抗辩 (Affirmative Defense) 的存在。

在侵权法考试中，即使原告证明了侵权行为的所有构成要件 (Prima Facie Case)，如果被告拥有有效的特免权，原告依然无法胜诉。
