questions.subject: Torts
questions.topic: Privilege Of Arrest And Other Crime Related Conduct
questions.question:
Local police notified local gas station attendants that a robber had recently committed armed robberies at five gas stations in the city. The police said that the robber was a 75-year-old woman with white hair who drove a vintage, cream-colored Ford Thunderbird. Attendants were advised to call police if they saw her but not to attempt to apprehend her. Armed robbery is a felony under state law.
A traveler was passing through the city on a cross-country journey. The traveler was a 75-year-old woman who had white hair and drove a vintage, cream-colored Ford Thunderbird. When the traveler drove into a gas station in the city, the owner thought that the traveler must be the robber wanted by the police. After checking the oil at the traveler's request, the owner falsely informed the traveler that she had a broken fan belt, that her car could not be driven without a new belt, that it would take him about an hour to replace it, and that she should stay in his office for consultation about the repair. The traveler was greatly annoyed that her journey was delayed, but she agreed. The owner then showed the traveler to his office and locked its only door. The traveler saw the owner lock the door but did not protest because she was tired. The traveler stayed in the owner's office while she waited for her car. The owner then telephoned the police and, within the hour, the police came and questioned the traveler. The police immediately determined that the traveler was not the robber, and the traveler resumed her journey without further delay.
Assume that the majority rules for intentional torts and their defenses apply.
If the traveler sues the owner for false imprisonment, will the traveler likely prevail?

choices.A: No, because the owner reasonably believed that the traveler was the robber.
choices.B: No, because the traveler suffered no physical or mental harm.
choices.C: Yes, because the owner lied to the traveler about the condition of her car.
choices.D: Yes, if the traveler reasonably believed she could not leave the owner's premises.

questions.explanation:
Explanation

Private citizen's privilege to arrest
Type of crime Approach Rule
Felony Majority
  • Felony has been committed and
  • defendant reasonably suspects that plaintiff committed it
Third
Restatement
  • Plaintiff committed felony for which defendant is arresting plaintiff and
  • defendant reasonably believes that law enforcement will likely be unable to apprehend plaintiff unless defendant immediately confines plaintiff
Misdemeanor Majority
  • Misdemeanor is being committed or reasonably appears about to be committed in presence of defendant and
  • misdemeanor is breach of peace
Third
Restatement
  • Misdemeanor creates substantial risk of bodily harm and
  • defendant reasonably believes that law enforcement will likely be unable to prevent or terminate crime unless defendant immediately uses force

False imprisonment occurs in most jurisdictions when a defendant intentionally confines the plaintiff within a limited area and the plaintiff is conscious of the confinement. But in most jurisdictions, a defendant who is a private citizen (i.e., not a police officer) is privileged to confine or arrest a plaintiff when:

  • a felony has been committed and
  • the defendant reasonably suspects that the plaintiff committed the felony.*

Here, the owner was privileged to confine the traveler because (1) five felony armed robberies had been committed at gas stations in the city and (2) the owner reasonably believed that the traveler committed those robberies since she and her car matched the police description. Therefore, the traveler will not prevail on her false imprisonment claim.

*Under the Third Restatement, a defendant is privileged to arrest a plaintiff when (1) the plaintiff actually committed the felony for which the defendant is arresting the plaintiff and (2) the defendant reasonably believes that law enforcement will likely be unable to apprehend the plaintiff unless the defendant immediately confines the plaintiff.

(Choice B) In a minority of jurisdictions and under the Third Restatement, a plaintiff who was not conscious of the confinement may still recover if he/she was harmed by the confinement. But the traveler here was conscious of her confinement since she saw the owner lock the door. Instead, her claim will fail because the owner was privileged to confine her.

(Choices C & D) Even if the traveler can show that the owner lied to her about the condition of her car to prevent her from leaving (intent to confine) and that she reasonably believed she could not leave (confinement and awareness), her false imprisonment claim will fail because the owner had the right to confine her.

📌 Educational Objective

In most jurisdictions, a defendant is privileged to confine or arrest a plaintiff when a felony has been committed and the defendant reasonably suspects that the plaintiff committed it.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Third) of Torts § 7: Intentional Torts to Persons (Am. L. Inst., Tentative Draft No. 3, 2018) (providing the definition for false imprisonment).
  • Restatement (Third) of Torts: Intentional Torts to Persons § 35 (Am. L. Inst., Tentative Draft No. 6, 2021) (explaining the privilege of arrest).
questions.zh-question:
当地警方通知了当地加油站的服务员，一名抢劫犯最近在该市的五个加油站实施了武装抢劫。警方称，抢劫犯是一名75岁的白发女性，驾驶一辆复古的米色Ford Thunderbird。警方建议服务员如果看到她就报警，但不要试图逮捕她。根据州法律，武装抢劫是重罪。

一名旅客正在进行跨州旅行，途经该市。该旅客是一名75岁的白发女性，驾驶一辆复古的米色Ford Thunderbird。当该旅客驾车进入市内一家加油站时，加油站老板认为该旅客一定是警方通缉的抢劫犯。应旅客的要求检查机油后，老板谎称她的风扇皮带断了，没有新皮带她的车就无法行驶，更换皮带需要大约一个小时，并让她在他的办公室里等待，以便就维修事宜进行商议。旅客对行程被耽搁感到非常恼火，但她还是在等待修车期间留在了老板的办公室里。老板随后报了警，不到一小时，警察赶到并对旅客进行了盘问。警方立即确定该旅客并非抢劫犯，旅客随即继续她的旅程，没有再被耽搁。

如果该旅客以非法拘禁为由起诉加油站老板，她是否可能胜诉？

zh-choices.A: 不会，因为老板有合理理由相信该旅客是抢劫犯。
zh-choices.B: 不会，因为该旅客没有遭受任何身体或精神上的伤害。
zh-choices.C: 会，因为老板就车况问题对旅客撒了谎。
zh-choices.D: 会，如果该旅客有合理理由相信她不能离开老板的经营场所。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

核心考点：非法拘禁 (False Imprisonment) 与 公民逮捕特免权 (Citizen's Arrest Privilege)

⚖️ 法律规则详解

本题考察的是侵权法中的抗辩事由 (Defenses)。虽然原告可能能够证明非法拘禁的构成要件，但如果被告拥有合法的特免权，则无需承担责任。

私人公民逮捕特免权 (Private Citizen's Privilege to Arrest)

普通法下，私人（非警察）在以下情况逮捕或限制他人自由享有特免权：

犯罪类型 特免权条件
重罪 (Felony) 1. 重罪事实上已经发生 (In fact committed)
2. 被告有合理理由相信 (Reasonably believes) 是原告实施的。
轻罪 (Misdemeanor) 必须涉及破坏和平 (Breach of peace) 且是在被告面前发生的。

🔍 案情分析

让我们将规则应用到本案事实中：

第一步：构成非法拘禁吗？
是的。老板通过谎称车坏了（欺诈）导致旅客不敢离开，这构成了对旅客意志的限制，且旅客意识到了被限制。这满足了 False Imprisonment 的表面构成要件 (Prima Facie Case)。
第二步：有抗辩事由吗？
我们需要检查公民逮捕特免权的两个要素：
  1. 重罪是否事实上发生？
    ✔ 是。 题目明确指出“一名抢劫犯最近实施了武装抢劫”，且武装抢劫是重罪。
  2. 是否有合理理由怀疑原告？
    ✔ 是。 警方描述非常具体（75岁、白发、复古米色 Ford Thunderbird），旅客完全符合这一特征。老板的怀疑是客观合理的。
结论：
因为老板满足了公民逮捕特免权的条件，所以他的限制行为是合法的 (Privileged)。因此，旅客不会胜诉。

❌ 选项辨析

选项 A (正确答案)
"不会，因为老板有合理理由相信该旅客是抢劫犯。"
这是本题的关键抗辩理由。只要重罪确实发生，且怀疑合理，特免权即成立。
选项 B (错误)
"不会，因为该旅客没有遭受任何身体或精神上的伤害。"
非法拘禁不要求实际伤害。只要原告意识到 (Aware of) 被限制，或者因限制受到伤害，即可起诉。如果旅客当时睡着了且没受伤害，这个选项才可能成立。但在本案中，她意识到了限制。
选项 C (错误)
"会，因为老板就车况问题对旅客撒了谎。"
虽然老板撒谎了（这是实施拘禁的手段），但这并不否定他的特免权。特免权允许他在合理怀疑的情况下进行拘禁，手段是否包含欺骗在此处不是决定性因素。
选项 D (错误)
"会，如果该旅客有合理理由相信她不能离开..."
这个选项描述的是非法拘禁的构成要件（原告视角的限制感）。虽然这证明了“拘禁”的存在，但它忽略了被告的“特免权”这一绝对抗辩。在MBE中，如果有有效的抗辩事由，原告就不能胜诉。

💡 考试通关秘籍

1. 区分警察与公民：
警察逮捕只需“合理根据” (Probable Cause) 认为重罪发生即可；而公民逮捕要求重罪必须事实上已经发生。如果本题中并没有发生抢劫，只是误报，警察有特免权，但加油站老板（公民）则没有。

2. 区分构成要件与抗辩：
选项 C 和 D 都在强调非法拘禁的构成要件（欺诈、限制感）。做题时要按顺序思考：
构成要件满足吗？ → 满足 → 有抗辩事由吗？ → 有 → 原告败诉。
不要停留在构成要件阶段。

questions.subject: Torts
questions.question:
A pilot was flying his small plane when he experienced engine trouble and was forced to make an emergency landing. He landed the plane safely in a large yard behind a home located in a relatively remote area. Unfortunately, when he disembarked from the plane, he was attacked and injured by two large dogs kept by the homeowner to discourage trespassers. The homeowner, who had seen the plane land, had ordered the dogs to attack. Several months earlier, the homeowner had posted large signs around the perimeter of the yard warning of the dogs.
Does the pilot have a viable claim against the homeowner for battery?

choices.A: No, because the homeowner had provided adequate warning.
choices.B: No, because the pilot was a trespasser.
choices.C: Yes, because the pilot can invoke the privilege of necessity.
choices.D: Yes, because the pilot could not reasonably have been expected to see the warning signs posted by the homeowner.

questions.explanation:
Explanation

Defenses for intentional harm to persons
(justifications & excuses)
DefensesCounterdefenses
Consent
  • Consent revoked
  • Exceeded scope of consent
  • No capacity to consent (e.g., youth, incompetence)
  • Consented to crime (e.g., statutory rape)
  • Fraud, mistake, duress
Defense of self & others
  • Used excessive force
  • Unreasonable mistake
  • Defendant was initial aggressor
Defense of property
  • Used excessive force
  • Necessity (public & private)
Arrest &
prevention of crime
  • Used excessive force
  • Unreasonable mistake
Parental discipline
  • Used excessive force

Battery requires that the defendant intend to cause contact with the plaintiff's person and the defendant's affirmative conduct cause contact that is harmful or offensive to the plaintiff. A defendant may generally use reasonable force (e.g., battery) to stop a trespass. However, force cannot be used to stop a trespass committed out of private necessity--i.e., an intrusion that is, or reasonably appears to be, necessary to protect oneself, third parties, or property.

Here, the homeowner committed a battery when he ordered his dogs to attack the pilot (intent to cause contact), and the dogs then attacked and injured the pilot (harmful contact). The homeowner's battery was not justified because the pilot had been forced to make an emergency landing on the homeowner's property to protect himself (private necessity). Therefore, the homeowner is liable for battery.

(Choice A) The homeowner could use watchdogs to discourage trespassers, since he provided adequate warning of the dogs' presence. However, he could only use the dogs to inflict the same level of harm he was privileged to inflict directly. And since the homeowner could not use force to stop a trespass committed out of private necessity, neither could the dogs. Therefore, the warning signs do not excuse the homeowner's battery.

(Choice B) Although the pilot was a trespasser, the homeowner could not use force to stop the pilot because his trespass was excused by private necessity.

(Choice D) A landowner must take reasonable care to make a watchdog's presence known to probable intruders, not all intruders. Here, the homeowner took reasonable care to warn probable intruders about his watchdogs by posting large warning signs around the perimeter of his yard. Therefore, it does not matter that the pilot could not reasonably have been expected to see the warning signs from the air.

📌 Educational Objective

Although a defendant is generally privileged to use reasonable force (e.g., battery) to stop a trespass, the defendant cannot use force to stop a trespass committed out of private necessity--i.e., an emergency intrusion that is, or reasonably appears to be, necessary to protect oneself, third parties, or property.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Third) of Torts: Intentional Torts to Persons § 102 (Am. L. Inst., Tentative Draft No. 1, 2015) (defining the requisite intent for battery).
  • Restatement (Second) of Torts § 77 (Am. L. Inst. 1965) (privilege to use reasonable force).
  • Restatement (Second) of Torts § 197 (Am. L. Inst. 1965) (private necessity).
questions.zh-question:
一名飞行员在驾驶其小型飞机时遇到引擎故障，被迫紧急降落。他将飞机安全降落在一处相对偏远地区住宅后的大院子里。不幸的是，当他下飞机时，他被房主为阻止侵入者而饲养的两只大狗攻击并受伤。看到飞机降落的房主命令狗进行攻击。几个月前，房主已在院子四周张贴了大型警示牌，警告有狗。

该飞行员是否可以对房主提起有效的殴击之诉？

zh-choices.A: 不可以，因为房主已经提供了充分的警告。
zh-choices.B: 不可以，因为飞行员是侵入者。
zh-choices.C: 可以，因为飞行员可以援引紧急避险特权。
zh-choices.D: 可以，因为不能合理预期飞行员会看到房主张贴的警示牌。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析：侵权法 (Torts)

本题考察的核心是财产保卫权与紧急避险特权之间的冲突与优先顺位。

正确答案是：C. Yes, because the pilot can invoke the privilege of necessity.

1. 法律逻辑拆解

要理解为什么飞行员可以起诉房主“殴击” (Battery)，我们需要分析以下三个步骤：

第一步：是否构成了殴击 (Battery)？

构成。 房主命令狗攻击飞行员，这满足了殴击的要素：

  • 意图 (Intent)： 房主意图引起有害或冒犯性的接触。
  • 因果关系 (Causation)： 狗的攻击是由房主的命令直接导致的。
  • 伤害 (Harm)： 飞行员确实受伤了。
第二步：房主是否有抗辩理由？

通常情况下，土地所有者有权使用合理武力 (Reasonable Force) 来驱逐侵入者 (Trespasser)。这就是 Defense of Property（财产保卫抗辩）。

但是，这个权利不是绝对的。

第三步：紧急避险特权 (Privilege of Necessity)

这是本题的关键。飞行员因为引擎故障被迫降落，这属于 Private Necessity（私人紧急避险）。

法律规则： 当侵入者行使“紧急避险特权”时，土地所有者丧失了使用武力驱逐侵入者的权利。

2. 核心考点：私人紧急避险 (Private Necessity)

在侵权法中，为了保护自己的人身安全或更具价值的财产，一个人有权进入他人的土地。这种特权产生了两个重要的法律后果：

  1. 免受驱逐权： 土地所有者不能将处于紧急避险状态的人驱逐出去，也不能对其使用武力。如果所有者强行驱逐或攻击避险者，所有者将对造成的伤害负责（即本案的情况）。
  2. 不完全特权 (Incomplete Privilege)： 虽然避险者进入土地不构成非法的 Trespass，但避险者仍需对土地造成的实际损害 (Actual Damages) 进行赔偿（例如，如果飞机压坏了草坪，飞行员要赔钱，但房主不能放狗咬人）。

3. 为什么其他选项是错误的？

  • 选项 A 房主提供了充分警告
    错误原因： 警告标志（Warning signs）通常用于减少对普通侵入者的责任，或者证明没有疏忽。但在故意侵权 (Intentional Torts) 中，即便有警告，也不能对享有“紧急避险权”的人使用武力。警告不能赋予房主伤害避险者的权利。
  • 选项 B 飞行员是侵入者
    错误原因： 虽然飞行员未经许可进入，但因为“紧急避险”，他的进入在法律上是被允许的（Privileged）。因此，他不是普通的 Trespasser，房主不能像对待普通侵入者那样对待他。
  • 选项 D 无法合理预期看到警示牌
    错误原因： 这是一个干扰项。无论飞行员是否看到警示牌，或者警示牌是否合理，核心问题在于房主是否有权命令狗攻击。由于紧急避险的存在，房主无权使用武力，警示牌的可见性与此无关。
🎓 MBE 考试技巧

遇到涉及 Property Defense（财产保卫）的题目时，立刻检查是否存在 Necessity（紧急避险）：

1. 如果是 Public Necessity（公共紧急避险，如为了救整个社区而炸毁房子）：完全免责，无需赔偿。

2. 如果是 Private Necessity（私人紧急避险，如本题）：
👉 人身伤害： 土地主不能伤害避险者（否则构成 Battery）。
👉 财产损害： 避险者要赔偿弄坏的东西（Pay for damages）。

questions.subject: Torts
questions.question:
A boater, caught in a sudden storm and reasonably fearing that her boat would capsize, drove the boat up to a pier, exited the boat, and tied it to the pier. The pier was clearly marked with "No Trespassing" signs. The owner of the pier ran up to the boater and told her that the boat could not remain tied to his pier. The boater offered to pay the owner for the use of the pier but, over the boater's protest, the owner untied the boat and pushed it away from the pier. The boat was lost at sea.
Is the boater likely to prevail in an action against the owner to recover the value of the boat?

choices.A: No, because the owner told the boater that she could not tie her boat to the pier.
choices.B: No, because there was a possibility that the boat would not be damaged by the storm.
choices.C: Yes, because the boater offered to pay the owner for the use of his pier.
choices.D: Yes, because the boater was privileged to enter the owner's property to save her boat.

questions.explanation:
Trespass excused by private necessity

Trespasser liable for broken flower pot
Landowner liable for dog bite

Under the doctrine of private necessity, a trespass to land is privileged when the intrusion is, or reasonably appears to be, necessary to protect oneself, third parties, or property from serious harm. The landowner cannot stop the privileged trespass and is liable to the trespasser for damages resulting from any attempt to do so.

Here, the boater tied her boat to the pier without the owner's consent (trespass) because she reasonably believed that the intrusion was necessary to protect her boat from capsizing in the sudden storm (private necessity). Although the owner had no right to stop her intrusion, he untied her boat and pushed it away from the pier, causing the boat to be lost at sea. As a result, the boater can recover the value of her boat from the owner.

(Choice A) The boater had the right to tie her boat to the pier over the owner's protest to save it from capsizing in the storm (private necessity). Therefore, the owner's objection to the boater's use of the pier is irrelevant.

(Choice B) Even if there was a possibility that the boat would not be damaged by the storm, the boater's trespass was still privileged because her intrusion reasonably appeared to be necessary to protect her boat.

(Choice C) A person does not have to pay to use the landowner's property for private necessity. Therefore, the owner would still be liable for damage to the boat even if the boater had not offered to pay for the use of the pier.

📌 Educational Objective

A landowner must permit a trespass arising from private necessity (an intrusion that is, or reasonably appears to be, necessary to protect oneself, third parties, or property from serious harm) and is liable for damages resulting from an attempt to stop a privileged trespass.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Second) of Torts § 197 (Am. Law Inst. 1965) (definition of private necessity).
  • Restatement (Second) of Torts § 77 cmt. d & e (Am. Law Inst. 1965) (defense of property).

一名船主突遇风暴，并合理地担心她的船会倾覆，于是将船开到一个码头，下船后将船系在码头上。该码头清楚地标有“禁止侵入”的标志。码头所有者跑向船主，告诉她船不能继续系在他的码头上。船主提出向所有者支付码头使用费，但所有者不顾船主的抗议，解开了船的缆绳并将其推离码头。最终船在海上遗失。

船主对所有者提起诉讼以追回船的价值，她是否可能胜诉？

zh-choices.A: 否，因为所有者已告知船主她不能将船系在码头上。
zh-choices.B: 否，因为船只存在不会被风暴损坏的可能性。
zh-choices.C: 是，因为船主已提出向所有者支付使用其码头的费用。
zh-choices.D: 是，因为船主为拯救她的船只而享有进入所有者财产的特权。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Intentional Torts: Defenses

⚖️ 核心考点：私人紧急避险 (Private Necessity)

当一个人为了保护自己、他人或财产免受严重伤害（serious harm）而有必要（或合理地认为有必要）进入他人土地时，该侵入行为享有特权 (Privilege)。

这种特权是不完全的 (Incomplete Privilege)：

  • 侵入者有权停留在土地上，土地所有者无权驱逐。
  • 但侵入者必须为对土地造成的实际损害 (Actual Damages) 负责。
📚 经典判例回顾

本题的情境几乎完全复刻了美国侵权法中的著名案例 Ploof v. Putnam (1908)。

在该案中，原告因暴风雨将船系在被告的码头上，被告的仆人解开了缆绳，导致船只损毁和人员受伤。法院判决：土地所有者无权在紧急情况下驱逐侵入者，并需对驱逐行为造成的损害承担责任。

🔍 案情分析

1. 紧急情况 (Emergency): 船主遭遇突发风暴，合理担心船只倾覆。

2. 特权产生 (Privilege Arises): 为了保全财产（船），船主有权进行“侵入”（系船在码头）。这构成了 Private Necessity。

3. 所有者的义务 (Owner's Duty): 面对享有特权的侵入者，码头所有者必须容忍其停留。虽然他可以要求船主赔偿码头的损坏（如有），但他绝对不能切断缆绳或驱逐船主。

4. 责任归属 (Liability): 所有者强行解开缆绳的行为是非法的（构成了 Conversion 或 Trespass to Chattels），因此他必须对船只的灭失负责。

💡 选项辨析

✅ 选项 D 正确
"Yes, because the boater was privileged to enter..."
这是最准确的法律依据。因为船主享有特权（Privilege），所以她的行为不是非法的侵入，而所有者阻止她行使该特权的行为则是非法的。

❌ 选项 A 错误
(Owner's objection)
在紧急避险（Necessity）的特权面前，土地所有者的反对或“禁止入内”标志是无效的。特权凌驾于所有者的排他权之上。

❌ 选项 B 错误
(Possibility of no damage)
法律标准是“合理的信念” (Reasonable belief)。只要船主当时合理地认为有必要系船以防倾覆，即使事后证明风暴可能不会损坏船只，特权依然存在。

❌ 选项 C 错误
(Offer to pay)
虽然这是一个干扰项，但逻辑不严密。船主是否有权进入，取决于“紧急情况”，而不是她是否“提议付费”。即使她没带钱，只要情况紧急，她依然有权系船。当然，根据 Vincent v. Lake Erie 规则，她事后必须赔偿码头的实际损失，但这与她是否有权进入是两个问题。

MBE 考试技巧：
遇到“风暴”、“躲避追杀”或“紧急着陆”进入他人领地的情形，
首先判断是 Public Necessity（为了公众利益，完全免责）
还是 Private Necessity（为了私利，有权进入但需赔偿损耗）。

本题考查的是 Private Necessity 中土地所有者的容忍义务。

questions.subject: Torts
questions.question:
The manager of a department store noticed that a customer was carrying a scarf with her as she examined various items in the blouse department. The manager recognized the scarf as an expensive one carried by the store. The customer was trying to find a blouse that matched a color in the scarf and, after a while, found one. The manager then saw the customer put the scarf into her purse, pay for the blouse, and head for the door. The manager, who was eight inches taller than the customer, blocked the customer's way to the door and asked to see the scarf in the customer's purse. The customer produced the scarf, as well as a receipt showing that it had been purchased from the store on the previous day. The manager then told the customer there was no problem and stepped out of her way.
In an action by the customer against the store for false imprisonment, which of the following, if supported by the evidence, will be the store's best defense?

choices.A: The customer assumed the risk of being detained by carrying the scarf in public view and then putting it into her purse.
choices.B: The customer should have realized that her conduct would create a reasonable belief that facts existed warranting a privilege to detain her.
choices.C: The customer was not detained but was merely questioned about the scarf.
choices.D: The manager had a reasonable belief that the customer was shoplifting and detained her only briefly for a reasonable investigation of the facts.

questions.zh-question:
一家百货公司的经理注意到，一名顾客在女装部挑选商品时，随身带着一条围巾。经理认出那条围巾是店里出售的一款昂贵围巾。该顾客试图找一件与围巾颜色相配的女衫，过了一会儿，她找到了一件。随后，经理看到该顾客将围巾放进她的手提包，支付了女衫的钱，然后走向门口。经理比顾客高八英寸，他挡住了顾客通往门口的路，并要求查看顾客手提包里的围巾。顾客出示了围巾，以及一张表明该围巾是前一天从该店购买的收据。经理于是告诉顾客没问题了，并让开了路。

在该顾客就非法监禁对商店提起的诉讼中，如果以下哪一项得到证据支持，将成为商店的最佳抗辩理由？

zh-choices.A: 顾客在公众视野中携带围巾然后将其放入手提包，即已自负被拘留的风险。
zh-choices.B: 顾客本应意识到，她的行为会使他人产生合理的相信，认为存在足以构成合法拘留特权的事实。
zh-choices.C: 顾客未被拘留，仅是就围巾被询问。
zh-choices.D: 经理有合理的理由相信顾客在进行商店盗窃，并且只是为了对事实进行合理调查而短暂地拘留了她。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Intentional Torts: False Imprisonment

核心考点：店家特权
(Shopkeeper's Privilege)

这是针对非法监禁 (False Imprisonment) 指控最常见的抗辩理由。商店在满足特定条件时，有权暂时扣留顾客进行调查。

⚖️ 法律规则 (The Rule)

店家特权 (Shopkeeper's Privilege) 的成立必须同时满足以下三个要素：

  1. 合理的相信 (Reasonable Belief): 店家必须有合理的理由怀疑该人进行了商店盗窃 (Shoplifting)。
  2. 合理的调查 (Reasonable Investigation): 拘留的目的必须是为了调查事实。
  3. 合理的时间与方式 (Reasonable Time & Manner): 拘留的时间必须短暂且必要，手段必须适当。

✅ 正确答案分析 (选项 D)

Best Defense

为什么选 D？

本题完美契合了店家特权的三个要素：

  • Reasonable Belief: 经理亲眼看到顾客把围巾放进包里且未付款就走向门口，这构成了怀疑盗窃的充分理由。
  • Reasonable Manner: 经理只是挡住去路并要求看围巾，没有使用过度武力或羞辱顾客。
  • Reasonable Time: 只要看到收据解释清楚后，经理立刻就放行了，拘留时间非常短暂。

因此，如果证据支持这些事实，这是商店对抗非法监禁指控的最佳抗辩。

❌ 为什么其他选项是错的？

选项 A & B 混淆了侵权类型 (Tort Categories)

选项A提及的“自甘风险” (Assumption of Risk) 和选项B暗示的“与有过失” (Contributory Negligence) 都是针对过失侵权 (Negligence) 的抗辩。

非法监禁属于故意侵权 (Intentional Torts)。你不能因为“不小心”或“应该意识到”就为故意剥夺他人自由的行为辩护。这些抗辩在此类案件中通常不适用。

选项 C 法律定义错误

选项C声称顾客“未被拘留”。这是错误的。在法律上，监禁 (Confinement) 只要限制了原告在固定界限内的自由，并且原告意识到这种限制，即告成立。

经理利用身体优势挡住去路 (Blocking the way)，在法律上已经构成了监禁行为，哪怕时间很短。商店不能否认拘留的事实，只能主张该拘留是有特权的 (Privileged)。

💡 MBE 考试技巧：
在处理 Intentional Torts 题目时，如果看到店家扣留顾客的情景： 1. 首先确认是否构成 False Imprisonment（通常都构成）。 2. 立即寻找 Shopkeeper's Privilege 作为抗辩。 3. 检查题干中的关键词：是否 "Reasonable"（合理的怀疑、合理的时间）。 4. 警惕那些试图用 Negligence 的抗辩（如 Assumption of Risk）来解释 Intentional Torts 的干扰项。

questions.subject: Torts
questions.topic: Defenses to claims for physical harms
questions.question:
A pedestrian walking home after a game of laser tag passed a narrow alley and thought that he saw a man attacking a woman. He ran forward, brandishing his laser tag gun and yelling, "Hands up, or I'll shoot!" In fact, the man was helping the woman, who had tripped, to her feet. However, the man, thinking that he was being threatened by a mugger with a gun, stumbled as he tried to run away from the pedestrian, falling and breaking his wrist.
If the man sues the pedestrian for assault, is the man likely to prevail?

choices.A: No, because the pedestrian reasonably believed that the woman was in imminent danger of bodily harm from the man.
choices.B: No, because the pedestrian used a toy laser gun to threaten the man.
choices.C: Yes, because the pedestrian intended to make the man afraid of imminent harmful contact.
choices.D: Yes, because the pedestrian was not entitled to use a threat of force to defend an unrelated third party.

questions.explanation:
Defense of others

Defendant can reasonably believe third party has the right
of self-defense

Initial
aggressor
Privilege to use nondeadly force
Privilege to use deadly force

Defendant cannot reasonably believe third party has the right
of self-defense

Initial
aggressor
No privilege

Assault occurs when (1) a defendant intends to cause the plaintiff to anticipate imminent harmful or offensive contact with the plaintiff’s person and (2) the defendant’s affirmative conduct causes the plaintiff to anticipate such contact. However, an assault is privileged and will not subject the defendant to civil liability when it is committed in defense of a third party—i.e., when the defendant reasonably believes that:

• the circumstances are such that the third party has a privilege of self-defense and
• the defendant’s action is immediately necessary to protect the third party.

Here, the pedestrian brandished his laser tag gun at the man, threatening to shoot him. This constituted assault because the pedestrian intended to cause, and did cause, the man to anticipate imminent harmful contact with his person. However, the pedestrian reasonably believed that this conduct was necessary to protect the woman (Choice C). Therefore, if the man sues the pedestrian for assault, the man is unlikely to prevail because the pedestrian reasonably believed that the woman was in imminent danger of bodily harm from the man.

(Choice B) The fact that the laser gun was a toy would not protect the pedestrian from liability if the man believed he was threatened with a real gun and no privilege applied. But here, the pedestrian could successfully assert the privilege of defense of third parties.

(Choice D) The privilege of defense of third parties may apply, as it does in this case, regardless of whether the third party is related to the defendant.

📌 Educational Objective

An assault is privileged when it is committed in defense of a third party—i.e., when the defendant reasonably believes that (1) the circumstances are such that the third party has a privilege of self-defense and (2) the defendant’s action is immediately necessary to protect the third party.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Third) of Torts: Intentional Torts to Persons § 24 (Am. L. Inst., Tentative Draft No. 6, 2021) (defining the privilege for defense of third parties).

questions.subject: Torts
questions.question:
Unaware that a lawyer was in the county courthouse library late on a Friday afternoon, when it was unusual for anyone to be using the library, a clerk locked the library door and left. The lawyer found herself locked in when she tried to leave the library at 7:00 p.m. It was midnight before the lawyer's family could find out where she was and get her out. The lawyer was very annoyed by her detention but was not otherwise harmed by it.
Does the lawyer have a viable claim for false imprisonment against the clerk?

choices.A: No, because it was unusual for anyone to use the library late on a Friday afternoon.
choices.B: No, because the clerk did not intend to confine the lawyer.
choices.C: Yes, because the clerk should have checked to make sure no one was in the library before the clerk locked the door.
choices.D: Yes, because the lawyer was aware of being confined.

questions.explanation:
A claim for false imprisonment requires proof that:

  • the defendant intended to confine the plaintiff within a limited area
  • the defendant's conduct caused the plaintiff's confinement OR the defendant failed to release the plaintiff from confinement despite owing a duty to do so and
  • the plaintiff was conscious of the confinement at the time it occurred.*

Here, the lawyer found herself locked in the library (conscious of confinement) after the clerk locked the library door (conduct causing confinement) (Choice D). However, the clerk did not lock the door with the intent to confine the lawyer because the clerk was unaware that the lawyer was in the library (no intent).

Therefore, the clerk is not liable for false imprisonment.

*In a minority of jurisdictions, a plaintiff who was not conscious of the confinement may still recover if the plaintiff was harmed by the confinement.

(Choice A) The fact that it was unusual for anyone to use the library at that time may help show that the clerk was not negligent in failing to detect the lawyer, but does not show whether the clerk acted intentionally. Therefore, this fact has no effect on the lawyer's false imprisonment claim.

(Choice C) Whether the clerk should have checked to make sure no one was in the library before locking the door is a negligence issue because it concerns what a reasonably prudent person in the clerk's position would have done. It is irrelevant to a claim for false imprisonment, which is an intentional tort requiring intent to confine the plaintiff.

📌 Educational Objective

False imprisonment occurs when (1) a defendant intends to confine the plaintiff within a limited area, (2) the defendant's conduct causes such confinement OR the defendant fails to release the plaintiff from confinement despite owing a duty to do so, and (3) the plaintiff is conscious of the confinement at the time it occurs.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Third) of Torts: Intentional Torts to Persons § 7 (Am. L. Inst., Tentative Draft No. 3, 2018) (discussing false imprisonment).
questions.zh-question: 一名书记员在周五下午晚些时候，不知道一位律师在县法院图书馆里。当时图书馆里有人是很不寻常的。该书记员锁上图书馆的门后便离开了。当这位律师在晚上7点试图离开时，发现自己被锁在里面。直到午夜，律师的家人才找到她的下落并让她出来。这位律师对被拘禁感到非常恼火，但并未因此受到其他伤害。 该律师能否对该书记员提起一项可行的 false imprisonment (非法监禁) 诉求？

zh-choices.A: 不能，因为在周五下午晚些时候有人使用图书馆是不寻常的。
zh-choices.B: 不能，因为书记员无意禁锢该律师。
zh-choices.C: 能，因为书记员在锁门前本应检查以确保图书馆内无人。
zh-choices.D: 能，因为该律师意识到了自己被禁锢。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Intentional Torts: False Imprisonment
正确答案：B

不能，因为书记员无意禁锢该律师。
(No, because the clerk did not intend to confine the lawyer.)

核心法律规则 (The Rule)

非法监禁 (False Imprisonment) 是一种故意侵权行为 (Intentional Tort)，其构成要件如下：

  • Act: 被告实施了禁锢或限制原告在特定区域内的行为。
  • Intent: 被告具有禁锢原告的故意 (Intent)。
  • Awareness/Harm: 原告在被禁锢时对此知情 (Aware)，或者因禁锢遭受了实际损害。

⚖️ 案情分析

本题的关键在于Intent (意图)。

虽然书记员锁门的行为确实导致了律师被关在图书馆内（满足了 Act 和 Confinement），且律师也知道自己被关住了（满足了 Awareness），但是：

题目明确指出书记员不知道 (Unaware) 律师在图书馆内。因此，书记员不可能有“禁锢该律师”的特定意图。

在 Intentional Torts 中，如果没有意图，就不构成该侵权行为。

🚫 易错点辨析 (Option C vs. B)

选项 C 提到“书记员本应该检查”(should have checked)。
这是一个典型的过失 (Negligence) 标准。如果律师起诉的是 Negligence，那么书记员未尽到合理注意义务 (Duty of Care) 可能是理由。但本题问的是 False Imprisonment，这是一个故意侵权。过失不足以构成故意侵权。
💡 MBE 考试技巧

在处理 Intentional Torts 题目时，第一步永远是检查被告是否具有Intent (故意)。

如果题目描述被告是“粗心的 (careless)”、“不知道的 (unaware)”或“本应该知道的 (should have known)”，这通常指向 Negligence，而不是 Intentional Tort。除非适用“转移故意 (Transferred Intent)”，否则没有故意就没有责任。

questions.subject: Torts
questions.question:
A landowner who owned a large tract of land in the mountains sought to protect a herd of wild deer that lived on part of the land. Although the landowner had posted signs that said, "No Hunting—No Trespassing," hunters frequently intruded to kill the deer. Recently, the landowner built an eight-foot-high chain-link fence, topped by three strands of barbed wire, across a gully on her land that provided the only access to the area where the deer lived.
A wildlife photographer asked the landowner for permission to enter the land to photograph the deer. Because the landowner feared that any publicity would encourage further intrusions by hunters, she denied the photographer's request. Frustrated, the photographer attempted to climb the fence. He became entangled in the barbed wire and suffered extensive lacerations. The wounds became infected and ultimately caused his death.
The photographer's personal representative has sued the landowner.
Is the personal representative likely to prevail?

choices.A: No, because the photographer entered the landowner's land after the landowner had refused him permission to do so and therefore was a trespasser.
choices.B: No, because the potential for harm created by the presence of the barbed wire was apparent.
choices.C: Yes, because the landowner had no property interest in the deer that entitled her to use force to protect them.
choices.D: Yes, because the landowner may not use deadly force to protect her land from intrusion.

questions.explanation:
Use of mechanical device to defend property

Mechanical device can be used to defend property when device is:

  • reasonably necessary to protect property from intrusion
  • reasonably proportionate to value of interest being protected—i.e., device cannot be unreasonably dangerous
  • customarily used for this purpose or reasonable care is taken to make its use known and
  • not intended or likely to cause death or serious bodily harm (e.g., barbed-wire fence, spiked wall)*

*Use of mechanical device that inflicts deadly force (e.g., spring gun, electric fence, human-trap) may be privileged if it satisfies requirements for using deadly force in self-defense or defense of others.

Almost every jurisdiction has enacted a survival statute that enables a decedent's personal representative to pursue tort claims on the decedent's behalf—so the photographer's personal representative can sue the landowner on the photographer's behalf. However, the landowner can assert she was privileged to use force to defend her property from trespassers like the photographer. A mechanical device (e.g., barbed-wire fence) can be used for this purpose when the device is:

  • reasonably necessary to protect the property from intrusion
  • reasonably proportionate to the value of the interest the defendant is protecting—i.e., the device cannot be unreasonably dangerous
  • customarily used for this purpose or reasonable care is taken to make its use known and
  • not intended or likely to cause death or serious bodily harm.*

Here, a barbed-wire fence was reasonably necessary to protect the landowner's land since her "No Trespassing" signs were frequently disregarded. The fence was not unreasonably dangerous since an eight-foot-high fence topped with barbed wire threatens only the most determined trespassers. The potential for harm created by the fence was apparent—not concealed—and it was not intended or likely to cause death or serious bodily harm (Choice B). Therefore, the use of the fence was privileged, and the personal representative is not likely to prevail.

*The use of a mechanical device that inflicts deadly force (e.g., spring gun, electric fence, human-trap) may be privileged if it satisfies requirements for using deadly force in self-defense or the defense of others (not seen here).

(Choice A) Because the photographer did not have permission to enter, he would have been a trespasser regardless of whether he had asked for and been refused permission. And since trespassers can recover for injuries caused by concealed or deadly devices (e.g., spring guns), the photographer's trespasser status is not enough to defeat his personal representative's claim.

(Choice C) Although the landowner had no property interest in the deer, she was entitled to use reasonable force to protect her property interest in the land.

📌 Educational Objective

A mechanical device is a privileged means of protecting property when it is (1) reasonably necessary to protect the property from intrusion, (2) not unreasonably dangerous, (3) customarily used for this purpose or reasonable care is taken to make its use known, and (4) not intended or likely to cause death or serious bodily harm.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Third) of Torts: Intentional Torts to Persons § 31 (Am. L. Inst., Tentative Draft No. 6, 2021) (setting forth the requirements for a defendant's use of a mechanical device to defend property).
  • Restatement (Second) of Torts § 926 (Am. L. Inst. 1979) (survival actions).

questions.subject: Torts
questions.question:
A teenager was riding a bicycle when she saw a classmate walking toward her. The teenager rode quickly toward the classmate, knowing that he would think she would run into him on her current trajectory. The teenager was not purposefully trying to harm or touch him. The classmate saw the teenager riding toward him and yelled at her to stop. The teenager swerved at the last moment and avoided hitting him. The classmate had a panic attack because he thought that the teenager would hit him.
Is the classmate likely to succeed if he sues the teenager for assault?

choices.A: No, because the teenager did not make contact with the classmate.
choices.B: No, because the teenager did not purposefully try to harm or touch the classmate.
choices.C: Yes, because the teenager acted with the requisite intent.
choices.D: Yes, because the teenager's conduct was extreme and outrageous.

questions.explanation:
Two types of intent
Purpose Girl desires to hit Boy A
Knowledge Girl is substantially certain she will also hit Boy B

Assault occurs when (1) a defendant intends to cause the plaintiff to anticipate an imminent, and harmful or offensive, contact with the plaintiff's person and (2) the defendant's affirmative conduct causes the plaintiff to anticipate such contact. The intent requirement is met when the defendant acts with either:

  • purpose - the desire to cause anticipation of an imminent harmful or offensive contact or
  • knowledge - the substantial certainty that the plaintiff will suffer such anticipation.

Here, the teenager rode her bicycle directly at her classmate, causing him to think that she would hit him (anticipation of imminent contact). And since the teenager acted with substantial certainty that the classmate would think she would run into him, she acted with the requisite intent. As a result, the classmate is likely to succeed in a suit against the teenager for assault.

(Choice A) Assault merely requires that the plaintiff be placed in anticipation of imminent contact. Actual bodily contact is not required. Therefore, the fact that the teenager did not make contact with the classmate is irrelevant.

(Choice B) The intent to make contact with the plaintiff is a requirement for battery, but assault merely requires the intent to cause the plaintiff to anticipate imminent contact. Therefore, the fact that the teenager did not purposefully try to harm or touch the classmate does not absolve her of liability for assault.

(Choice D) Extreme and outrageous conduct (i.e., conduct that is unacceptable in civilized society) is an element of intentional infliction of emotional distress--not assault, which only requires intentional conduct.

📌 Educational Objective

For assault, intent exists when a defendant acts with the purpose (desire) or knowledge (substantial certainty) that his/her conduct will cause the plaintiff to anticipate an imminent, and harmful or offensive, contact.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Third) of Torts: Intentional Torts to Persons § 105 (Am. L. Inst., Tentative Draft No. 1, 2015) (providing the elements for assault).

questions.subject: Torts
questions.question:
A farmer kept antiques in an uninhabited farmhouse on his property. The farmhouse had been broken into several times in the past, and some of the farmer's goods had been stolen. Instead of posting "No Trespassing" signs, the farmer decided to install an alarm system to deter intruders. While the farmer was in the farmhouse installing the alarm system, he heard a window open in the adjoining room. The farmer crept very quietly to the door of the room, threw the door open, and found a 10-year-old intruder. The farmer immediately struck the child very hard in the face, breaking her nose.
In an action on behalf of the child against the farmer to recover for the injury to her nose, is the child likely to prevail?

choices.A: No, because the farmer did not use deadly force.
choices.B: No, because the farmer had probable cause to believe that the child was a thief.
choices.C: Yes, because the farmer should have posted a "No Trespassing" sign.
choices.D: Yes, because the farmer used excessive force.

questions.explanation:
©UWorld

In defending against a plaintiff's action to recover damages for an intentionally inflicted injury (e.g., battery claim), a defendant can argue that he/she was privileged to use force to prevent the plaintiff's imminent intrusion on the defendant's land or personal property. This privilege applies when:

  • the plaintiff's imminent intrusion is not privileged
  • the defendant first asks the plaintiff to desist and the plaintiff disregards the request*
  • the defendant reasonably believes that the plaintiff is intruding or imminently will intrude upon the defendant's property and that the intrusion can be prevented or terminated only by the means used
  • the means used are reasonably proportionate to the value of the interest the defendant is protecting—i.e., the defendant cannot use excessive force and
  • the means used are not intended or likely to cause death or serious bodily injury.

Here, the child's entrance on the farmer's property was unprivileged because she did not have the farmer's permission to enter. This entitled the farmer to use reasonable force to remove her from his farmhouse (e.g., by carrying her off his property). Instead, the farmer used excessive force because he struck the girl very hard in the face and broke her nose. Therefore, the child will likely prevail in an action to recover for the injury to her nose.

*The defendant need not ask the plaintiff to desist if the defendant reasonably believes that (1) a request will be useless or dangerous or (2) substantial harm will be done before the request can be made.

(Choice A) Although the farmer striking the girl very hard in the face was not deadly force, it was excessive force.

(Choice B) Even if the farmer had probable cause to believe that the child was a thief, he was only privileged to use reasonable force to protect his property (not seen here).

(Choice C) A defendant need not have posted "No Trespassing" signs to defend his/her property.

📌 Educational Objective

A defendant who uses force to prevent a plaintiff's imminent intrusion on the defendant's land or personal property can only use means that are reasonably proportionate to the value of the interest the defendant is protecting—i.e., the defendant cannot use excessive force.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Third) of Torts: Intentional Torts to Persons § 30 (Am. L. Inst., Tentative Draft No. 6, 2021) (setting forth the requirements for a defendant's use of force to defend property).
questions.zh-question:
一名农夫将古董存放在其地产上一座无人居住的农舍里。该农舍过去曾被多次闯入，农夫的一些财物被盗。农夫没有张贴“禁止非法侵入”的标志，而是决定安装一个警报系统来威慑入侵者。当农夫在农舍里安装警报系统时，他听到隔壁房间有窗户打开的声音。农夫悄悄地爬到房间门口，猛地推开门，发现一个10岁的入侵者。农夫立即猛击孩子的脸部，打断了她的鼻子。

在一场代表该儿童向农夫提起的、就其鼻子受伤要求赔偿的诉讼中，该儿童是否可能胜诉？

zh-choices.A: 不会，因为农夫没有使用致命武力。
zh-choices.B: 不会，因为农夫有合理理由相信该儿童是小偷。
zh-choices.C: 会，因为农夫本应张贴“禁止非法侵入”的标志。
zh-choices.D: 会，因为农夫使用了过度武力。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Intentional Torts / Defense of Property
核心考点：财产保护权

在侵权法中，被告有权使用合理武力 (Reasonable Force) 来保护其财产免受侵犯。但是，这种特权有两个关键限制：

  • 武力必须与威胁成比例 (Proportionate)。
  • 绝不能使用过度武力 (Excessive Force)。
🔍 案情关键点分析

本题考察的是“合理性”的界限。我们需要对比双方的情况：

  • 入侵者：一名 10 岁的儿童，虽然是非法侵入 (Trespasser)，但并未表现出对农夫的人身威胁。
  • 农夫的反应：猛击面部并打断鼻子。

结论： 面对一个没有造成即时人身威胁的 10 岁儿童，直接重击面部显然超出了“阻止侵入”所需的必要限度。

✅ 正确答案：D

理由：农夫使用了过度武力 (Excessive Force)。

一旦被告使用的武力超过了合理必要的范围，财产保护的特权 (Privilege) 即告丧失。此时，被告必须对过度武力造成的伤害（即殴打行为 Battery）承担责任。

🚫 避坑指南 (为何其他选项错误)
选项 A (致命武力)： 这是一个常见的干扰项。虽然农夫确实没有使用致命武力（如开枪），但这并不意味着他免责。只要武力是过度的（即使是非致命的），被告就需要负责。
选项 B (小偷/合理理由)： 即使孩子是小偷，法律也不允许对非暴力财产犯罪使用严重的身体伤害作为惩罚或驱逐手段。特权仅限于“驱逐”，而非“报复”。
选项 C (告示牌)： 是否张贴 "No Trespassing" 标志与农夫是否可以使用暴力殴打入侵者无关。标志可能会影响入侵者的主观状态，但不会赋予地主使用过度暴力的权利。
💡 MBE 答题技巧

在涉及 Defense of Property 的题目中，永远记住：
人身安全 > 财产安全。

如果题目中出现“为了保护空屋子/古董”而对人（尤其是弱势群体如儿童）造成严重身体伤害，通常都属于 Excessive Force。

questions.subject: Torts
questions.question:
A basketball player suffered an injury while participating in an impromptu basketball game at a public park. The injury occurred when the player and an opponent each tried to rebound the ball after a missed shot at the basket. During that encounter, the opponent swung his elbow to strike the player in his stomach to prevent him from getting the ball and injured him. The player now seeks compensation from the opponent.
At the trial, evidence was introduced tending to prove that the game had been rough from the beginning, that elbows and knees had frequently been used to discourage interference by opposing players, and that the player had been one of those making liberal use of such tactics.
In an action by the player against the opponent for battery, will the player likely prevail?

choices.A: No, because the opponent did not intend to injure the player.
choices.B: No, because the player consented to the rough play.
choices.C: Yes, because the opponent caused contact with the player.
choices.D: Yes, because the opponent intended to strike the player with his elbow.

questions.explanation:
Explanation
Scope of apparent consent
A and B play on opposing teams in a football game.
Same conduct A tackles B
Substantially similar conduct A tackles B offside
Conduct exceeds scope A punches B
↓
consent
↓
no consent
↓
no consentExplanation
Scope of apparent consent
A and B play on opposing teams in a football game.

Same conduct

A tackles B

Substantially similar conduct

A tackles B offside

Conduct exceeds scope

A punches B

consent            no consent

Battery occurs when a defendant intended to cause contact with the plaintiff's person, the defendant's affirmatively contact caused such contact, and that contact caused bodily harm or was offensive to the plaintiff. However, consent (actual, apparent, presumed, or emergency) is a defense to battery. And a plaintiff's participation in an athletic activity (e.g., basketball) may amount to apparent or presumed consent—especially if:

  • the defendant's conduct does not violate a safety rule of the sport
  • the conduct typically occurs during the activity and/or
  • the conduct does not involve significant risk of very serious injury or death.

Here, the opponent caused harmful contact with the player by intentionally striking him with his elbow (Choices C & D). The opponent's conduct violated a safety rule of the sport of basketball. But such rough play was typical in this game because the participants—including the player—had frequently used their elbows and knees. And elbowing a person in the stomach does not pose a risk of serious injury or death. Therefore, the player consented to the rough play, and the opponent is not liable for battery.

(Choice A) Although the opponent did not intend to injure the player, he still committed a battery because he intended to cause contact with the player. However, the player consented to such contact by participating in the game.

📌 Educational Objective

A plaintiff's participation in an athletic activity may amount to apparent or presumed consent to battery—especially if (1) the defendant's conduct does not violate a safety rule of the sport, (2) the conduct typically occurs during the activity, and/or (3) the conduct does not involve significant risk of very serious injury or death.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Third) of Torts: Intentional Torts to Persons §§ 101–104 (Am. L. Inst., Tentative Draft No. 1, 2015) (providing an overview of the tort of battery).
  • Restatement (Third) of Torts: Intentional Torts to Persons § 16 cmt. f (Am. L. Inst., Tentative Draft No. 4, 2019) (explaining the factors in considering whether participation in an athletic activity amounts to apparent or presumed consent).

questions.subject: Torts
questions.question:
While a woman was riding her horse on what she thought was a public path, the owner of a house next to the path approached her while shaking a stick and shouting, "Get off my property." Unknown to the woman, the path on which she was riding crossed the owner's private property. When the woman explained that she thought the path was a public trail, the owner cursed her, approached her horse, and struck the horse with his stick. As a result of the blow, the horse reared, causing the woman to fear that she would fall. However, the woman managed to stay on her horse, and then departed. Neither the woman nor the horse suffered bodily harm.
In an action against the owner for damages, will the woman likely prevail?

choices.A: No, because the owner was privileged to exclude trespassers from his property.
choices.B: No, because the woman suffered no physical harm.
choices.C: Yes, for battery and assault.
choices.D: Yes, for trespass to chattels.

questions.explanation:
Explanation
Battery v. Assault
Intentional act
(striking horse with stick)
Battery
Contact
harmful or offensive contact
(horse struck by stick)
Assault
Apprehension
apprehension of imminent contact
(fear of falling)

Battery occurs when:

  • the defendant intends to cause contact with the plaintiff's person
  • the defendant's affirmative conduct causes such contact and
  • that contact causes bodily harm or is offensive to the plaintiff.

Contact with the plaintiff's person encompasses contact with anything connected to the plaintiff's person. Therefore, the owner committed a battery when he intentionally struck the horse the woman was riding.

Assault occurs when:

  • the defendant intends to cause the plaintiff to anticipate an imminent, and harmful or offensive, contact with the plaintiff's person and
  • the defendant's affirmative conduct causes the plaintiff to anticipate such contact.

Here, the owner intentionally caused the woman to anticipate imminent, harmful contact (fear of falling) when he struck her horse, so the owner committed an assault. And though a plaintiff cannot recover twice for the same harm (i.e., no double recovery), the owner's act of striking the horse caused the woman two distinct harms-contact and apprehension. Therefore, she can recover for battery AND assault.

(Choice A) A landowner is privileged to use reasonable force to stop an unexcused trespass if the landowner (1) first asks the trespasser to leave and (2) reasonably believes that force is necessary to remove the trespasser. Here, the owner told the woman to get off his property, but there is no evidence that force was necessary to remove her (e.g., had he told the owner she was staying).

(Choice B) The harm requirements for battery (harmful or offensive contact) and assault (apprehension of contact) can be satisfied without proof of bodily harm. Therefore, the woman's lack of physical harm will not prevent her from recovering damages.

(Choice D) Trespass to chattels by intentional intermeddling with another's possession of tangible property requires proof of actual damages-e.g., impairment of the physical condition or value of the chattel. But here, there is no evidence that the woman's horse was impaired-e.g., unable to walk.

📌 Educational Objective

Battery requires that the defendant's affirmative conduct cause harmful or offensive contact, while assault requires the defendant's affirmative conduct cause anticipation of such contact.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Third) of Torts: Intentional Torts to Persons § 101 (Am. L. Inst., Tentative Draft No. 1, 2015) (listing the requirements for battery).
  • Restatement (Third) of Torts: Intentional Torts to Persons § 105 (Am. L. Inst., Tentative Draft No. 1, 2015) (listing the requirements for assault).
questions.zh-question:
一名女子在她认为的公共小径上骑马时，小径旁一所房屋的所有权人一边挥舞着棍子一边走近她，并大喊：“离开我的地盘。”该女子不知道的是，她所骑行的小径穿过了该所有权人的私人土地。当该女子解释说她以为那是一条公共步道时，所有权人咒骂她，走近她的马，并用棍子击打了马匹。由于这一击打，马匹受惊后腿直立，导致该女子担心自己会摔下来。然而，该女子设法稳住了身子，没有从马上摔下来，然后离开了。该女子和马匹均未遭受身体伤害。

在向该所有权人提起的损害赔偿诉讼中，该女子是否可能胜诉？

zh-choices.A: 不会，因为所有权人有权将非法侵入者驱逐出其财产范围。
zh-choices.B: 不会，因为该女子没有遭受身体伤害。
zh-choices.C: 会，因为构成了伤害罪（battery）和侵犯（assault）。
zh-choices.D: 会，因为构成了动产侵权（trespass to chattels）。

questions.zh-explanation:
正确答案解析

为何选 C？(Battery & Assault)

本题考察的是故意侵权行为（Intentional Torts）中的两个核心概念：非法侵犯（Battery）和恐吓（Assault）。

虽然女子和马都没有受到身体伤害，但法律保护的是人身完整性和免受恐惧的权利。

1. 非法侵犯 (Battery)

定义：被告意图造成有害或冒犯性的接触，并实际导致了该接触。

关键考点：人格延伸原则 (Extended Personality Rule)

你可能会问：“房主打的是马，不是人，为什么构成 Battery？”

在美国侵权法中，Battery 的对象不仅包括原告的身体，还包括与原告身体紧密相连的物体（anything intimately connected to the person）。

  • 经典案例：Fisher v. Carrousel Motor Hotel（抢夺盘子视为侵犯人身）。
  • 本案应用：女子骑在马上，马被视为她身体的延伸。击打马匹等同于对女子进行了冒犯性接触（Offensive Contact）。

2. 恐吓/侵犯 (Assault)

定义：被告意图使原告对即将发生的有害或冒犯性接触产生合理的忧虑（Apprehension）。

本案应用：

  • 房主挥舞棍子并击打马匹。
  • 马匹受惊直立（reared）。
  • 题目明确指出女子“担心自己会摔下来”（fear that she would fall）。

这种对即将发生的身体伤害（摔落）的恐惧，满足了 Assault 的构成要件。

为什么其他选项是错的？

选项 A (财产抗辩 Privilege)：
虽然土地所有者可以驱逐非法侵入者（Trespasser），但必须使用合理武力（Reasonable Force）。
在本案中，女子已经解释她是误入，且没有表现出威胁。房主直接用棍子打马属于过度武力，因此丧失了抗辩权。

选项 B (无身体伤害)：
Battery 和 Assault 不需要实际的身体伤害（Bodily Harm）。
只要有冒犯性接触（Offensive contact）或恐惧（Apprehension），原告即可获得名义损害赔偿（Nominal Damages）。

选项 D (动产侵权 Trespass to Chattels)：
动产侵权要求证明动产受到了实际损害（价值降低或物理损坏）或原告被剥夺了使用权。
题目明确说“马匹未受伤害”，因此该主张不成立。

🎓 MBE 拿分技巧

  • 看到“手中之物”被触碰：立即联想 Battery。无论是手杖、盘子、牵着的狗还是骑着的马，都属于“人格延伸”。
  • 区分侵权类型：
    Intentional Torts（如 Battery）→ 不要求实际伤害。
    Negligence（过失）→ 必须证明实际伤害。
  • 动产侵权陷阱：如果题目说“摸了一下你的车，车没坏”，这不是 Trespass to Chattels；但如果“摸了一下你手里抱着的狗”，这可能是 Battery。

reason.en: Sets up the owner's privilege-to-exclude defense in choice A.
reason.zh: 引出選項A中土地所有人驅離侵入者的特權抗辯。

keywords.text: struck the horse with his stick

reason.en: The owner's affirmative act that satisfies battery through the connected horse.
reason.zh: 所有人以積極行為經由所騎馬匹成立毆打。

reason.en: Establishes assault by imminent harmful contact with her person.
reason.zh: 表明其對即將發生之對人有害接觸的 apprehension，成立 assault。

keywords.text: Neither the woman nor the horse suffered bodily harm

reason.en: Distracts test-takers toward choice B but does not defeat battery or assault.
reason.zh: 易誘導考生選B，但不阻却 battery 或 assault。

reason.en: Shows the owner asked her to leave but did not limit force to what was necessary.
reason.zh: 顯示所有人已要求離開，但未證明使用武力為必要。

reason.en: Contact with the horse counts as contact with the woman's person for battery.
reason.zh: 擊打馬匹視為對其本人之接觸，成立 battery。

reason.en: Overstates defense by ignoring limits on reasonable and necessary force.
reason.zh: 忽略武力须合理且必要的限制，夸大抗辩。

reason.en: Misstates battery and assault as requiring proof of bodily harm.
reason.zh: 错误认为 battery 与 assault 须证明身体伤害。

reason.en: Correctly identifies distinct contact and apprehension harms from one act.
reason.zh: 正确识别同一行为造成的接觸与 apprehension 两种独立损害。

reason.en: Swaps in a tort requiring actual damage to the horse, which is absent.
reason.zh: 替换为须证明马匹实际损害的动产侵权，而本案无此要件。

highlights.text: struck the horse with his stick

reason.en: Intentional offensive contact with the horse satisfies battery against the rider.
reason.zh: 故意以冒犯方式击打所骑马匹，对骑手成立 battery。

highlights.text: causing the woman to fear that she would fall

reason.en: The rearing horse created imminent apprehension of harmful contact with her person.
reason.zh: 马匹惊立使其对即将发生之对人有害接觸产生 apprehension。

highlights.text: Neither the woman nor the horse suffered bodily harm

reason.en: Lack of injury does not bar recovery because offensive contact and apprehension suffice.
reason.zh: 无伤害不妨碍求偿，冒犯性接觸与 apprehension 已足。

highlights.text: the path on which she was riding crossed the owner's private property

reason.en: Explains why choice A's exclusion privilege is raised but does not justify striking the horse.
reason.zh: 说明为何出现驱离特权问题，但不justify击打马匹。

questions.subject: Torts
questions.question:
A tile contractor was hired to install ceiling tiles in a new, multi-story office building. To speed up the installation process, the tile contractor rented scissor lifts from an equipment rental company. A sprinkler-system contractor who was also working on the building owned several identical scissor lifts that he was using to install sprinkler systems in the ceiling of each of the building's floors. The tile contractor mistakenly directed one of his employees to the wrong floor to retrieve the scissor lift from that floor. Consequently, the employee retrieved one of the lifts owned by the sprinkler-system contractor. The tile contractor used the lift for more than two weeks before the sprinkler-system contractor found and regained possession of the lift. The lift was in the same condition as when the tile contractor had taken it.
The sprinkler-system contractor sued the tile contractor for trespass to chattels, and the tile contractor defended on the basis that his taking and use of the lift was a reasonable mistake.
For whom is the court likely to rule?

choices.A: For the sprinkler-system contractor, because a reasonable mistake is no defense to a trespass-to-chattels action.
choices.B: For the sprinkler-system contractor, because the tile contractor's mistake was not a mistake of law.
choices.C: For the tile contractor, because the condition of the lift had not been changed by his actions.
choices.D: For the tile contractor, because the sprinkler-system contractor's lift was identical to the ones rented by the tile contractor.

questions.explanation:
Trespass to chattels
Plaintiff has possession or immediate right to possession of chattel
↓
Defendant intentionally interferes with possession through either:
Dispossession
↓
Harm inferred
Use or intermeddling
↓
Causes harm
  • actual harm to chattel
  • substantial loss of use of chattel or
  • bodily harm to plaintiff

Trespass to chattels (ie, tangible personal property) occurs when the defendant intentionally interferes with the plaintiff's possessory rights by either:

• dispossessing the plaintiff of the chattel or
• using or intermeddling with the plaintiff's chattel.

Only the intent to do the interfering act is necessary. Therefore, the defendant's belief, because of a mistake of law or fact, that he/she was privileged to act is no defense to a trespass-to-chattels action (Choice B). This is true even if the mistake was reasonable.

Here, the tile contractor intentionally dispossessed the sprinkler-system contractor of his scissor lift for more than two weeks. The tile contractor's apparent belief that the lift taken was one of the lifts he had rented (mistake of fact) is no defense—no matter how reasonable that mistake may have been given that the lifts were identical (Choice D). For this reason, the court will likely rule for the sprinkler-system contractor.

Choice C) In cases of dispossession (as here seen), the plaintiff can recover for loss of use of the chattel without proof of actual harm (eg, damage to the chattel). Therefore, the tile contractor can be liable to the sprinkler-system contractor even though the tile contractor's actions had not changed the condition of the lift.

📌 Educational Objective

Trespass to chattels is an intentional interference with another's tangible personal property through dispossession, use, or intermeddling. The defendant's erroneous belief, because of a mistake of fact or law, that he/she was privileged to do the interfering act is no defense.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Second) of Torts § 244 (Am. Law Inst. 1965) (effect of mistake on trespass to chattels).
questions.zh-question:
一名瓷砖承包商受雇为一栋新建的多层办公楼安装天花板瓷砖。为了加快安装过程，该瓷砖承包商从一家设备租赁公司租用了剪式升降机。另一名同样在该大楼工作的消防喷淋系统承包商拥有几台相同的剪式升降机，他正用这些升降机在每层楼的天花板上安装消防喷淋系统。瓷砖承包商错误地指示其一名员工去错误的楼层取回那里的剪式升降机。结果，该员工取走了一台属于消防喷淋系统承包商的升降机。在消防喷淋系统承包商发现并收回该升降机之前，瓷砖承包商使用了它超过两周。升降机的状况与瓷砖承包商取走时相同。

消防喷淋系统承包商以侵犯动产（trespass to chattels）为由起诉瓷砖承包商，而瓷砖承包商则以其取用升降机是合理错误为由进行辩护。

法院可能支持哪一方？

zh-choices.A: 支持消防喷淋系统承包商，因为合理错误不能作为对侵犯动产（trespass to chattels）诉讼的抗辩理由。
zh-choices.B: 支持消防喷淋系统承包商，因为瓷砖承包商的错误并非法律上的错误。
zh-choices.C: 支持瓷砖承包商，因为其行为未改变升降机的状况。
zh-choices.D: 支持瓷砖承包商，因为消防喷淋系统承包商的升降机与瓷砖承包商租用的升降机完全相同。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Intentional Torts / Trespass to Chattels
✅ 正确答案：选项 A 支持消防喷淋系统承包商，因为合理错误不能作为对侵犯动产诉讼的抗辩理由。
核心考点：意图与错误

侵犯动产 (Trespass to Chattels) 是一种故意侵权行为。其核心要素是：

  • 被告实施了故意 (Intent) 的行为；
  • 该行为干扰了原告对动产的占有权 (Right of Possession)。

⚠️ 关键规则： 这里的“意图”仅指实施该物理行为的意图（即“我想拿走这个东西”），而不需要“想要侵犯他人权利”的意图。

因此，错误 (Mistake)——即使是善意的、合理的错误——不是抗辩理由。

案情分析
1. 意图 (Intent) 成立 瓷砖承包商指示员工去取升降机，员工主观上“想要”取走那台特定的机器。这就是法律要求的 Intent。虽然他以为那是自己租来的（事实错误 Mistake of Fact），但这不影响意图的成立。
2. 剥夺占有 (Dispossession) 承包商使用了该升降机超过两周。这构成了对原告动产占有权的严重干涉。
3. 结论 由于意图存在且发生了干涉行为，侵权成立。因为错误（Mistake）不是有效的抗辩（Defense），所以法院会支持原告。
为什么其他选项是错的？
❌ 选项 C (未改变状况)：
这是一个常见的陷阱。侵犯动产有两种形式：
  1. 剥夺占有 (Dispossession)： 只要拿走了东西（如本案，拿走了两周），原告无需证明物体损坏即可索赔（至少可索赔使用价值）。
  2. 单纯干涉 (Intermeddling)： 如果只是摸了一下或短暂移动，通常需要证明实际损害 (Actual Damages)。
本案属于剥夺占有，因此即使升降机完好无损，被告仍需负责。
❌ 选项 D (升降机完全相同/合理错误)：
这在故意侵权法中是无关紧要的。在过失侵权 (Negligence) 中，“合理性” (Reasonableness) 是核心；但在故意侵权 (Intentional Torts) 中，只要你故意实施了侵犯行为，你的理由再合理（例如：“它们长得一模一样！”）也不能免责。
遇到涉及 Trespass to Land（非法侵入土地）、Trespass to Chattels（侵犯动产）或 Conversion（转化/严重侵占）的题目时，请记住：

Mistake is NO Defense.
（错误不是抗辩理由）

哪怕被告以为那是他自己的地、他自己的车，只要他是有意识地走上去或开走的，他就承担责任。

reason.en: Explains why the mistake seemed reasonable but remains irrelevant.

reason.en: Targets the no-damage distractor in dispossession cases.
reason.zh: 针对剥夺占有情形下“无损害”的错误选项。

reason.zh: 将抗辩规则适用于这一故意侵权。

reason.zh: 以错误类型区分设陷，但两种错误均不能抗辩。

C.text: condition of the lift had not been changed

reason.zh: 错误暗示责任须以财产受损为前提。

reason.en: Frames the legal issue and its intent requirement.
reason.zh: 框定法律争点及其故意要件。

highlights.text: defended on the basis that his taking and use of the lift was a reasonable mistake

reason.en: The stated defense directly controls which answer applies.
reason.zh: 所提出的抗辩直接决定应选哪项答案。

reason.en: Supports dispossession and loss-of-use harm without physical damage.
reason.zh: 支持剥夺占有及使用损失，无需物理损害。

questions.subject: Torts
questions.question:
A college student and her roommate were invited to a Halloween party. The roommate decided to dress up as an anime character whose defining feature was bright green hair. The roommate planned to buy a wig, but the student convinced the roommate to allow the student to dye the roommate's hair using a temporary green dye that would wash out after a single shampoo. They went to a store where the roommate accidentally purchased a bottle of permanent dye. The student noticed that the dye was permanent but did not point out the roommate's mistake. Instead, the student applied the permanent, bright-green dye to the roommate's hair. Unable to dye her hair back in time for her next shift, the roommate lost her part-time job as a server.
If the roommate sues the student for battery, is the roommate likely to prevail?

choices.A: No, because the roommate consented to having her hair dyed by the student.
choices.B: No, because the student did not misrepresent the permanent nature of the dye.
choices.C: Yes, because the roommate lost her part-time job as a server.
choices.D: Yes, because the student was aware of the roommate's mistake.

questions.explanation:
Negation of actual consent
Lack of capacity
  • Plaintiff’s lack of capacity due to youth, intoxication, or intellectual incompetence may negate validity of consent
  • Plaintiff who appreciates nature, extent & potential consequences of defendant’s conduct has capacity to consent to it
  • Adult generally is rebuttably presumed to have capacity to consent
Duress
  • Actual consent given under duress (e.g., physical force, threats) is not valid
  • Threat must be of present action, not future action
  • Threats of economic duress & moral pressure generally do not render plaintiff’s consent invalid
Substantial mistake
  • Actual consent due to substantial mistake regarding nature of invasion of plaintiff’s interests, extent of expected harm, or defendant’s purpose in engaging in conduct is vitiated as defendant:
    • caused mistake by affirmative misrepresentation or fraud or
    • knew of mistake

When a defendant intends to cause contact with the plaintiff’s person, the defendant causes such contact, and that contact is harmful or offensive to the plaintiff, the defendant is liable for battery absent a defense. Actual consent is a defense to battery (and other intentional torts) when (1) the plaintiff is willing for the defendant’s contact to occur and (2) that conduct is within the scope of the plaintiff’s consent. And actual consent is valid despite the plaintiff’s substantial mistake regarding the nature of the invasion of his/her interests unless the defendant:

  • caused the mistake by affirmative misrepresentation or fraud or
  • knew about the mistake.

Here, the student applied permanent, bright-green dye to the roommate’s hair (harmful contact). Although the roommate consented to having her hair dyed by the student, the roommate believed that the dye she had purchased was temporary (substantial mistake) (Choice A). The student was aware of the roommate’s mistake but said nothing. Therefore, the roommate’s consent is no defense, and the roommate will likely prevail in her suit against the student for battery.

(Choice B) Although the student did not misrepresent the permanent nature of the dye, the student knew that the roommate mistakenly believed it was temporary. This is enough to render the roommate’s consent invalid.

(Choice C) Battery does not require proof of actual harm, so evidence that the roommate lost her job does not provide a basis for her to prevail. Instead, this evidence goes to how much she can recover in damages once her battery claim is established.

📌 Educational Objective

Actual consent to a contact is valid despite the plaintiff’s substantial mistake regarding the nature of the invasion of his/her interests unless the defendant (1) caused the mistake by affirmative misrepresentation or fraud or (2) knew about the mistake.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Third) of Torts: Intentional Torts to Persons § 13 (Am. L. Inst. Tentative Draft No. 4, 2019) (defining actual consent).
  • Restatement (Third) of Torts: Intentional Torts to Persons § 15 (Am. L. Inst. Tentative Draft No. 4, 2019) (setting forth how actual consent can be negated by substantial mistake).
questions.zh-question:
一名大学生和她的室友被邀请参加一个万圣节派对。室友决定装扮成一个动漫角色，其标志性特征是亮绿色的头发。室友本打算买一顶假发，但该学生说服室友让她用一种一次性洗发水就能洗掉的临时绿色染发剂为室友染发。她们去了一家商店，室友在那里意外地购买了一瓶永久性染发剂。该学生注意到染发剂是永久性的，但没有指出室友的错误。相反，该学生将永久性的亮绿色染发剂用在了室友的头发上。由于无法在下次轮班前将头发染回原色，室友失去了她作为服务员的兼职工作。

如果室友以伤害罪（battery）起诉该学生，室友是否可能胜诉？

zh-choices.A: 不会，因为室友同意该学生为她染发。
zh-choices.B: 不会，因为该学生没有歪曲染发剂的永久性质。
zh-choices.C: 会，因为室友失去了她作为服务员的兼职工作。
zh-choices.D: 会，因为该学生知晓室友的错误。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Intentional Torts: Battery
核心法则：无效的同意 (Vitiated Consent)

在故意侵权法中，如果原告的同意是基于对事实的重大错误 (Substantial Mistake)，且被告知晓该错误 (Aware of the Mistake)并利用了这一点，则该同意无效。

来源: Restatement (Second) of Torts § 892B

本案逻辑推演
1
侵权行为 (Battery)：
学生将永久染发剂涂在室友头上，构成了有意图的、有害或冒犯性的身体接触 (Intentional harmful/offensive contact)。
2
抗辩理由 (Defense)：
通常情况下，室友允许学生染发构成了同意 (Consent)，这是 Battery 的有效抗辩。
3
关键转折 (The Twist)：
室友同意的前提是染发剂是临时性的，但实际上是永久性的。这是一个关于侵犯性质的重大错误 (Substantial Mistake)。
✅ 正确答案 D 的法律依据

虽然学生没有撒谎（没有积极的欺诈行为），但她知晓 (Aware) 室友的错误却保持沉默。

法律规定：当被告知道原告是在错误理解事实的情况下给予同意，而被告未予以纠正时，该同意被视为无效。因此，室友的同意不能作为抗辩，学生需对 Battery 负责。

❌ 易错点辨析
  • 选项 A (Consent)： 错误。如上所述，因被告明知原告存在重大错误，该同意已失效。
  • 选项 B (No Misrepresentation)： 这是一个常见的干扰项。法律不要求被告必须有积极的欺骗行为 (Affirmative Misrepresentation)。仅仅是知情不报 (Silence with knowledge) 足以使同意无效。
  • 选项 C (Damages)： 逻辑错误。Battery 是 Actionable per se（本身即构成诉因），不需要证明实际损害（如失业）。虽然失业可以增加赔偿金额，但不是胜诉的理由。
🎓 MBE 考试技巧

在处理 Intentional Torts 题目时，一旦看到“同意” (Consent)，立即检查是否存在以下使同意无效的情况：
1. Duress (胁迫)
2. Fraud (欺诈)
3. Incapacity (无能力)
4. Mistake known to defendant (被告明知的错误)

本题考查的就是第4点。记住：Silence + Knowledge = Liability。

question_analysis.skill_tested: Apply consent defense exceptions to battery

reason.en: Defines the nature and extent of contact the roommate believed she consented to.
reason.zh: 界定室友认为自己同意的接触性质与范围。

reason.en: The actual invasion differed from what the roommate understood she was authorizing.
reason.zh: 实际侵害与室友理解的授权内容不同。

keywords.text: did not point out the roommate's mistake

reason.en: Student's awareness of the mistake can vitiate consent even without affirmative misrepresentation.
reason.zh: 被告知晓错误可在无积极虚假陈述时仍使同意无效。

reason.en: Frames the claim and triggers analysis of whether valid consent is a defense.
reason.zh: 框定诉讼请求并触发对有效同意是否构成抗辩的分析。

keywords.text: convinced the roommate to allow the student to dye

reason.en: Shows the roommate initially authorized contact, setting up the consent defense issue.
reason.zh: 表明室友最初授权接触，从而引出同意抗辩问题。

A.text: consented to having her hair dyed

reason.en: Ignores that consent is invalid when the defendant knows of a substantial mistake about the invasion.
reason.zh: 忽视被告知晓关于侵害性质的重大错误时同意无效。

B.text: did not misrepresent the permanent nature of the dye

reason.en: Confuses the need for affirmative fraud with the separate rule that knowledge of mistake suffices.
reason.zh: 混淆积极欺诈要件与知晓错误即可使同意无效的规则。

C.text: lost her part-time job as a server

reason.en: Battery liability does not depend on proof of actual harm such as job loss.
reason.zh: 殴打责任不取决于失业等实际损害的证明。

reason.en: Directly states the exception that defeats the consent defense here.
reason.zh: 直接指出在此情形下否定同意抗辩的例外。

highlights.text: temporary green dye that would wash out after a single shampoo

label.zh: 关于侵害性质的重大错误

reason.en: Shows the roommate consented only to temporary dyeing, not permanent alteration.
reason.zh: 表明室友仅同意临时染发，而非永久性改变。

highlights.text: The student noticed that the dye was permanent but did not point out the roommate's mistake.

reason.en: This fact triggers the rule that known mistake renders consent ineffective.
reason.zh: 该事实触发知晓错误则同意无效的规则。

highlights.text: If the roommate sues the student for battery

reason.en: Poses whether intentional hair dyeing is actionable battery despite initial permission.
reason.zh: 提出在最初许可下故意染发是否构成可诉的殴打。

highlights.text: accidentally purchased a bottle of permanent dye

reason.en: Creates the substantial mistake about the nature and extent of the expected contact.
reason.zh: 造成对预期接触性质与范围的重大错误。
